## The first part of this appendix, extracted from the sixth chapter of the sixth book of the *Table of the Revelation of Divine Majesty*, contained in the first chapter of Genesis: in which the Author sharply rebukes the doctrine of the Heathens and their Christian disciples.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'S' depicting a seated figure, likely a scholar or saint, surrounded by ornate foliage and scrollwork.</image-desc> The writings of the Heathens <note>original: "Ethnicorum"</note> have so gained the prize in Christian schools that the schoolmasters themselves know or understand little or nothing of the Biblical writings of the Old and New Testaments; even though God, in His first decree—in which He spoke with Moses and the Israelites—commanded both the younger and the older to instill the fear of God in all the people, so that they might call upon Him alone and observe His precepts, ordinances, and sanctions. Indeed, His servant Moses, by divine command, spoke thus to the entire Israelite people: "These are the precepts, customs, and laws which the Lord your God commanded that I should teach you, and that you should learn and do them in the region which you are going to occupy, so that you may fear the Lord your God and observe all His mandates and precepts, which I enjoin upon you and your children and grandchildren through all your life, that you may live long. Hear, O Israel, and observe, that you may do that which God gives you in His commands, so that it may be well with you and you may be greatly multiplied, just as the Lord God of your fathers spoke to you,
<margin>Deuteronomy 6</margin>
in a land flowing with milk and honey. Hear, O Israel: the Lord your God is one. Love the Lord your God with all your heart, and all your soul, and all your strength. And these words, which I command you today, shall always be kept in your heart, and you shall announce them to your children and remember them, and speak of them when you are in your house or walk on the way, when you sit down or rise up; and you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be a memorial before your eyes, and you shall write them on the posts of your door. For the Lord your God is a jealous God <note>original: "Deus zelotes"</note> in your midst, lest the anger of the Lord burn against you and consume you from the face of the earth. You shall not tempt the Lord your God."

<column-break/>

Here you see (my fellow Christians) the way in which God opened a school for His children, namely by commanding that the fear and precepts of the Lord be set before and instilled even in infants, right from their very cradles. Indeed, he commanded that they should carry the divine precepts with them in their hearts, remember them, and speak of them, whether they sit at home under their own roofs, or travel abroad through foreign places—whether they are carried, or ride, or sleep, or walk, or rise. Nor should they only remember them, but also put them into action and arrange their lives according to them with all their strength. And, lest they should ever forget them, but always carry them with them in present memory, they are commanded to bind the divine precepts as a sign upon their hands and to write them on the walls of their houses and the posts of their doors for a perpetual memorial. But if they will not be obedient to those divine precepts, and moreover continue to tempt God as if the matter were not serious, or as if no punishment were to be inflicted on transgressors, God threatens them in that case with the most cruel and heavy punishments: that He will wipe them off the face of the earth.

Although these things were most rightly ordained by God, you nevertheless allege many vain and futile reasons to the contrary, asserting that the young can neither perceive nor understand such arduous matters concerning God and divine precepts, much less put them into practice. You argue that, for this reason, easier and less difficult things should be presented to them: namely, the *Fables* of Aesop, the *Distichs* of Cato, the *Bucolics* of Virgil <note>The "Bucolics" or "Eclogues" are Virgil's famous poems about pastoral life, standard reading in 17th-century schools.</note>, and other writings of the Heathens which have been daily and common in Christian schools until now, on the grounds that they are better suited for youth. Furthermore, you say they should read for the sake of their minds the *Comedies* of Terence and Plautus, and that the books of "Saint" Aristotle <note>The author uses "Sancti Aristotelis" sarcastically here to mock the near-religious reverence Christians held for the Greek philosopher.</note> should be handed to them, in which he treats natural and supernatural things and the essence of God, describing at the same time the order of the world and the heavens. From these books, forsooth, the young are supposed to draw [knowledge] of God and the divine [creatures]...

...the knowledge of [natural] things and the entire world. Then, truly, after these foundations have been laid, they believe that the same youth must be advanced to the writings of the Rhetors and the Heathens <note>original: "Ethnicorum," referring to non-Christian classical authors like Aristotle and Cicero</note>, and exercised in the recitation of public orations. This is done so that they may be rendered all the more bold, and so they might be able to propose those things which they have learned about natural and supernatural matters—and even about the essence of God and divine creatures and the world—to others in turn, with constancy and a great spirit. Once this is finally done, you think that your children, imbued and instructed in that manner, are the best and most learned orators and preachers—so much so, indeed, that no one is able to conquer or surpass them in disputing and debating.

<margin>Matthew 22. Mark 12.</margin>
Regarding these things, however, you ought to know that you err by the width of the whole sky <note>original: "errete toto coelo," a Latin idiom meaning to be completely mistaken</note>, since you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God. Are you so wise and perceptive, and yet you do not understand what God requires of you? For you do not notice that those follies from the writings of the Heathens are hammered into boys with much greater and more difficult labor than if they were educated in the fear of God and the divine precepts. Indeed, if an infant of four or five years learns to read the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note> and retains it in memory, he has done his duty sufficiently. Afterward, short interpretations are to be handed down to them, so that they may practice them with one another through questions and answers. And although they may not sufficiently understand all these things during infancy, they nevertheless perceive this utility from it: that they are able to retain them with a firm memory until they grow up, attain mature judgment, and inquire into their true sense and understanding. Nay, furthermore, by this method they become accustomed from an early age to speak of God and to hear others debating about Him. Later, higher things in the divine law, in the Prophets, and the Psalms can easily be proposed and hammered in, and at the same time, interpretations of the same can be handed down. Thus, through accurate and daily exercise, they may perceive, understand, and retain all those things better and more correctly in memory, since they are distracted and hindered by no Heathen follies concerning them. And these things are indeed performed piously: upon such an education, God bestows the Holy Spirit and divine blessing, art, science, and understanding. But you dismiss all these things and bring forward your Heathen Doctors; you must apply much labor and trouble regarding them before you can hammer that Heathen doctrine into your children and disciples. At the same time, your disciples consume a great deal of time—even ten, twenty, and sometimes thirty years—before they drink in and learn those subtle tricks for circumventing others. Yet, when all these things have been so clearly perceived that nothing further remains that they have not mastered, they are not much more learned than that "German Michael" <note>A personification of the common, simple, or unrefined German man</note>, and they know neither God nor His creatures—

<column-break/>

—nor do they know anything else about them, except that the grass is green, that a cow is marked with various colors, that a horse is dappled, that water is wet, and that God is such as they themselves dream Him to be from the traditions of the Heathens, and that the world is eternal <note>The Aristotelian view that the world had no beginning, which contradicted the Biblical account of Creation</note>.

These and similar things they know how to paint and adorn with their "caparisoned" <note>fancy or decorative</note> sophistries to such an extent that they are able to provoke even a sleepy dog from the ashes with them. Meanwhile, they do not know the properties and virtues of even the smallest grain of *Magancricens* <note>Likely a corruption or specific term referring to the mustard seed (Sinapis), used biblically as the smallest of seeds</note>, or at least not even in the smallest part. And yet they nonetheless wish to be held as learned, and to dispute about God and His works, in which they are truly blinder than a mole fleeing the light. Oh, miserable and blinded ones! Do you not fear to dispute about God and His works, which you do not know? For no one knows God, except the Spirit of God alone. Since, therefore, like true Heathens you do not have the Spirit of the Lord, and for that reason you also do not know God, how will you debate or write about God and His creatures with any foundation of solid truth? For here one must attend to that saying: "Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you." But you have deserted God and His doctrine, and in its place you have proposed and hammered Heathen doctrine into your children and disciples; and for that reason, God has left you in your errors, so that through that doctrine of yours you do not have the Holy Spirit. Instead, through the reading of Heathen writings, you invite an unclean spirit into your schools in place of the Holy Spirit, who also faithfully assists you and promotes your works, so that he may draw and reduce both you and your disciples into his power and under the crown—or rather the yoke—of his empire. For although in your schools you chant that little song, *Come, Holy Spirit* <note>original: "Veni Sancte Spiritus"</note>, and afterward you spend the entire day reading Heathen writings to your disciples with the greatest zeal, hoping the Holy Spirit will come to you—nevertheless, it is not He, but in His place your idol, the Devil, who comes to you. He helps you in your schools, since you are his instruments as long as you handle those Heathen books. But you reply that other schools are also held among you at the same time, in which the Holy Scripture is read, so that, of course, no defect might be detected in either. You say that some schools must be held in which Philosophical matters are treated—specifically those which the Heathens described best of all, for you claim they cannot be drawn from the Holy Scriptures. But afterward, you say, once someone has fully learned Philosophical precepts from the writings of the Heathens, he easily emerges as a most excellent Doctor of the Sacred Page.

### ->APPENDIX TO THE FIRST SECTION<-

O raving fools! What spirit of impurity has suggested this philosophy to you—or as you call it, wisdom—that it must be sought among the Devil, his sons, and the Heathen <note>original: "Ethnicorum," referring to non-Christian classical authors like Aristotle or Cicero</note> deserters of God? This is despite God Himself testifying that He alone is the true fountain and source of wisdom.
<margin>Baruch 3</margin>
Have you not understood well enough that God has opened only one school, in which He commanded that He alone be feared, His mandates observed, and He alone be served? How do these things agree: that you strive to have a school of Sacred Scripture, and at the same time build a Heathen school for the Devil himself? For you cannot serve both God and the Devil. Furthermore, that school of yours which you call "Theology" does not have a form pleasing to God. For you admit no Teacher into it unless he has first perceived and absorbed the basic elements—and indeed the complete foundations—of Heathen writers. For you assert that only such a person is fit to teach Holy Scripture; thus the Devil sits at the helm <note>original: "ad clavum," literally at the tiller of a ship</note> in both of these schools of yours, openly circumventing men in public and enticing them to himself. Therefore, you most wretched disciples, consider these things more deeply. Shake off this devilish yoke, desert your impious schools, and turn to your God—the most fit Headmaster <note>original: "ludimoderatorem," a schoolmaster</note>—who offers and promises you knowledge, arts, and wisdom; indeed, even the Holy Spirit and eternal life. For you see that in those Heathen schools, the fear of the Lord and the Divine precepts are neither bound to the hand, nor inscribed on the walls, posts, or gates, as God otherwise commanded to be done for a perpetual memory of them. Much less does anyone, at home or in the country, while sleeping, walking, or rising, remember them or speak of them. Instead, the contrary is before your eyes: namely, that all houses, walls, dining rooms, windows, doors, posts, books, cups, plates, small discs, knives, swords, spears, and rings are filled with the maxims and sayings of Heathen sages in place of God and the fear of His divine commands—lest the masters of such things should ever forget their Teacher and his doctrine. This is truly to tempt God and their Lord shamelessly. For while these men erect Heathen schools instead of opening schools to God, they blaspheme Him by suggesting that He does not take this business seriously or that it is not in His heart. And consequently, they think they will be subject to no punishment for this transgression of the divine mandate. They tempt God in this very way:

<column-break/>

when they invoke Him for the granting of the Holy Spirit, yet meanwhile they pursue devilish doctrine. Therefore, the Lord has sworn that He will blot out these blasphemers and tempters from the face of the earth.

That aforementioned school, which God Himself instituted, was meant to be the Mother and origin of His Israelite Church, from which so many Priests, Levites, Singers, and Deacons came forth. They read, taught, and learned Divine doctrine together with the Prophets and the civil leaders in the Church of God, from the time of Moses until the coming of Christ. This was done so that through all these things, by the power of God, they might fully know all His creatures and acquire such wisdom that they surely foresaw the future: that the Messiah, the true Son of God, would be born of a Virgin in Bethlehem of Judah. And later, when Christ was born and went up to the temple in His own time, He found there Doctors and disciples reading and teaching Moses and the Prophets, without any depravity, corruption, or mixture of Heathen doctrine. But because they would not believe that the true Messiah had already been revealed, and that the Law and the Prophets had reached their goal and end in the presence of Christ, He transformed that Jewish Church into a Christian Church. He instituted Baptism in place of circumcision and introduced new schools and Doctors. And they also preached unanimously against the doctrine of the Heathens and their idolatry, and directed the people to Christ alone: that He is truly God with the Father and the Holy Spirit, equal in Majesty, glory, and power; that He assumed true humanity for the sake of our sins, was crucified for our sins, and in this way redeemed us from eternal death; and that He rose from the dead on the third day, ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of God, from whence He shall come to judge the living and the dead. This doctrine was in full vigor during the time of the twelve Apostles and for a long time after their departure. All Heathen doctrine was rejected <note>original: "explosâ," literally "hissed off the stage"</note> and many of their books were burned, until finally those perverse Heathens—who even before the birth of Christ were held in high esteem and authority outside the Church of God—insinuated themselves again among Christians through their books. They mixed themselves in and sowed their poison, and by their sophistries <note>original: "Sophisticationibus," meaning deceptive or overly complex philosophical arguments</note> they turned many Christians away from the once-acknowledged and received Christian faith. Furthermore, they filled all the schools of the Christians with their books, as is observed daily before the eyes of everyone in these our times. For Satan [has given] such [power] to those Heathen Sophists...

### ->ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.<-

...through the tricks of sophistry, he <note>Referring to the Devil, mentioned on the previous page</note> has brought it about that he has not only seduced many Christians from the true faith, but furthermore has so blinded those who remained with the great evil of madness that they carry those Heathen <note>original: "Ethnicos," referring to non-Christian classical authors like Aristotle, Plato, or Cicero</note> books in their schools and allow them to take root. They are so delighted by them that they cannot be persuaded by any reason to remove them or cast them out of the schools, so that they might instead open and establish true schools of God. Therefore, so that this abominable error and horrific abomination might finally be uprooted from the Christian Church and the schools be purged of them, the magistrate should take serious notice of this and compel schoolmasters <note>original: "ludimagiſtros"</note> to abolish such Heathen books and consume them with fire.

<margin>Acts 19.</margin>
Once this is done, the word of God will grow vigorously and remain firm, just as happened in the time of Paul in Ephesus, where a great many books were burned <note>The author refers to Acts 19:19, where new converts burned their books of magic</note>. For indeed, if anyone wishes to turn away and remove an evil, it is necessary to remove the cause of that evil.

If you do not want an infant to be injured by a knife, the little knife must be taken away and removed. Since, therefore, so much damage is inflicted upon the Christian Church through Heathen books, all Princes ought rightfully to apply themselves diligently so that, at the first opportunity, they take the doctrine of the Heathens and their books out of their schools, remove them, and burn them with fire. They should strictly forbid and interdict the printing and distribution of them under threat of the heaviest punishment. Furthermore, they should also undertake consultation and deliberation with learned, skilled, and prudent men as to how schools can be established and opened everywhere according to the prescription of the Divine mandate, in which only the fear of God and divine precepts are taught and read aloud, together with the Prophets, Psalms, Gospels, and the political laws <note>original: "politicis ſanctionibus"</note> of Moses.

Serious attention must also be paid at the same time, with the greatest zeal and accurate diligence, lest that poison and Heathen sophistry creep back in secretly within private walls through certain people, and in this way overturn the whole business in turn. In this way, the devil can be resisted, so that he might be less able to stir up such a great and pitiable evil in the Christian Church. For all his works are empty, and he dreams of nothing else but sheer vanity, by which he leads men away from God. I would wish you, who are disciples, to be warned of this. Furthermore, it is also a wonder to hear that the Jews, Turks, and Heathens hate our books so much that they not only do not read them, but even consider it a crime and a sin if anyone should even pick up a single leaf of them with their hand. To such a degree, surely, do they love and protect their own religion and doctrine...

<column-break/>

...lest anything Christian be mixed into it. They also rejoice greatly when they hear or see that their abominable books are held in such high price and honor among us, so much so that they are not only publicly presented in our schools and debated from, but even sermons are held from the pulpit for the people using them, and their opinions and sayings are cited for the confirmation of our doctrine and religion.

From this, again, this greatest evil emerges: that while we attempt to convert the Heathens through our Christian doctrine, we nevertheless meanwhile use the writings of the Heathens, neglecting the school of God. They conclude that our doctrine is entirely false, and that theirs, on the other hand, is true and blameless. Therefore, they prefer to persist in their Heathen confession rather than be converted to the true Christian faith, especially since we ourselves, who are Christians, are caught <note>original: "altipelemur," likely an error for 'aucupemur' or similar, meaning trapped or influenced</note> by their opinions and thus are made Heathens ourselves. We do not consider that God will not let these "Heathen-Christians" go unpunished. But if anyone wishes to convert the Heathens from their idolatry and false, fictitious doctrine to the true Christian Church, it must be pursued in a far different way and manner. For not only must all their books be cast out from the schools and the entire Christian Church and burned, but it will also be necessary to refute, disprove, and shatter their false dogmas with the solid foundations of Christian truth, and conversely, to profess and preach the true doctrine of love and divine precepts together with the Holy Gospel with constant and pious zeal.

For by this means, at last, they will learn and understand who God our Creator, Redeemer, Protector, and Savior is, and that their false doctrine and idolatry is totally displeasing to Him and is condemned. Then, most especially, they will learn that all those who are not Baptized, and do not believe Jesus Christ to be the Son of God, have no life in themselves but are to be condemned with the Devil. On the other hand, those who believe in Christ will rise again with Him and will occupy the kingdom of heaven by hereditary right, possessing it for all eternity in the highest happiness and joy before the face of God. Indeed, this is what all Christians most highly desire—that it might also happen for the Heathens, and that they might obtain and possess the kingdom of God together with them, if only they are truly converted to the Christian faith. For the Gospel is also lawfully announced to the Heathens, and the gate of heaven is open to all those who turn to Christ and His kingdom and seek it from the heart. From this, you now see, you patrons and schoolmasters <note>original: "ludimagiſtri"</note> of Heathen-Christian schools, how much...

# APPENDIX TO THE FIRST SECTION

...you bring so much damage and evil into the Christian Church, while you train your students in Heathen doctrine <note>The author uses "Heathen" (Latin: *Ethnica*) to refer specifically to the classical Greek and Roman authors like Aristotle, Cicero, and Virgil, whose works dominated the curriculum of the time.</note> from their very cradles, as it were; and you thrust that poison into their mouths like pre-chewed food, by which they are led away from true and sound doctrine. Furthermore, by this profession of yours regarding Heathen writers, you provide an occasion for the Heathens themselves to be less inclined to embrace the Christian faith, so that they instead persist in their blindness with continued obstinacy. God will seek and avenge the blood of those who are seduced and hindered from eternal salvation—their destruction—from your hands. Or do you not also think it will come to pass that, at the Last Judgment, your students (whom you led away from God) and the Heathens (whom you prevented from reaching the knowledge of the truth) will most severely accuse you and complain of you? The students will complain that you seduced them from the true path of the Christian religion into the pathless wastes of the Heathens; the Heathens will complain that by your public lecturing and profession of Heathen writers in your schools, you confirmed them in their heresies and errors and rendered them so much more obstinate. Thus, they did not hear the solid principles and foundations of Christian truth from you; much less were they warned to abandon false doctrine and idolatry to embrace the true Christian religion and seek Christ the Savior within it. Yet you do not yet believe these things will be so; but to your great misfortune, you will eventually find them to be all too true. Or perhaps it will seem a 

<column-break/>

light thing to you to desert the fear of God and divine precepts to follow the false doctrine of the Heathens? Are you ignorant that the deities and idols of the Heathens are true devils, from whom they borrowed their false doctrine, arts, prophecies, and deceits? What were Apollo, Diana, and Jupiter? What were the Sibyls? What were the "mountain women" <note>likely a reference to Oreads or mountain nymphs</note>, the Pygmies, the forest gods, the virgins or water nymphs? Did they not consult all of these in their necessities and difficulties? Meanwhile, they abandoned the true and only God, who nevertheless offers you all grace and mercy of His own accord, because He wishes to open and reveal to you the past, present, and future—indeed, the wonderful and great mysteries together with His treasures. And yet, madness still drives you to prefer following the devil and his lying oracles, to seek counsel from them, and to promote and handle their false and fabricated doctrine, rather than to cling to the true and living God alone and be saved. Do you not know that He is a strong and jealous God, who does not wish to give His honor to another, but requires that we fear Him alone and observe His precepts and sanctions only? He requires that we turn away from all Heathen and idolatrous things, and by no means have or adore any other God besides Him. Thus you see all your actions and works are mere vanity, in which you will also utterly perish, unless you send a dismissal to Heathen doctrine <note>original: "nuntium miseritis," a legal idiom for "divorcing" or "breaking off" a relationship</note> and turn with your whole heart to God and His doctrine.

Indeed, this world has become so blinded that no one believes such grace can be granted to a human by God that they might see a spirit. Yet, these very people wish to be considered Christians and Children of God, even though they possess no faith that is effective and living. They believe with the mouth only, and in no way with the heart; thus they think it sufficient for themselves if they confess their faith only with their mouths and lips, while meanwhile their heart is as far from it as can be, and is separated from it by no less a space and interval than the East is divided from the West. Faith ought to take root in the heart and breast, and from there grow upward and bring forth fruits worthy of a Christian man. Therefore, these people boast of their faith in vain, since not even the smallest fruit of faith can be found in them. Who among them, by the greatness and constancy of his faith, has restored health to his neighbor? Or who has recovered from illness through it? Who has beheld any divine vision by the power of his faith? Or who has obtained anything memorable or noteworthy through its truth and constancy? Let even one come forward from many thousands of thousands and show at least the smallest effect of his faith.

I would make a wager that you are all going to say that you could not heal the official’s son <note>Likely referring to the "nobleman's son" in John 4:46-54 or the possessed boy in Mark 9.</note>; and at the same time you will ask what the cause might be that you were unwilling to perform it. But the Lord will answer you, that this impossibility lies in your unbelief. If you cannot certainly work some effect, you do not have true faith. If you do not have true faith, you are not Christians. But if you are not Christians, why do you boast of the Christian faith? Surely this path of boasting and vainglory should be blocked, and you should be excommunicated until a promise is made that you will admit and teach a better and fuller instruction of faith in the Christian Schools.

As long as this does not happen, you are to be regarded as unbelieving Heathens <note>original: "Ethnici"</note>, and must be cast out from Christian society. For you treat Christ with Garlic-breath—that is, with ignominy—while you profess His name and faith but are caught in your lies. For this reason, Christ’s name is torn apart with blasphemy and insults among the Gentiles, because your faith is empty and dead, and performs or achieves nothing at all in the name of Jesus. You Magistrates, what care do you take of your Schools? How is your youth instructed in the faith? Where are your Christian books? In what manner do your Doctors present Moses, the Prophets, and the Gospels, along with the Epistles? When, finally, will the fruits and

But indeed, you have something else entirely to answer, asserting forsooth that there is no need for miracles at this time, because those signs were necessary only in the Primitive Church so that the infidels might be converted to the Christian faith; but that in this age of ours, it is no longer desired, but is sufficient that faith be proposed to men through sermons without miracles. But I, my friends, would like you to answer me on one point: What did Christ do? What did His Apostles do while they journeyed in this world? And likewise, that they also healed the sick in both body and soul, cast out demons, and thus left an example for posterity to follow in teaching the people and healing the bodies and souls of the sick?

### The third part of this appendix from chapter 105, book 5, of the Table of the Revelation of Divine Majesty, in which the creation of the Thunderbolt Stone is discussed against the Peripatetics. <note>The "Peripatetics" were the followers of Aristotle, whose physical theories dominated the universities of the time.</note>

The greatest part of men cannot be led to believe that anything falls or is cast down from the air to the earth. And if ever frogs, cows, or calves and other miraculous things fall, they think these were all first suddenly lifted into the air by the force of the wind and thus afterward fall back to the earth. When they hear that a thunderbolt <note>original: "jaculum tonitrui," literally a "dart of thunder."</note>, polished like some transparent crystal, or even a <term>Thunderstone</term><note>original: "Ceraunium lapidem." Also known as ceraunites, these were often prehistoric stone tools or fossils found after storms and believed to be the physical manifestations of lightning bolts.</note> of white, blue, green, and various other colors is sent down from heaven, by which houses, towers, fortresses, and indeed even sometimes stony crags are shattered, broken to pieces, and set on fire, they respond that those stones are born from fine dust raised upward by the heat of the Sun and drawn into the moist clouds, and are broken into partly oblong and partly round shapes, and thus hardened, are cast down and dislodged with force when a more vehement heat exerts its strength into the moist clouds. This, forsooth, is that so-often-chanted <term>Aristotelian Philosophy</term>, so that it is a sorrow that they speak so futiley, ineptly, and ridiculously regarding the miracles of God, while they turn their backs on true science, and use and delight in these lying dreams in place of the truth; and they even

<column-break/>

do not blush to boast and glory in them. But it is difficult to turn them away from their follies, since they ought to know that these stones are prepared by the Angels of God and sent from above. Those animals are also born in the water in higher places, as was briefly indicated before; the air also and the heaven are made from water, and sometimes things born and grown in that water are cast down. It follows, therefore, that gems and metals are made from water in the air or heaven, and are sometimes cast down into these lower regions; and thus those golden flints and other stones born in the water above are cast down from above in many places to us men on earth, by which divine miracles are revealed and God is celebrated among the human race. Although these and other arguments for exploding the doctrine of the Heathens are very frequently disputed and proposed in many places, and are confirmed and announced upon the solid foundations of truth in the assembly of Christians, no effect truly and really follows from it. Indeed, even in this age of ours, one may see how the books of the Heathens [are used] not only in all Universities and <term>Grammar Schools</term><note>original: "Trivialibus scholis," schools teaching the Trivium: grammar, logic, and rhetoric.</note>, but in the cities...

### The fourth part is Chapter 78, Book 7, of the table of the Revelation of Divine Majesty: which explains the mysteries of the air and the truth of Meteors against the minds of the Peripatetics <note>The Peripatetics were followers of Aristotle; the author is challenging the standard Aristotelian science taught in universities.</note>.

---

All things were created through the Word of God: therefore, all things are also governed, moved, and led by the Word of God. The "wise ones" of this world do not want to admit this, but instead they fashion for themselves a peculiar opinion in which they maintain that "Nature" performs all things, and that Nature operates through "secondary causes" into "tertiary" ones <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "secondary causes" are the physical laws or intermediate agents through which a "First Cause" (God) acts. The author rejects this as a way of distancing God from the world.</note>, and that "a fool generates a fool." Yet these fictions and opinions of theirs are nothing other than pure, manifest lies. For that "Nature" does not exist in the entire Universe of things as something that might work or produce anything on its own, as God does, who created all things by His Word. Whatever blessing He has bestowed and attributed to each creature, that creature obeys it, and it complies with that Word and Divine command, not departing from it by so much as a fingernail's breadth. All creatures whatsoever persist within the boundaries and limits of divine obedience—except for man, who withdraws from God, despises His precepts and doctrine, fashions gods and idols for himself, and establishes religions and decrees peculiar to himself in sacred buildings. He depraves the Word of God and compels others to prefer their own ordinances and traditions over the Word of God: to invoke saints, to venerate the relics of saints as sacred, to pray for the dead, to administer the holy supper instituted by Christ under only one kind <note>original: "sub una tantùm specie." This refers to the Catholic practice of providing the bread but not the wine to the laity during the Eucharist.</note>, and whatever other

<column-break/>

delusions of this kind exist, which are observed to the disgrace and belittlement of the Divine Word. Nevertheless, that Word will remain firm and will eventually judge those who despise it. In the same way, the "Wise of the world" or Philosophers also rave, for they do not grant that God works all in all, and that His Word moves, stirs, and preserves everything. Instead, they ascribe it to their "Nature," pretending that God works through means, and indeed through secondary and tertiary causes. Thus these raving "wise men" are either unwilling to understand that God works uniquely through His Word and not through any other means—and certainly not through those "causes" alleged by them—but rather He works *within* those things. God created the first body—namely water—as something wet or moist through His Word, and this very thing remains moist even today after the lapse of so many thousands of years. No other "cause" is seen there that makes the water wet or renders it moist. Above and in the water, God established the air, so that it might float upon the waters and impel and move them, and preserve them in that liquid and molten substance. This likewise happens even today. Along with the air, He also created by His Word the Angels and spirits, who are in the air regarding the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunder, fire, and Chasmata <note>original: "Chasmatum." Atmospheric phenomena that appear as openings or "chasms" in the sky, often associated with auroras or unusual light effects.</note>...

### APPENDIX TO THE FIRST SECTION

...of thunder, lightning, water, heat, cold, humidity, dryness, and many other things of that kind, perform and execute their task and office. And this very thing even today occurs through His Word. Concerning all these things, those secular wise men or Philosophers write incredibly foolish books for themselves, in which not even a single point, let alone a whole letter, is true. Instead, whatever has flowed from their brains into the pen and from there further onto the paper—this is all that can be read in them, and it is nothing other than pure, unadulterated lies. 

Nay, even the very spirit of the mouth in those "wise men" is entirely lying and false. Nevertheless, they wish to be called wise, and they try to persuade others to present their books above all to students in their schools, and to exercise them well in those books, so that they might emerge more learned from them; for they claim that the entire foundation of all other arts consists in those works. 

Note, however, how pointlessly they write about those things already mentioned: namely, from where clouds, rain, snow, hail, frost, heat, cold, lightning, the thunderstone <note>original: "lapis Ceraunius." In the early modern period, prehistoric stone tools found in the earth were often believed to be physical "bolts" that fell during lightning strikes.</note>, floods of water, and good and bad weather arise. Truly, no more foolish dreams could occur to anyone than those with which these donkeys <note>The author frequently uses "asini" (donkeys/asses) to insult scholars who rely on reason rather than scripture.</note> describe the matters mentioned. 

This happens solely because they know neither God nor His most holy Word, and thus they even despise the Holy Scripture. They do not read it, but instead dwell only on their own delusions, sewing lie upon lie. But if they had read through the Holy Scripture with the same zeal with which they unrolled their lying books and volumes, they would have found the truth about the air and the weather: namely, that those things do not behave in the way they wrote in their lying books. 

Rather, God has His own special storehouses <note>original: "arcas Thesaurarias." A reference to Biblical passages like Job 38:22, which describes God keeping snow and hail in "treasuries."</note> for these types of things already mentioned, from which He brings forth winds and storms, and He makes His angels and spirits into winds and flaming fires. If all these things were taken from the Holy Bible and gathered into one bundle—as perhaps at some time a partial sketch of all of them will be made in a special book—how you lying busybodies <note>original: "ardeliones." A term for meddlers or those who make a great show of doing nothing useful.</note> would flee with those figments and delusions of yours! 

Since God has His own special storehouses to bring about the variety of weather, along with Angels and Spirits, and from there brings in all those things we see: how wonderfully the storms arise, how miraculously the thunderstone hardens, by what means heat and cold generate thunder—so that it reaches even to towers, houses, and trees—how will you ever, under the pretext of truth, prove or defend these and your other delusions, O most impudent liars, against the express Holy Scripture? You will clearly never be able to

<column-break/>

*After the Author of this treatise, with diligent inquiry leading the way, had understood that all Sympathy and Antipathy had arisen immediately from certain differing passions of the soul or life-giving Spirit; one of which is concupiscible <note>desiring or attracting</note>; the other indeed is Irascible <note>angry or repelling</note>, and yet had perceived that these were present by effect in creatures—as much in animals and vegetables as in minerals—he was inflamed with no small desire to find and distinguish the radical cause of the same thing. But when he had considered with himself again and again, that the eternal power (which is the head and root of all) is a simple and absolute nature in itself, he could discern no such diversity in its essence, insofar as it exists eternally in itself as nothing but a single and same Identity:*

And this negative or contractive action of its own is the perfect Character of its non-willing, the general effects of which are Darkness and privation: But, when on the other hand, that hidden unity sends forth a benign and salutary ray and splendor of its essence (which is the expression of its will) into the Chaos or deformed abyss, then the darkness and privation are forced to give place to light and position, as if to the act of life and formal existence. # THE ARGUMENT OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK I.

...rather than positive, both in the virtues of heaven and in the inhabitants of the earth. Therefore, it follows that darkness and light are one and the same in that Archetypal unity <note>Archetypal refers to the original divine blueprint or the mind of God before creation</note>: Since everything within that unity is good, insofar as the unity is in itself the sole and absolute goodness. As far as it pertains to the effective and informing emanation of light, these properties indeed appear to creatures as such, and seem to produce various—indeed, even infinite—contrarieties in this world. These are judged by mortals to be either good or evil according to the effects they experience from them. However, it seems evident to the Author that these two contrary outflows or extensions, proceeding in effect from one and the same essential eternity, were the principles of all things, insofar as the dark Chaos <note>original: Chaos obscurum</note> brought forth waters from its bowels by the presence of light. These waters were that single matter from which the heavens and the earth, and consequently the entire world, were made: For the life-giving emanation of eternal light imparted form, figure, virtue, and motion to them.

Therefore, after the Author seriously considered these things, his reason immediately informed him that the world was composed and fabricated from matter, or a subject, that was contrary in its disposition. For it is not possible that parents who differ from each other by nature should bear offspring who are concordant and in agreement with them in condition and nature; and yet such was the Creator’s will <note>original: Creatoris voluntas</note>, that these two properties, like dissonant tones, should be bound together into a union of unison or unity—as if in His own image—by the inviolable bond of the eternal Spirit of love and concord. Thus, thereafter, matter, which is the substance of the dark waters, might serve in the place of a female to the formal and masculine emanation, or the illuminating Spirit sent forth from unity. By this means, at last, a Typical Tri-unity <note>original: Triumun Typicum; a symbolic representation of the Trinity reflected in the physical world</note> might be established from duality (or the confusion of unities) in the image of the Archetype. This Archetype, existing as purely Spiritual, was that radical eternal life and essence of the world which was without beginning. 

And for this reason, it is necessary that the world, created as it is in the image of the Archetype, should enjoy a Universal Soul <note>original: anima Catholica</note>, by means of which it can act and live according to the pattern of Him from whom both its form and matter are derived. Consequently, it is necessary that it be clothed in the two aforementioned properties, namely that of "Willing" and "Unwilling" <note>original: Voluntatis & Noluntatis; Fludd uses these terms to describe the positive/creative and negative/passive aspects of the divine power</note>. From this, the author notices that both the internal and external Type, or the Typical world, must necessarily be subject to contrary passions and alterations that arise from those two properties in the Archetypal unity. 

Namely, sometimes its soul is suited to a dark and privative disposition, following in that property the nature of the waters, which are the offspring of the Dark Abyss <note>original: Tenebrosae Abyssi</note> or the formless chaos, over which divine power has dominion. In this state, it seems to put on the character of "Unwillingness" within unity. At other times, the soul affects and imitates the action and property of light which emanates from the eternal fountain of unity. In this state, it clearly seems to act, inform, and as it were "will," or put on a positive and lucid nature, and consequently be signed with the seal or impression of "Willing" within unity. 

And this is that effective result of the sacred will: For it seemed to the Author that, since the whole world was forged from two contrary properties—namely, from formal light and dark humid matter—it must consequently follow that the Universal Soul in the world, or the Spirit thereof which generally gives life (and consequently every particular formal existence which is derived from the Universal Soul no differently than infinite rays from a single sun) is subject to passions and alterations of an opposite condition. From this, therefore, arises that constant friendship and enmity observed between good Angels and evil Spirits. From this come those daily changes and variations, as much lovely as hateful, which occur by reason of the variety of influences—either harmonious or discordant with each other—even in heaven...

From this, those contrary effects proceed, which are breathed out into the Universal <note>original: "Catholicum" – used here in its literal sense of 'universal' or 'all-encompassing'</note> Sublunary <note>The "sublunary" region refers to the Earth and its atmosphere, which, according to ancient science, was the only place subject to change and decay</note> Element by winds that are opposite in both location and condition, or by those that are natural and agreeable. Whence both harmony and discord, along with a multiform diversity of meteors <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, clouds, and lightning</note>, are produced within it. From this comes the multiplicity of affections, the opposition of dispositions, the passions of the Spirits, and, to put it in a word, that sympathy and antipathy observed to exist between creatures, whether simple or composite, be they animal, vegetable, or mineral. Therefore, the Author, spurred by these foundations, concludes that it is right and just to agree with the opinions of those two most excellent philosophers, Heraclitus and Empedocles, regarding this matter. One of their opinions is that all things come to be through strife and enmity—that is, from Enmity and Friendship. The other is that the soul is composed of the four elements and of friendship and strife. From this he argues for that contrary disposition between the watery Spirit (the moist nature of the world) and the clear ray of the shining mind, with respect to their origin. For by "strife" he understands both spiritual and bodily contention, namely regarding that contrary power or strength that exists between the formal, all-informing light and the Dark matter—both by reason of the body in the act of corruption, when the soul is ready to depart from it, and in the "antipathetic" or irascible passion of the soul, in which the Spirit labors and suffers unnaturally. And these opinions of the aforementioned philosophers do not seem to differ from the sense of the wise man, who says that God made all things in pairs, one of which is the opposite of the other, and nothing was made that is imperfect.

->CHAPTER I.<-

->In this chapter it is demonstrated that God is that pure, simplest, and Universal Unity which comprehends all number and multiplicity within Himself.<-

Just as there is no one—no matter how exalted in the sphere of mathematical perfection or how deeply immersed in the mystic depths of abstruse arithmetic—who can observe or discern anything by the agile intuition of their more mature intellect that could rightly claim a place before Unity in either order or antiquity (whence Unity is recognized by the wisest of philosophers to be the principle and root of all numbers and multiplicity), so indeed no one consistent with himself can deny that this radical identity—when considered in its pure and simple nature—cannot be limited by any quantitative dimension, nor included or comprehended in any number, nor divided into distinct portions, nor defined by any substance or entity. And from this, the wise conclude that Unity is the most ancient and most radical principle of all things, inasmuch as it comprehends within itself all substances, quantities, and qualities. This is no different than how a point in Geometry, considered in its naked and simple essence, is observed to be indivisible—indeed, something barely perceptible and almost indeterminable. And yet, the point is recognized by mathematicians

<column-break/>

to be the infallible root, not only of any geometric line, but also of all other continuous dimensions in Mathematics <note>original: "Mathesis" – a term often encompassing the whole of the mathematical sciences</note> and Physics, insofar as the point itself comprehends all magnitudes within itself and is comprehended by none.

Thus, experienced mathematicians have found two principles of any dimensions whatsoever which preceded and excelled all other things in the nature of reality in terms of order and time. These were found as a symbolic representation <note>original: "Typicam" – a type or shadow of a greater reality</note> or image of the innermost, most central, and most hidden point within the divinity—or of that most splendid Unity remaining in the same state in which it existed before the creation of the world. Namely, when it kept itself hidden and secret within itself—that is, reserved from every act of creation. So that, in this condition of the existence of unity, it could not yet be held to be "God," insofar as it had not yet produced any creature through creation by which it might be worshipped as God. Nor could it be rightly held to be the "Father," since it did not yet appear to have begotten any son—whether Archetypal <note>The divine original</note> or Typical <note>The physical image</note>. Nor did it seem to be estimated as the Highest Good, insofar as the abyss was still covered in darkness, or the *hyle* <note>original: "hyle" – a Greek term for the primordial, unformed matter or "stuff" of the universe</note> was still deformed and did not yet participate in His shining and life-giving goodness. For, as yet...

# BOOK I, SECOND SECTION.

...was still empty and void; nor should it have been called beautiful or shapely, because it had not yet shared the rays of its beauty with any creature. Nor should it strictly have been called "eternity," since in that hidden state, it appeared to human capacity not to exist at all; indeed, it was esteemed as nothing, and consequently had no commerce with eternity, the age of spirits, or time. Furthermore, it could not claim the name of "Principle" <note>In this context, "Principle" (principium) refers to the starting point or origin of something else</note> in such a condition, since it had as yet no relation to creating any thing. It was so hidden and obscured from mortal apprehension, so unknown in its own order and antiquity, and so inscrutable and incomprehensible in its essence, that it could in no way be categorized as a substance, quantity, or quality. Instead, it was a certain Transcendent Being, reserved and consisting in itself alone, having no beginning or root from which it might be drawn. Nevertheless, within its divine power—as if in a place containing all things without end or limit—everything that now appears explicitly was then contained implicitly, even though, in respect to the meager capacity of mortals, they were esteemed as Nothing. For this reason, some who were well-versed in the laws of true wisdom left in their eternal monuments the teaching that this Mystical Unity, when it was wrapped in the mists of the Dark Abyss and remained, as it were, empty and idle, was regarded as א Nothing. Not-being, not-end.

<margin>Reuchlin, Book 3 of *On the Kabbalistic Art*.</margin>
Since the thinness and poverty of the human intellect’s capacity in the consideration of divine things is such that it usually imagines and judges those things which do not appear to the eyes to not exist at all: for this reason, the more excellent ranks of Kabbalists <note>The "Cabalistic crowds" or schools refers to Christian and Jewish scholars of the Kabbalah, a mystical interpretation of the Bible</note> called this radical unity in its abstruse and hidden condition the **Dark Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph Tenebrosum". Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>. This Hebrew letter is received among the Jewish Doctors or Rabbis as the figure of unity in arithmetic, and is consequently understood hieroglyphically to represent God in His absolute Monadic nature, insofar as He is seen to be contracted in Himself alone without any sign of emanation. In this state, Mercurius

<margin>*Pymander*, 12. *Pymander*, 3.</margin>
Trismegistus <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many ancient mystical and scientific texts were attributed</note> describes Him in these words: "The Monad (he says) before the beginning of the world shone for itself and not for others." And elsewhere more clearly: "There was an infinite shadow in the Abyss, and water above, and a subtle intellectual spirit was within the Chaos by divine power."

<margin>Genesis 1.</margin>
And Moses says: "Darkness was upon the face of the Deep." By these words, the wise are able to discern from afar what the divine power was before any creature appeared explicitly from the dark Chaos. They can also easily conceive what the radical principle of darkness was—namely, the retention or hiding of the actual rays of eternal light within that luminous unity in which there is no darkness at all. Thus, Original Darkness

<column-break/>

can be considered as nothing other than the mere absence of the luminous emanation from the radical unity, which is the fountain and origin of all action. That divine light of life-giving cannot be present or emanate where the will of that simple and absolute unity is negative (a state of absence). From this, it follows of necessity that "darkness was upon the face of the deep," and that "the earth was empty and void" or formless, before the divine essence shone forth and "was moved upon the waters." Thus, darkness was made into a Tabernacle of leisure and rest; for where the divine act or sacred emanation is absent—or at least where it does not wish to act and emit its rays—all things are said to remain in potentiality, and consequently exist without actual virtue, that is, as if dead and motionless. While this state of privative power <note>The power of withholding or "saying no"</note> holds dominion, the properties of cold and numbness are in force, because heat is generated by motion, and motion is something inseparable from light. This light has its root in the luminous unity, which for this reason is called the "Father of Lights." Wherefore it follows that the divine essence in this state contracts and retains itself within itself; and then the dark Chaos reserved in the divine power must be deprived of motion and heat. It is inclined toward density and thickening by reason of the dominion of cold. It is the foundation of privation and, consequently, is an enemy to life and the essence of creatures, insofar as its nature is opposed to act, motion, and heat (which are the ministers of divine emanation), and is therefore the origin of death, corruption, and deformity.

We conclude, therefore, that just as light is the beginning of life, position, motion, and the divine will in its revealed nature, so primordial darkness is the head and fountain-head of death, emptiness, privation, rest, and finally the **non-will** <note>original: "noluntas" – a technical term for the negation of the will</note> of the divine essence. Hence the Holy Scriptures testify that when it pleases God to emit the health-giving rays of His countenance upon creatures, they are recreated with good and life; but when He hides His luminous face in part, they grow sick and are troubled; and if He should totally withdraw the aspect of life, they immediately expire and die.

<margin>Psalm 104:20. Deuteronomy 31:17. Psalm 13:1.</margin>
Hence Moses also says: "God leaves the wicked and hides His face from them, so that many evils befall them." And David elsewhere: "How long will you hide your face from me? Cheer me with your countenance; your visitation preserves my spirit." By these things it is clear that this divine essence observes the action of its non-will and its will both after the creation of the world and before it: in the former, it is accustomed to withhold life from the creature by means of an act of privation; in the latter, it imparts life to it and preserves it. For by its rarefying property, it created and vivified the world and all things that are in the world.

## CHAPTER II.

->*In which it is proven that all things were implicitly and ideally in God and from God, before anything appeared explicitly or was made.*<-

<margin>

The state and mode of existence of the eternal unity, before anything was created—according to the small strength of my intellect—as well as the effects which it produced in the potential or unformed subject of all things, I have sufficiently and clearly explained in the preceding sections. I also expressed there that all things in that state were folded within and hidden <note>The author uses the terms "complicitly" (folded in) and "explicitly" (unfolded) to describe the process of creation from potential to reality.</note> in the omnipotent and incomprehensible point of divine perfection. In that condition, they remained and existed as if they were Nothing, as far as we are concerned; for no form (which serves to assign a name and being to things) had yet been put on. Therefore, regarding this state of unformed power in relation to our existence, the wise have called it the Divine Power. But, so that we may confirm this whole matter more clearly by sacred Authority: the Apostle says: *From him, through him, and in him are all things.* <note>original: "Ex ipso, per ipsum & in ipso sunt omnia."</note> And elsewhere: *All things are from God.* And elsewhere: *One Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in us all.* And again: *All things were created through him and in him, and he is before all things and all things hold together in him.* And elsewhere: *He is all in all.* And Sirach says: *We have said many things, yet we have not reached the end: the sum of our words is, He is the all.* <note>original: "summa dictorum est, ipsum esse omnia." Referring to the Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:27.</note> The poets seem to agree with these sacred words when they say: *Jupiter is whatever you see, wherever you move.* <note>The author quotes the poet Lucan here, using "Jupiter" as a poetic placeholder for the omnipresent Divine Being.</note> And: *All things are full of Jupiter [God], etc.* From these, it is very easily gathered that God generated, produced, made, and created nothing that was not eternally from himself and in himself, so that all things emanated and proceeded from him—namely, from the hidden into the manifest, from the unknown into the known, from pure and Archetypal Simplicity into a Typal likeness, from the fountain into the sea, and from the point into the circle. This verifies the saying of the wise philosopher:
<margin>To Asclepius.</margin>
*God is the center of all things, whose circumference is nowhere;* or, as others would have it, *he is the center and the circumference.* Hence, let me be permitted to infer that every begotten, originated, created, produced, and separate thing comes from the unbegotten, infinite, unoriginated, unproduced, unseparated One: every lower thing from the higher, every bodily thing from the spiritual, every visible thing from the invisible, every temporal thing from the age, and every age-bound thing from the eternal. Hence, just as it is said of God that *from him, through him, and in him are all things,* so it is also said that *he is over all and through all and in all.* There follows, therefore, a consideration of the universe by its emergence and descent—or, as it were, by its progress from the center toward the circumference. In God all things were, being nothing but purely God; then all things

<column-break/>

came from God into the **Principle** <term>Principle (Principium): The initial starting point or source of being.</term>, and then all things were nothing but purely the Principle, yet God remained in himself. From the Principle, all things proceeded into the **Word** <note>original: "Verbum"</note>, and then all things were nothing but purely the Word, yet the Principle remained. From the Word, all things proceeded into the **Spirit of the Lord**, and then they were nothing but purely the Spirit of the Lord, yet the Word remained. From the Spirit of the Lord, all things proceeded into the **waters**, namely the higher waters, and then all things were nothing but purely the waters, yet the Spirit of the Lord remained. From the higher waters, all things descended into the **lower waters**, and then all things were nothing but purely the lower waters, while the higher remained. From the lower waters—as if from a **universal element** <term>Catholic Element: Here the word "Catholic" is used in its original Greek sense of "katholikos," meaning universal or general, rather than referring to the Church.</term> altered into four forms—and from invisible stars, all things proceed into **visible bodies**, and then all things are nothing but purely visible bodies, while the elements and invisible stars remain. Finally, when all these things have been unfolded and completed, the whole universe is contracted into a **fifth being**, that is, into **Man**, where all things are nothing else but purely Man, yet the Universe remains safe and whole. Thus Man exists as the last of all, who has and bears all things within himself, and is all things, because he is essentially the image of him who was before all—who is the blessed God, who was all things, who poured out all things, and who encloses all things within Man. This whole process we can confirm by holy testimony and the assertions of the Kabbalists:
<margin>
Isaiah 45:7.
Wisdom 11:18.
John 1.
Genesis 1.
</margin>
For we have it in the scriptures that God, the fountain of all, created the darkness, and that this dark abyss was the unformed principle which implicitly contained all things in itself; and that the Word was in the beginning, and again, that this Word emerged from the darkness. And that the Spirit of the Lord was carried over the waters, which appeared from the depths of the dark abyss. And that all things in the beginning were waters, yet the luminous power of the spirit was not extinguished. And that these waters were divided into higher and lower, but the first power of creation was evident in those higher ones, since the **Empyrean heaven** <term>Empyrean: The highest, most celestial part of the heavens, associated with pure light and fire.</term> was created before the sublunary element. Then, from the higher waters along with the lucid spirit with which the heavens were adorned, the lower waters were formed and ordered: for the lower things are ruled by the higher. Finally, all things composed of the lower waters were created by means of invisible stars sent out from the higher waters; and at last, as the perfection of all, Adam was made in the image of God as a compendium of the whole world, containing it within himself. Hermes says this: **Pimander** <note>original: "Pimander." This refers to Poimandres, the "Shepherd of Men," a visionary figure representing the Divine Mind in the Hermetic writings.</note>, the mind of divine power, changed its form and suddenly revealed the universe: for I saw all...

While the previous page established God as the "Dark Aleph" or the hidden potential of all things, this page describes the actual unfolding of creation—from the first light and the "Word" down to the physical world and humanity—and then reverses the logic to show how everything can be traced back to that single divine source.</meta>

### BOOK I, OF THE SECOND SECTION.

...all things were turned into a light, exceedingly great and pleasant, which delighted me wonderfully as I gazed upon it. A little later, a certain dreadful shadow crept underneath with a slanting revolution, migrating into a moist nature, which was then agitated with an ineffable expression, from which a great smoke broke forth into a sound. And from that sound a voice emerged, which I thought to be the voice of the light; from the voice of the light, the **Word** <note>original: "Verbum"</note> came forth as a finished work. Standing by this moist nature, it nourished it. Then, from the inner parts of that moist nature, a pure and light fire immediately flew out, seeking the heights; the light air, obeying the spirit, took its place in the middle region between the fire and the water. The earth and water, however, lay so mixed together that the face of the earth, overwhelmed by water, was nowhere visible. Afterward, the earth brought forth the living creatures it had held within. But the Father of all, being **Intellect** <note>original: "intellectus," referring to the Divine Mind</note>, life, and splendor, procreated a man similar to himself, etc. 

By these things he argues that God, or the divine mind, in his simple unity, was divine power; and thus in God, all things were nothing but truly God. Then he changed himself into the **Dark Principle**, and then all things were nothing else than the Dark Principle, since all things were contained within it folded together <note>The author uses the concept of "complication" (folding in) and "explication" (unfolding) to describe how the universe exists within God before being expressed in physical form.</note>, yet God remained. Then a luminous emanation was made, by which—the darkness having been put to flight from the principle—the **Word** was made; and then all things were nothing but the Word, yet the principle remained. From the Word, all things proceeded into the **Spirit of the Lord**, and then they were nothing but the pure Spirit of the Lord, and so on for the rest.

Furthermore, it is also written in the book <term>Bahir</term> <note>The *Sefer Ha-Bahir* is one of the earliest and most important books of the Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism.</note>: "Nothing" is the principle, except for Wisdom. When this Wisdom is withdrawn into the abyss of darkness and remains as if idle, or (as they say) looking toward nothing, it is therefore called <term>Ain</term> <note>Hebrew: "Ayin," meaning Nothing or the Boundless.</note>. Nothing. Non-being and non-end; because we, punished with such a thin poverty of intellect regarding divine matters, judge those things which do not appear in the same way as those things which do not exist. But, when it shows itself, that it is something and truly subsists, then the dark <term>Aleph</term> <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet (א), often used to represent the beginning or the unity of God.</note> is converted into the luminous *Aleph*: or the great *Aleph*, when it desires to go out and appear as the cause of all things, does so through <term>Beth</term> <note>The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet (ב).</note>, the letter following immediately after, and is named <term>אב</term> **Ab** <note>Hebrew for "Father."</note>. That is, the Father of all generation and production; for he makes all things. 

From this, it is clear that this digression is supported by the consensus of both the Holy Scriptures and the wisest Philosophers and Kabbalists. But if we wish to move in a backward manner, ascending from the circumference of things to their central point—as if from the earth to the highest heaven—we think we must begin with man. For he was the last and lowest step of the superior ladder, through which we descended from heaven to earth by a demonstration *from the cause* <note>original: "à priori"</note>, and as if from **Alpha to Omega**. And so, by a demonstration *from the effect* <note>original: "à posteriori"</note>, we shall proceed as if from **Omega to Alpha** in this manner: **Eve**, the Mother of all living, was not made from an absolute nothing, but essentially from **Adam**,

<column-break/>

who says: *this is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.* And before Eve was drawn out from Adam, there was then nothing in Adam but Adam himself, who was the **microcosm** <note>literally "little world"; the idea that a human being reflects the entire universe in miniature.</note> and the folding-together of the whole universe. Adam the microcosm was not made from nothing—that is, not from himself, nor through himself—but from the **Macrocosm** <note>the "great world" or the universe at large.</note>. And before he was drawn out and came into his own being, he himself was nothing else in the macrocosm than the macrocosm itself, or the great world. 

The macrocosm was not made from a mere and absolute Nothing, but from the **higher waters**, that is, it stood forth from the **Angelic world**. And before this happened, the great world in the higher waters was nothing else than the higher waters themselves, or the Angelic world itself. The Angelic world, or the higher waters, did not emerge from nothing, but from the **Spirit of the Lord**, who poured them out from himself and moved over them. And before this pouring-out happened, all the higher waters or Angelic substances in the Spirit of the Lord were nothing else than the Spirit of the Lord himself, without any distinction or multitude. 

The Spirit of the Lord did not come from nothing, but from the very **Word** brought forth from the mouth of the first-born. And before the Spirit of the Lord was distinguished or proceeded from the Word into its own being or person, it was then in the Son and with the Son as nothing else but the Son, without any distinction or multitude. The **Word** or the **Son** did not come from Nothing—that is, not from itself—but from the **Principle** <note>referring to the "Beginning" mentioned in the Gospel of John.</note>, according to that saying: *The Word was in the Beginning.* And before this Word was born from the Principle into its own person, then the Word itself in the Principle was nothing else but the Principle, essentially one in and with the Principle, without distinction or multitude. 

But the **Principle**, in which the Word was, did not arise from nothing, nor from itself, but from **God**. For it came forth from the mouth of the Most High. And before it came forth, the Principle in God was nothing else than God himself—essentially, eternally, and most simply one and the same, without distinction. Thus God, the unity of all, had all things in himself from eternity; and just as he is one in himself, so also was he all things—yet in such a way that he himself remained in himself without change or diminution of himself. And thus he produced all things from the beginning and distinguished each thing in its own being. He had nothing to do with any "Negative Nothing" (which we mentioned above), since he is one in himself, or that eternal unity, comprehending all things within himself. Consequently, he is the fountain and origin from which all things—both eternal and temporal—proceed and consist in their essence. In no other way do all the numbers of Arithmetic proceed or emanate from unity and are comprehended in unity. For, however widely a number extends itself, it always has **unity** to begin it, and likewise to conclude it; and in the truth of the matter, it has nothing besides unity...

### Fol. 70.

...has toward the forming of its interior parts. But for your better instruction, through a diligent inspection of **Cossic numbers** <note>original: "numeros Cossicos." From the Italian 'cosa' (thing), this was an early term for algebra. Here, the author uses algebraic progression to explain spiritual emanation.</note>, you may observe how this Divine, central, and essential unity comprehends all creatures within itself, both before and after their creation. For we ought to know that there is nothing in this world that is not either a **root**, a **square**, a **cube**, or some other composite figure. The **root** represents the principle of all Cossic proportions or magnitudes; the **square** designates a simple and spiritually-originated figure, which is created or produced from the multiplication of the root; while the **cube** is forged from the expansion of the square (the originated figure) into its own root. From this, one may see that the entire cubic body—and consequently the square itself—is contained within the root. In conclusion, it is nothing other than the root itself, multiplied in and by itself. 

But, so that this demonstration of mine might come closer to the view of your understanding, I urge you to consider the nature and property of that divine **Monad** <note>The "Monad" refers to the ultimate, indivisible Unity or God.</note> or unity with a bit more diligent care. Specifically, as it exists in its simple and sincere being, you will understand that it contains within itself, in a "folded" <note>original: "complicitè," a term used in Hermetic philosophy to mean "enfolded" or "potentially present."</note> way, those three aforementioned Cossic dimensions (and consequently all other things it has now produced "unfolded" <note>original: "explicitè"</note> through creation) within the typical world, without any departure from its punctual or central depth. And this is clearly proven by this Arithmetical demonstration: for if we unfold unity in itself and by itself as a root, it will produce nothing but itself for a square; which again, by multiplying only itself, it brings forth in place of a cube—namely, mere unity. Thus, you will find the root, the square, and the cube to be nothing but one and the same. From this, it is evident that although we have here three branches of a single point, which seem to differ in their formal progression (I mean the root, the square, and the cube), yet in essential truth, there is nothing but that real and radical unity or identity, in which all things remain potentially or "enfolded," and that in a most hidden manner. And for this reason, the wise man says: To God all things are—

->You guide all things from above<-

For this reason, that most learned **Abbot Odo**

In the Treatise on numbers: The Ternary.
