<meta>This page continues Fludd’s discussion of how the divine Trinity (the number 3) acts as the mediating force in the universe. Having established the mathematical foundations of the intellectual, celestial, and elemental worlds, he now visualizes these relationships through the geometry of light and matter, introducing his famous "Pyramid of Light" and "Pyramid of Matter" to explain the origin of the World Soul and the Sun.</meta>

# BOOK I, OF THE SECOND SECTION.

...darkness, or the dark Chaos, or the abyss, is so named because the darkness had not yet shone forth to give form to the waters. Between these two extremes, a **3** is placed <note>original: "interponuntur 3"</note>, like a peaceful unity full of charity, which is a lovely middle ground for joining the two extremes—namely, light and darkness—into a perpetual friendship. This is the divine spirit of love and concord which, residing in the middle between those two principles (both in position and condition), unites and joins the divine **formal fire** <note>The active, shaping force of spirit.</note> with the moist **material nature** or spirit of darkness. Thus, those two natures, which were once opposites, remain in a sympathetic agreement; and therefore, that formal triad is called the "bond of the Elements," connecting strife and friendship with the chains of concord.

This excellent harmony of the world-soul has been explained by me in the most fitting way possible by means of two Pyramidal figures, one of which is **formal** and the other **material**. The base of the **Formal Pyramid** is adjacent to the fountain of divine light, and this Pyramid denotes the lucid emanation of the spirit that informs and enlivens all things, flowing from the bright fountain into the existence or formless matter of the world, such that its cone <note>apex or point</note> penetrates all the way to the center of the dark earth or abyss. On the opposite side, the base of the **Material** or watery Pyramid is in the place of the earth's diameter, which passes from east to west through the center of the earth, as if in a place most opposite and remote from the formal base. Its cone, however, ascends all the way to the center of the base of the Formal Pyramid, just as you see depicted here.

### Figure of the Pyramid.

<image-desc>A cosmological diagram consisting of two overlapping, inverted triangles (pyramids). The top pyramid's base is at the top, labeled "Formal Fountain." Its apex points downward. The bottom pyramid's base is at the bottom, labeled "Earth, the Material Fountain." Its apex points upward. At the central intersection where the two pyramids overlap equally, there is a circular emblem featuring a radiant sun with a face, labeled "Sphere of Equality."</image-desc>

<column-break/>

Now, where the intersection is made in the middle between both Pyramids, I have drawn the arc of a circle: because the portions of both the formal and material Pyramids are equal at that point of intersection. Therefore, following the opinion of the **Platonists**, I call the Sphere or orb passing through that intersection the **Sphere of Equality**, and in another respect, the **Sphere of the Soul**. It has its position directly in the middle of the stellar heaven, which for this reason is called **ether** or **fiery air**; as if one were to say, an equal portion of the spirit of the waters and of the formal fire descending from God, the Father of Lights. 

And therefore, just as I placed the **3** in the center or middle of the line in the previous demonstration—namely, between the unity of divine light (**1**) and the dark Chaos or the shapeless and confused dyad (**2**) <note>The number two, representing duality and division.</note>—so in the world was the spiritual body of the visible Sun of this typical world placed. In this Sun, the invisible and uncreated Sun of the **Archetypal world** <note>The divine realm of pure ideas.</note> placed its Tabernacle; and for this reason, it is rightly called the **Sphere of the Soul** by the Platonists. Indeed, we find by its effect that all life-giving power proceeds powerfully from the Solar influence. Furthermore, both in respect to the eminent beauty of that creature and its life-giving act, it is clearly evident that it abounds with the blessed sparks of divine light. Again, daily experience teaches even the rustic and the farmer that the Sun is the most brilliant organ through which He who gives life to all things pours out and distills the effects of His kindness—the divine nectar of life—into the lower realms every day. 

Now, I shall prove and demonstrate that this most perfect and excellent concord of life remains and has its seat in the middle of the line (acting like a stretched String or Chord) from the unity, or center of the formal base, to the duality, or center of the material base—as if it were the String of the **Symphonic World-Monochord** <note>A single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate mathematical musical intervals; here used as a metaphor for the universe.</note>—through musical consonances. The most perfect consonance in Music is the **Diapason** <note>The octave.</note>, because it approaches more closely than all others to the nature of sacred unity. For it is half of the unison, and consequently is most aptly compared to the emanation of the most holy life which arises from unity. Therefore, it is not wrongly called the **Idea** or image of unity. And just as unity, though it is but a single essence in the divinity, comprises three persons representing the three consonances of the **Archetypal Harmony**, so also the Diapason comprises within itself two other musical concords: namely, the **diapente** <note>The musical interval of a fifth.</note> and the **Diatessaron** <note>The musical interval of a fourth.</note>. 

Now, we prove in this way that this most perfect consonance consists and is placed in the middle of the unison, and by its central position in the unison, it creates the two Diapason concords. # ON MOYSAICAN PHILOSOPHY.
V 3
<meta>catchword: CHAPTER V.</meta>

one of its strings will vibrate and give the sound of the **Universal Unison**. For, just as the string is one, so the sound will be absolutely one in itself and will act as the father of all harmonies, of which the firstborn and most worthy will be the **Octave** <note>original: "Diapason"</note>, which is procreated from the belly or center of the Unison in this way: Press the string that forms the Unison exactly in the middle, and then both half-portions of the string will relate to each other in a double proportion, namely as 2 to 1. And thus the Octave, the most perfect harmony, will be produced. This is a sufficient argument to demonstrate that the perfection of the Octave resides in the **Solar seat**, and consequently, that the formal and living concord of the entire world—as if of a **monochord** <note>A single-stringed instrument used by ancient and Renaissance scientists to demonstrate the mathematical laws of music and the universe.</note> (whose spirit I relate to the string of the monochord) extended from the seat of God all the way to the earth—is in that middle and central place, just like the heart, which is the seat of human life. And yet, through the rays of the Sun, this life or soul of the world is made **Universal** <note>original: "Catholica," here meaning all-pervading or universal rather than referring to the Church.</note> and fills all things: not otherwise than the vital blood expands universally through the fabric of the **microcosm** <note>The "little world," i.e., the human body, which mirrors the "macrocosm" of the universe.</note> by means of the veins and arteries. But I fear now that I have pursued this point—namely, the proof of the world soul—at too much length; therefore I leave it, so that I may approach more closely the subject at hand, especially since in the fourth book of the first section (where I maintained that Saint Jerome’s translation was true, namely: **GOD HAS PLACED HIS TABERNACLE IN THE SUN**), I treated the Solar mystery more fully; now indeed I shall proceed to the second opinion of the Philosophers. The ancient Philosophers, **Democritus**, **Orpheus**, along with the **Pythagoreans**, asserted that all things are full of Gods: yet they refer all these Gods back to a single, supreme **Jupiter**. By "Gods," they mean the divine virtues infused into all things, which **Zoroaster** called "divine Allurements" <note>original: "Illices"</note>, and Bishop **Synesius** called "Symbolic attractions"; others call them souls, others "powers" <note>original: "fortes"</note>, upon which the virtues of things depend. In this they seem not to err much, except that they distinguish the divine essence into a diversity of Gods; nevertheless, they appear to excuse themselves and purge themselves of this error by referring all those Gods to a single Jupiter: by which relation they seem to acknowledge the continuity and indivisibility of the soul with the divinity. They agree, therefore, with the Scriptures in that they confess the divine essence is present in every created thing.

<column-break/>

The **Platonists** and all those Philosophers who share their opinion agree in every matter with Orpheus and Democritus, except in this: that they call this divine spirit the **Soul of the World**; the others said it was Jupiter, and where the latter constantly call the virtues possessing creatures "Gods," the former name them specific souls which have a continuous relation with the World Soul. In no different way and in the same sense, the Scriptures say that the incorruptible **Spirit of God** is in every thing.

<margin>Wisdom 12:1</margin>
I conclude, therefore, that since the World Soul has for its internal part a splendid emanation of eternal unity, and for its external part a subtle, universal spirit of the waters or a moist nature (which serves as a moist vehicle or material organ in which and through which it works spiritually everywhere and in every thing), we must recognize that there is a certain kind of contrariety even in the universal Soul of the world itself, without which there would be no action or passion in a created soul. For insofar as it is created from the **luminous soul** or uncreated active nature, it tends toward the **Deification** and exaltation of the created Spirit, if it adheres to it; and from the created **passive spirit**, which is the offspring of the obscure and dark abyss or **Chaos**, it is therefore easily inclined toward moving the nature of darkness. It is no wonder if, by reason of the various conditions of that spirit, there are present in it sometimes good passions and sometimes evil passions, which operate in an opposite or contrary manner not only in the heavens and the earth of the **macrocosm** and its creatures (whether celestial or elementary, whether animals, vegetables, or minerals), but also in the lesser world, which is **man**. This shall be declared in the first chapter of the following book of this section. But first, I think it worthwhile to unravel and lay bare the true mystery of the specific soul of the microcosm: and then afterward to show how all other souls of creatures—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—proceed and are derived from this Universal Soul of the greater world, and are preserved and multiplied by it in their state of life. For this uncertainty has not yet been fully and clearly discussed by the most excellent Philosophers up to this day: and consequently, this discourse of mine should not be made light of or inspected lightly and negligently even by the most learned men of this age.

### CHAPTER V.

#### *How all particular souls are said not only to proceed from that Universal Soul of the world, but also to have their preservation and multiplication in it and from it; and I shall begin first with the soul of the most noble creature, namely man.*

<margin>Pimander, Book 1</margin>
Hermes, called Mercurius Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure perceived as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, a series of sacred texts on philosophy and magic.</note>, spoke with sufficient wisdom when he said that the world was made according to the likeness or pattern <note>original: "typum"</note> of God. Therefore, just as one is called the **Archetype** <note>The original model or divine idea in the mind of God.</note>, so the other is called the pattern. For this reason, he asserts elsewhere: "I know that the world exists from God and in God; but man
<margin>Pimander, Book 8</margin>
exists from the world and in the world; but the beginning and the container of all things is God." And
<margin>Pimander, Book 9</margin>
again: "God is the Father of the Cosmos or the world, but the Cosmos is the father of those things within the Cosmos; and the Cosmos is indeed the Son of God, and is rightly called Cosmos <note>In Greek, *Kosmos* implies both "universe" and "orderly beauty" or "adornment."</note>, because it adorns all things with the variety of generation, as well as with the perpetual operation of an infinite life, the speed of necessity, the joining of the Elements, and the order of things born. The Cosmos preserves forever whatever it has received from God from its very origin," etc. In these words, he does not seem to differ from the meaning of the Divine Page <note>A common term for the Holy Scriptures.</note>. For there we find that in the beginning God created the world from formless matter, and that he adorned the moist nature of the world, or the heavens, by means of his life-giving spirit; and that by the breathing of that same Spirit of life into the world, the world and all its creatures were animated; and that those creatures receive their material existence from the substantial Elements of the world. Thus, just as God, through the pouring out of his life-giving spirit—which works all things in the world—caused the moist and passive nature of that world to operate; and that mundane spirit thus became animated (since its divine power is poured into the whole and into every part of it along with its internal "naturing" nature <note>original: "natura naturante," a Scholastic term referring to God or the creative principle of nature as an active force.</note>); it is not wrongly called the **Universal Soul** <note>original: "anima universalis"</note>. Thus, without further doubt, every particular soul in the vast cavity of the mundane machine proceeds from, or is procreated, depends upon, or is preserved and multiplied by and in this Universal Soul. For it is the role of this soul, according to Scripture, to breathe into and
<margin>Acts 17</margin>
give life to all things, and as it is held elsewhere, to give "life, breath, and all things." Therefore, not only the **Microcosm** <note>Man, the "little world."</note> but also the **Macrocosm** <note>The universe, the "great world."</note> live, move, and exist in Him. Nor is it strange if I assert to you **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, often criticized by Fludd for their focus on material logic over spiritual mystery.</note> that all individual souls consist in that Universal Soul of the world, no differently than all solar rays are in the Sun; since it is your own firmly established axiom that "the whole contains its parts." From which it follows that every particular part draws its existence from the fountain of the whole. But the universal material Spirit of the world is

<column-break/>

actuated and informed by the universal eternal Spirit, creating and giving life to all things, which in its essence is indivisible. Therefore, just as from the immense fountain of life, the influences of life—exhaled under the form of infinite rays from one invisible Sun—are actually sent out to infinite creatures so that they may live and be "informed" <note>given their essential form or soul</note> by them; so indeed these rays of life are no less continuous and indivisible from the fountain of life (or the spiritual and invisible Sun) than solar rays can be discerned or separated from the visible Sun. Nor was it sufficient for Adam to put on a microcosmic body—namely, a mass of clay or earth for his material or elemental portion—unless that divine spirit, sent from God into the world, had breathed a portion of its divinity (namely, the breath of life) into it, by means of which he moved, lived, and existed in the human state. And therefore Hermes said, not without consideration, that the world was the image of God, and man the image of the world. For just as God gave life to the watery spirit of the world by his breath of life, so that spirit of life (which is a single essence, indivisible from the Father), having been sent into the world and filling its universal spirit, gives life to, preserves, and multiplies not only man, but every other animal, vegetable, and mineral creature. For, as Solomon testifies, "The
<margin>Wisdom 12:1</margin>

<margin>Prometheus.</margin>
The Philosopher called the human soul a natural fire; and Prometheus called it a celestial fire enriching men with life. And since it is handed down that this Prometheus held possession of that fire, he is therefore imagined by the Poets to have been severely punished by Jove for his surreptitious theft of that fire from heaven. But Hermes calls it the fire of the word adhering to a moist nature. And <margin>Hermes. Zoroaster. Heraclitus.</margin> Zoroaster and Heraclitus say that it was an invisible fire, by means of which all generation and multiplication is accustomed to happen. Since, therefore, that fire of life is never to die in an animal creature, it is necessary that for its conservation and multiplication it be nourished every moment of time by its like in the air: which, if it were not to happen, the life of the creature would necessarily vanish, and thus the creature would perish. And this is that which <margin>Parmenides.</margin> Parmenides seems to suggest when he says: *Nature rejoices in its own nature*. For this reason, the fiery virtue of life, having its position in the center of the creature’s heart, attracts its like from the air by means of inhalation through a certain magnetic property, with great joy, delight, and appetite. For (as I have said) the hidden food or nourishment of life is in the air. This, then, is the reason why a certain anonymous author, most excellently versed in the mysteries of God and nature, says this: > O nature of celestial truth, multiplying natures! O strong nature! Nature conquering and overcoming, and making its own natures to rejoice! By which he argues that by the aid and visitation of this celestial nature, the vital spirits and the flames enclosed within them grow and multiply. For by the virtue of this, not only life, but also the fruits of generation proceed and are produced in an infinite manner. We infer from these things which have now been said, that the elementary air is full of the influences of life, vegetation, multiplication, and formal seeds: insofar as it is itself the treasury chest of God, rich and exuberant with divine rays and celestial gifts. Nor does this assertion of mine regard only the animal kingdom of composition, but also that of vegetables: for they flourish by this very spirit, and by this they multiply infinitely and have their existence. For I am myself an eyewitness, and can also demonstrate if need be, that the spirit of vegetable wheat, in which a secret spirit dwells, is a pure volatile salt <note>A term in early chemistry for a salt that easily evaporates, often associated with the vital essence of a substance.</note>, which is nothing other than air made specific to wheat. This volatile salt is an unctuous liquor, as white and clear as crystal, the interior of which is nevertheless filled with a vegetable fire, by means of which it is multiplied infinitely. For that formal fire is a certain magnetic power, through which like life and vegetation is extracted abundantly for itself from the rays of the Sun—which is the treasury chest of God for life and vegetation—by means of the aerial vehicle. I perceived, therefore, that this vegetable spirit, set free from its elementary bonds

<column-break/>

and reduced into the form of a most limpid liquor, was so greedy for the formal rays of the sun and sought them with such sympathy, that when it was exposed to the solar rays for the space of three hours, it attracted to itself such a solar or formal tincture that it was changed from a whitish and crystalline color into a blood-red ruby. By this experiment, the formal method of multiplying both animals and vegetables was most easily revealed. For this is the reason why a grain of wheat is multiplied, as it were, unto infinity. Furthermore, no true and skilled Philosopher can be ignorant that the nitrous <note>Refers to the "spirit of nitre," believed by early modern scientists to be a vital life-force present in the air.</note> nature of any thing, which is nothing but air, attracts both the air and the celestial form to itself by the virtue of that secret spirit which inhabits it: since a formal act cannot be breathed into a creature except through an aerial medium or vehicle. And this is also the reason why both the quantitative substance of the creature (in respect to the aerial vehicle) and the formal essence of the creature increase daily and have their growth. From this it is clear that from that same spirit both vegetation and multiplication arise. These things having been perceived with diligence, the reason will be ready at hand as to how the chyle <note>original: "Chylus" — the milky fluid taken up by the lacteals from the food in the intestine after digestion.</note>, a whitish humor, is transmuted into the ruddy color of blood by exaltation, and also the mode of vegetation and multiplication in animals, and of multiplication or increase by way of animal generation. But since in my first treatise on Anatomy, where I spoke at sufficient length on the Anatomy of Wheat or Bread concerning the wonderful properties of that vegetable spirit, I will not speak more of them in this place, but will turn myself to the mystery of the microcosmic soul. The spirit of life was inspired by God into earthy man in such a way that I doubt the mass would have been reduced into an animal creature otherwise than when the Spirit of God <note>original: "Ruach-Elohim"</note> had breathed upon the waters; they were immediately animated, vivified, and formed into the image of the great world: for which reason the Platonists called it the "great animal." But as the world was made in the image of God before man was created, and then afterwards man himself, by the virtue of the same spirit, was formed in the world according to the pattern of the Word of Life or the image of the aforesaid spirit: so we ought to consider that man has the manner of his vivification, sustenance, preservation, and multiplication from the soul of the world and its elements. By which he argues for that distinction previously reported by me between the mind, the soul, and the spirit, and shows that the highest mystery of the soul...

...the triad is mind, Father, and Word. It is as if I were to say with Hermes that the luminous and eternal spirit of God, within the Quintessential or Ethereal spirit, creates the soul in the air, and introduces it by means of an aerial vehicle into the human body, in which it produces the effects of life-giving and the multiplication of the species. For this reason he says elsewhere: <margin>Pimander 10.</margin> "The soul of man is carried in this manner: the Mind in reason, reason in the soul, the soul in the spirit, and the spirit in the body. The spirit, diffused through the veins and arteries and the blood, moves the living creature on every side," etc. We ought, therefore, to imagine that the air, which is drawn to the heart through inhalation, is full of this kind of divine Treasure of life; once introduced to the human heart in its vehicle through breathing, it never ceases to attract its like to itself by a certain sympathetic virtue. For nature rejoices and delights in the presence of its like, as we have said. Furthermore, that the heart is the precious sanctuary of the vital treasure, <margin>Psalm 123.</margin> David seems to acknowledge in these words: "Guard your heart," he says, "above all keeping, for from it proceed the actions of life." <note>original: "Cor tuum... custodi supra omnem observationem: quia ab eo procedunt actiones vitæ." This verse is actually from Proverbs 4:23, though the marginal note cites the Psalms.</note> The manner and the instruments through which that spirit attracts in a sympathetic way, and (after attraction) expels that aerial vehicle which is superfluous, are as follows.

Since without the sparks of life and generation, which swim in the air in a hidden way, no mortal—indeed, no creature—could live or endure for a moment of time, it is necessary that these be attracted by the creature and introduced through breathing continually and at every minute interval. For without that healthful act and its effect, the animal must immediately be suffocated. For by the suppression and deprivation of air, the soul will instantly cease from its life-giving act or operation, seeing as it is nothing other than the act of eternal light in the mundane soul. For the soul is fashioned, as has been said, from the luminous virtue of the emanating divinity and the subtle, moist nature of the world; the former assigns the "innate heat" <term>innatum calidum: the fundamental heat of a living body</term> and the latter the "radical moisture" <term>humidum radicale: the essential fluid that fuels the innate heat</term> to creatures. Therefore, this twofold virtue is renewed and multiplied by the constant or continuous inhalation of air. This spirit of the animal, and consequently of the man, is then drawn by inhalation into the left chamber of the heart,

<column-break/>

or the ventricle, by the contraction of the heart's straight fibers. In this act, the transverse and oblique fibers are relaxed, whereby the region of the heart is dilated and opened; this action is called **Diastole** by Physicians. In the time or space of this motion, the heart—by a certain attractive virtue—introduces the air with its vital treasure through the "venous artery" <note>original: "arteriam pulmonum venosam." Known today as the pulmonary vein.</note> of the lungs into its own left region. This Treasure serves not only for seminal life-giving and generation, but also for spiritual multiplication and the nourishment of the vital and internal spirits of generation—just as the Liver is accustomed to draw to itself the chylous juice of gross nourishment through the mesenteric veins for the nourishment and growth of the "natural spirits." These natural spirits are destined by the Creator for the growth and increase of the body's parts. Again, after the vital nature has received this aerial spirit with its secret Treasure, and has introduced it into the left chamber of the heart (as if into its well-furnished and subtly adapted laboratory), it begins to sieve it—or "anatomize" it—to open it and search its vitals. By a **Divine and wonderful Alchemy**, it separates the celestial nature with its divine act—which I call the true Treasure of life or the invisible fire of life—from its grosser and more useless aerial vehicle. It سپس includes such a subtle, volatile, and more worthy portion of the air (which is the essential and immediate vehicle of the vital Treasure, and like an ethereal soul in the air, as Hermes says) into the **Aorta** or the great artery, as if into a sanctuary or casket of vital spirits. Simultaneously, it emits the superfluous portion of useless air through exhalation. This expulsive action is usually performed by the contraction of the transverse fibers in the substance of the heart and the dilation of the straight ones; by this action, the heart is also contracted and compressed, and this action is called **Systole** by physicians. It must be understood, however, that for the better preservation and containment of this golden Treasure of life in that arterial sanctuary, God ordained three **semilunar valves** at the opening of the Aorta joined to the left region of the heart. These are opened by the entry of that vital food, and then immediately closed, lest the enclosed Treasure should exit again through the same gate by which it entered. For this reason, those valves are so shaped by God that they open from the inside and are closed from the outside. In the same way, on the opposite side, those two valves inserted at the opening of the "venous artery" <note>pulmonary vein</note> are open on the outside and closed on the inside; these are called **Mitral valves** because they are very similar to the miters of Bishops. Their duty is to let in the inhaled air and to emit the superfluous and useless portion of it. From this it is clear that easy access is granted to the air, as the carrier of the Treasure of life, into the chamber of the heart, but exit is denied to the Treasure which the air carried.

# BOOK I, OF THE SECOND SECTION.

Now truly, I shall express in a few words the action and effects of that spirit of life, after it has been so enclosed in the arterial trunk. It is certain that, having been made a captive <note>enclosed within the physical body</note>, it dilates itself through the branches and subdivided channels of that same artery throughout the whole human body. For through the branches of the Great Artery <note>the aorta</note>, called the Carotids, a rectified portion of this now-specified spirit ascends to the brain; through those (I say) small channels and conduits, the more celestial and superior part of this extraction in natural Chemistry (inasmuch as it is more excellent in dignity and subtlety than the other parts of the entire fountain of life, and consequently more filled with sparks of the divine mind) claims for its seat the highest region of the Microcosmic palace, as if it were its own Empyrean heaven <note>the highest, most fiery part of heaven</note>. For here the mental ray ascends in its rational vehicle, and chooses that place as its "heaven of heavens": yet under this law and condition, that the rays of its virtue and power expand or extend themselves through all the branches of the Catholic <note>original: *catholici*, meaning universal or general</note> Artery. For this reason, all physicians, both Pagan and Christian, conclude that man's voluntary action has its seat or position in the brain, insofar as it is the region of the animal faculty <note>from *anima*, the soul's power of movement and sensation</note>; while on the other hand, his other two actions—namely the vital in the heart and the natural in the liver—seem to be subject to that animal faculty, since they are involuntary actions. And this is the cause why the brain is the seat of reason and intellect, and as it were the first mover in the microcosmic machine.

Then, in the second series, that portion of the introduced spirit which is purified in the workshop or laboratory of human nature and adapted for vital action is carried into those small branches of the Great Artery which are named cervical: and these are the arteries that assign life to the region of the chest. Therefore, in this place, that portion of the spirit takes on the impression of that spiritual vivacity which pertains to the vital and Thoracic parts; and also in the branches called the Coronary artery, it assumes for itself the internal idea of those spirits which concern the vivification of the heart; and so too in the other arterial branches, namely the Humeral, Thoracic, Axillary, and the rest, along with that life-giving spirit which they contain. For, as this spirit was in the open air, so it was Universal and had every virtue within itself potentially and "folded up" <note>original: *complicité*, a term meaning all possibilities exist unified in a single point</note>. But when it has entered any creature, it is then specified and "unfolded" <note>original: *explicité*</note> as it turns itself into the nature and condition of whatever region of the animal creature it is in. So it is that this invisible spirit, lurking in a barely perceptible vehicle and as if floating in the thin substance of the aerial spirit, not only expands and dilates itself for the vivification and sustenance of life in every limb of the body, but also by contracting itself into a barely perceptible spermatic cloud (which happens in the act of copulation or coitus through a certain magnetic virtue animated by divine love) and now having the impression of the entire progenitor, by a wonderful and swift action and passage into

<column-break/>

the two arterial spermatic vessels of preparation <note>the arteries leading to the reproductive organs</note>, namely the right and the left, it descends from every limb of the body, but especially from the three principal ones <note>likely the brain, heart, and liver</note>. And there that celestial spirit, overflowing with divine fire according to the image of the radical Archetype (in which all things were previously delineated spiritually and ideally and contained "folded up," before they were laid open "unfolded" to us—hardly otherwise than King David boasted that he had the image of the temple totally described by the finger of God, which was then afterwards actually built by Solomon according to that model) contains the internal and invisible form of that body, which in fact was then afterwards to be delineated and produced visibly and realistically; that is, it contains and possesses within itself ideally the figure of the internal or spiritual man. Just as, on the side of the external and corporeal man, the icon or effigy, which is composed of the four Elements, proceeds from the visible sperm of the man contained in the two venous seminal vessels of preparation; so it is that from the meeting of the sperm of the arterial vessels <note>carrying the spirit/form</note> with that of the venous vessels <note>carrying the matter</note>, a mixture is made between the matter and the form of the man, that is, between his internal and external. In this internal part is that aforementioned divinity, which conforms its external house to the image of the species. But we have all this confirmed by the sacred page.

<margin>Psalm 139:13</margin>
"You possess," says David, "my reins <note>the kidneys or inmost parts</note>; from the time I was covered in my mother’s womb, my power was not hidden from You, since I was made in secret, artfully fashioned as if in the lowest parts of the earth. Your eyes see my mass, and in Your book all my members are written, from which days they were being formed, when not one of them yet existed, etc." From which it is clear that the divine power was in the seed, which is the internal part of man, whose "finger"—man having been previously described in his divine idea—is explicitly fashioned out of and in the external seed or sperm. To this purpose also are these words of Job:

<margin>Job 33:4</margin>
"The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life, etc." As if he had said: out of the mass of sperm, the divine spirit made me, no differently than He made Adam out of mud or clay, and afterwards breathed into me His breath of life, and I became a living soul. And Solomon says:

<margin>Ecclesiastes 11:5</margin>
"Just as you do not know what is the way of the spirit, and by what reasoning the bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman; so you do not know the works of God, who is the maker of all, etc." Certainly, this text has a very mystical intention, and can be applied especially to this subject of ours. For just as I used that text to prove existence in the macrocosm <note>the universe</note>, so indeed it can be more aptly applied to this microcosmic <note>human</note> business. For, as Job says, "The Spirit of God made me," so this text shows how difficult it is to explain the secret of human generation, implying that man is ignorant of the way and progression of the divine spirit in the sperm; which intention the sequence of the text also confirms: "You know not by what reasoning the bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman." But whoever...

Whoever understands the action of the spirit and the way it proceeds in that work, let them know the manner by which these things are so wonderfully operated. But all this is explained more clearly by Job:

<margin>Acts 17</margin>

In this vessel dwells the spirit of life; it is the fountain and origin of the internal man. ### The Argument of this Book.

After the author had found the essential roots of Sympathy and Antipathy through diligent inquiry and had explained them in the preceding book—wherein he proves they are nothing but a single Universal <note>original: "Catholicam sive universalem." The word "Catholic" here is used in its original sense of "universal" or "all-encompassing."</note> simplicity in essence, even though that unity is endowed with two opposite properties, natures, and conditions, much in the same way that a will [voluntas] is also endowed with a refusal [noluntas] <note>original: "voluntas est noluntate prædita." A philosophical play on words: "will" and "un-will" (the power to say no), representing the two poles of a single faculty.</note>—he did not think it fitting to conclude only by circumstances and reasons supported by mere probability the **fact** <note>original: "ὅτι" (hoti). A Greek logical term referring to "the fact that a thing exists."</note>, namely, that the thing is so. Therefore, in this present book, he strives with his greatest effort to show the **reason why** <note>original: "διότι" (dioti). A Greek logical term referring to the "cause or reason why" a thing is so.</note>, that is, why and how that twofold act is disseminated into the vast cavity of the world.

And indeed, he found this last branch of inquiry so difficult for mortal capacity to investigate that in the pursuit of such a great work, no small labor and the deepest speculation of the Artist <note>In this context, "the Artist" refers to the philosopher or natural scientist practicing the work.</note> is required. For this reason, he is content to be guided and led on a path so rough and difficult by the light and, as it were, the North Star of those sublime Spirits—both Theological and Cabalistic—who received the resolution and explanation of so great a doubt from the eternal Spirit of Wisdom. For He alone is the revealer of such deep secrets, as the most wise Solomon, the Prophet David, and the royal Psalmist testify. Nay, truly, He Himself, since He is the only actor in Sympathy and Antipathy, is entirely sufficient to reveal this secret to mortals and to paint it in its living colors—a secret which worldly philosophers seek and hunt for with such industry and labor of mind, yet in vain and without fruit.

From the observation of Canons and Axioms, therefore, as well as the sacred scriptures and the most learned Rabbis—both Hebrew and Egyptian—he has gathered that the eternal Archetypal world <term>Archetypal world: The highest realm in this philosophy, the world of pure ideas or the mind of God.</term> radically proceeds from a single, simple, and universal source of light. This source emits an emanation or outflow endowed with ten various properties <note>This is a reference to the ten Sephirot, or divine attributes, in the Jewish Kabbalah.</note> into the Aeonial <term>Aeonial world: Also called the "Evial" world; the realm of angels and eternal spirits that exists outside of linear time.</term> or Angelic world. Likewise, the Angelic world pours those divine outflows of light through an Angelic vehicle into the temporal world. Thus, the ethereal or celestial region of the temporal world is made a sanctuary of divine influences, from which they are rained down—more or less according to the will of Him who sent them—into the Elemental world to carry out His commands, both severe and benign.

By this kind of descent <note>original: "degradatione," referring to the "stepping down" of divine power through the different levels of reality.</note>, the author perceived that God, by means of His Word, has imparted to the whole world a single, unique, and essential yet differing emanation. He did this so that all things in it, participating more or less in the one universal essence, might differ from each other and among themselves, both in species and as individuals. He also perceived that the property of that multiform divine outflow established and created Angelic creatures (or spiritual organs) of different conditions and offices. Through these, and in them, He operates centrally at every moment of time with various and multiform power. Consequently, it clearly appears to the author that, since there are properties of contrary strength in the divine outflow or extension, it is necessary that there be also Angelic spirits corresponding in nature and condition to each Divine property, by whose mediation things are administered in this world. For in these spiritual organs or Angelic Instruments, and through them, the rays of the splendor of eternal influence descend first into the starry region of the temporal world, and then afterward from there they are poured out into the sublunary or Elemental—

IN the preceding portion of this work, you have seen the radical and essential unity revealed in general terms, along with its two branches that are opposite in property (which are the markers of "Will" and "Non-will" <note>original: "voluntatis & noluntatis." This refers to the divine impulse to create/attract versus the impulse to withdraw/repel.</note>), as well as the two universal effects of that same unity: namely, friendship and hatred, found in all things both good and evil, and all those passions—whether spiritual or corporal—which are derived from them. It remains now for us to descend into the depths of our discourse and penetrate to the very "innards" of Sympathy and Antipathy, which are manifested by their effects not only in the things of the temporal world, but also in those of the eternal world. For no one, even those only moderately versed in science—provided they are instructed by Experience, that mother of fools—can be so wrapped in such lack of skill or ignorance that they cannot discern with open eyes the hidden effects of celestial and terrestrial things in the Sympathy and Antipathy implanted in them at creation. <column-break/>

of the words "Sympathy" and "Antipathy," so that you may better and more directly perceive their distinct natures or essences. "Sympathy" is a Greek word, namely <term>Συμπαθεια (Sympatheia)</term>, and it is derived from <term>συv (syn)</term>, that is, "with" or "together," and <term>παθος (pathos)</term>, that is, "passion" or "suffering," which proceeds from the verb <term>πα’χω (pascho)</term>, that is, "I suffer" or "I am acted upon." From this it is clear that the first kind of "passion" proceeds from the divine act or the positive, luminous unity, as if from concord and love, and is properly called "compassion." However, the second kind of "passion" <note>Antipathy</note> arises from the divine power or the dark and privative unity, as if from discord and hatred; these are the effects of two natures of contrary strength fighting against one another. We can therefore not inaccurately define **Sympathy** as the relationship of two spirits, emanating either from the same divine property, or irradiating from two similar ones—that is, those things which draw their radical emanations from the same or two similar divine properties. For example: all creatures that participate in those benign and lovely rays or "irradiations" which are emitted by God through the Angelic organ into the Sphere of Jupiter are poured down from that orb or Sphere all the way to the earth, and are communicated to the infinite creatures therein that live under that property of the Divine Will...

that is, proceeding radically from divine emanations of opposite conditions—such as those of Jupiter and Mars, or Jupiter and Saturn, which are enemies to one another—the arrival and meeting of such creatures, or the sight of their rays, will be mutually unpleasant, with a secret reluctance and resistance of their spirits: so much so, that by a certain natural instinct, one desires in every way to flee and avoid the sight of the other; and the spirit of one endeavors to resist the rays emitted by the other, as will be more clearly expressed in what follows. But, since the general cause of Sympathy and Antipathy is a certain hidden and secret emanation or irradiation from one creature into another, it will be necessary to look into the very marrow of so profound a business, so that we may more plainly and clearly discern the general source and root of all radiations and emanations: for by this means we shall uncover the hidden cause of the differences in them, and follow their extensions—namely, from their root to the trunk, and from the trunk to the branches, and finally from the branches to the twigs and leaves—descending through almost infinite individuals.

### CHAPTER II.

#### *How and by which attributes or properties of God the Hebrew Rabbis and more skilled Kabbalists prove that the contrariety of natures depends upon a single eternal essence, as if from the root of all things.*

<margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*, book 3.</margin>
It is established as certain that, just as there are infinite creatures of diverse natures in the machine of the world, so indeed any one of them was created in various forms in the beginning, and then afterwards from that time generated in a successive manner through various influences of heaven and many thousands of varieties of rays descending from above, and sustained from the moment of generation until that of corruption. Wherefore the wiser of the Kabbalistic Rabbis affirm that there is not any plant or herb below that does not have a star in the firmament which strikes it and says to it, "Grow." Nor does the Scripture seem to oppose this opinion of theirs, as will be declared below. But since the radical investigation of this matter requires a still higher speculation, it is necessary first of all that we search with diligence how all creation was effected by the emission of divine rays, and whether that emanation of rays was ordered in a property that is manifold, or of one and the same condition. I have manifested to you clearly enough in the preceding sections that all things were created in the beginning of things by one eternal spirit of Wisdom, who, like an eternal messenger or Universal Angel <note>original: "Angelus Catholicus."</note> from *Ensoph* <term>Ein Sof: The Infinite or "Without End," referring to the divine origin in Kabbalah.</term> (as the Kabbalists say)—that is, from the infinity or infinite source of light—was sent forth in the form of an emanation or a most splendid

<column-break/>

<margin>Wisdom 7:25. John 1:1. John 1:5.</margin>
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 1:24. Proverbs 8.</margin>
outflow to all things enfolded and reserved in the divine power, to give them form and bring them into explicit action: and this I shall endeavor to prove from these testimonies of Holy Scripture. Solomon calls that spirit a "holy spirit of discipline," a "vapor of the power of God," and a "certain pure emanation of the brightness of the Almighty God," and the "brightness of eternal light," and a "mirror without spot of His Majesty," and the "image of His goodness": which, since it is one, can do all things, and remaining in itself, it renews all things, etc. By which he argues that although it is in its essence only a single emanation, yet by reason of the multiplicity of its properties it can do all things, however much they may seem to us to be of contrary condition. Hence the Text says elsewhere: *There is in wisdom a spirit that is unique, manifold, etc.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 7:22.</note>—that is, a divine outflow unique in essence or substance, but manifold in property. Furthermore, Saint John confesses that the life of all was in the Word. And yet the essence of the Word, in which was life, is unique, being indeed light, in which there are no darknesses at all, however much we notice that the life or conditions of creatures are various, and as much Antipathetic as Sympathetic. And Sirach <note>Referring to the author of Ecclesiasticus.</note> says that this Spirit proceeds from the mouth of the Most High: And Solomon, that it was with Jehovah in the beginning of His way, composing all things in creation:

...nining: From which it is clear, that it was through the emanation or extension of universal <note>original: "Catholicorum," here meaning all-encompassing or general.</note> rays from the eternal, unique, luminous source, that all things were multi-formally shaped and animated. But that emanation, according to the variety of the will and pleasure of its source, extends itself into various rays differing in disposition and condition.

<margin>Reuchlin, book 3, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*.</margin>
For just as from the same root of a tree the trunk or body, branches, twigs, leaves, and fruit rise up: so indeed the divine emanation, like the trunk of the Sephirotic <term>Sephirotic: Referring to the Sephirot, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</term> tree, proceeds directly from its root *En Soph* <note>Hebrew: "Ein Sof," meaning the Infinite or Boundless.</note>, or the source of infinity, from which then its branches, and from the branches the twigs, and from the twigs the fruit arise. It follows, therefore, that just as the trunk of the tree rises from its root and seems, as it were, to be created, so indeed that emanation or sacred spirit proceeds from the radical unity, and seems to be created, as it were, anew. <margin>Ecclesiasticus 1:4, 9.</margin> And hence the wise man says: *Wisdom was created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from eternity; He himself created her in the Holy Spirit, and poured her out upon all his works.* By this he denotes that this emanation had its origin from God the Father, but that it sends out its particular rays everywhere for the existence and virtues of all creatures.

<margin>Psalm 33.</margin>
The Psalmist seems to testify to these things: *By the Word of the Lord,* he says, *the heavens were created, and all their power by the breath of his mouth.* Here, therefore, you have the origin of that spirit and its office in the world—namely, that it attributes to every creature its own force or power of moving, living, acting, multiplying, and pursuing one another with love or hatred according to the will of its Father. Wherefore it is clear from the aforesaid that this spirit, with respect to its essential essence, is eternal, but by reason of its emanation into the world, it is called "aeveal" <note>original: "aevialis," referring to *aevum*, a state of existence between time and eternity, often associated with angels.</note> or of an Angelic nature. Whence the preceding text says: *And the understanding of prudence from eternity.*

We proceed, therefore, in the progression and multiplication of that emanation in this manner: From the trunk of the tree go forth branches, both general and special as well as individual; those which are stronger, coming after the trunk, are like the arms of the body itself, then follow the smaller branches and finally the twigs. To these we can relate the different stations of the Angels in the aeveal or Angelic world, assigned to them according to their dignities by reason of the divine influences which they receive from their universal branch or holy emanation, Jesus Christ, sent out from the root *En Soph* or his Father.

<margin>Colossians 1:15, 16.</margin>
The Apostle confirms this in these words: *Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature, because in him all things were founded in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether Thrones, or Dominions, or Principalities, or Powers; all things were created through him and in him, and he is before all, and all things consist in him.* Thus, all the Angels of the higher or Empyrean <term>Empyrean: The highest heaven, occupied by the purest fire or light and the presence of God.</term> orders proceed from him in the first series no differently than the arms of a tree 

<column-break/>

from its trunk. And just as we see that the arms, being closer to the trunk, are more robust, more beautiful, and firmer than the branches: so the Empyrean or "super-substantial" Angels are closer and more conjoined to the universal emanation; and consequently they are richer in divine virtue and light and more adorned with beauty, and this through degrees of dignity according to how much they more or less immediately approach the seat of the uncreated emanation of the source—that is, the more they approach the face of the uncreated luminous essence, which imparts to them the most excellent light and glory.

It is no different than what we see in the arms of a trunk: the closer they are to the trunk, the larger they are in their existence or substance. After these, we see that the smaller branches rise immediately from those arms, and have a place for their consistency distinct or divided from the arms, even if their bulk is not divided from the arms. By the same reasoning, we observe that the Olympic <term>Olympic: In this context, referring to the aetherial or planetary spheres below the highest heaven.</term> or aetherial intelligences or Angels draw their virtues and life immediately from those Empyrean ones; and that in various forms and in a variety of measures of excellence, they reserve those influences in the stellar bodies, as if in their treasury chests, for the use of lower things.

Then, as the branches proceeding from the wooden arms attribute life and being to other twigs rising from them: so also the Olympic Angels pour their influences into those Elemental spirits, whose princes are four in number, presiding over the four winds and the four corners of the world, assigning to them the force or power of life, growth, and generation, and even of corruption. By these things one may see that God, through the spirit of wisdom sent out by way of emanation, and consequently the great firstborn Angel—who was indeed created first of all and has His name—imparts his virtue to the Empyrean Angels, who then afterwards pour out His nature in many ways into the Olympic spirits, from whom again the Elementals draw their faculties or essences.

And yet all these essential virtues, whether in the Empyrean, Aetherial, or Elemental heaven, are continuous and indivisible from the holy emanation, which is inseparable from its root: no differently than the trunk of a tree is noticed to be continuous and indivisible from the root, the arms from the trunk, the branches from the arms, and the twigs or shoots from the fruit and leaves.

Behold then (judicious reader) the dimension of the aeveal world according to the saying of the preceding text: *Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature, in whom all things were founded in heavens and on earth, visible and invisible, whether they be Thrones, or Dominions, etc.* That is, the creatures of the aeveal world, as much in the heavens and elements as on the earth, are founded in Christ: but this is also held by the Fathers of the Church

### SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part I.

#### 141

...since (as Rabbi Moses <note>Rabbi Moses ben Maimon, also known as Maimonides (1138–1204), a preeminent Jewish philosopher.</note> says) God is and has been above all essence, insofar as He existed before any thing was. And this was that precious name that Moses desired to know from God, when he received from Him this response: **יהוה** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God, often transliterated as Yahweh or Jehovah.</note>, this is my name forever. Indeed, this name is so pure that it can neither be articulated nor compounded, much less expressed by a human voice. As for the other names or denominations of God, which are ascribed to Him based on His effects, these are attributed to God not according to His essence, but only according to the works performed by Him—that is, insofar as He appears as all in all, and exists and operates in all things.

It is necessary, therefore, for our better instruction in this matter, that we understand that since the divine nature is and operates in every created thing and also exists outside of them (for He is the center of any thing, whose circumference is nowhere—that is, outside of all things), in this respect His essential name, the **Tetragrammaton**, is common and universal <note>original: "Catholicum," used here in its root sense of universal or all-encompassing.</note>, acting in every branch of the **Sephirotic** or **Cabalistic tree**. Indeed, it holds dominion over the entire trunk or body of that tree, and consequently all ten other names of God are referred to it by their specific properties, just as arms are related to a trunk, insofar as they have a relation to His various properties or virtues within one individual essence.

Therefore, all those names attributed to Him from His works are comprised in Him and under Him. For the properties of His non-willing, negation, and privation, as well as those of His willing, affirmation, and position—and consequently of death and life, of curse and blessing, of evil and good in respect to creatures (even though nothing is ideally evil in Him, who is the highest and only goodness), of hatred and friendship, of discord and concord, of **Antipathy** and **Sympathy**—are all comprised under Him. It is **Jehovah** who kills and makes alive, leads down to the grave and brings back.

It is He Himself who sends the plague, consumption, burning fever, leprosy, scab, ulcers, hemorrhoids, and the sores of Egypt; who strikes with madness and blindness, with fear and trembling of heart, and affects us with cares and vexations. These are ascribed to Him from the effects that follow their pronunciation, some of which incline toward darkness and privation, others toward light and position; some toward severity, others toward the fruit of His kindness; and some indicate the privation of His own act, which occurs by drawing His rays back into Himself. 

For by such an act of His, the effects of darkness are produced: namely, essential coldness, numbness, immobility, rest, freezing, contraction, and so on. Others are produced by His actual outflow or extension from the center to the circumference: namely, light, motion, heat, expansion, thinning, and so on. I wish, therefore, to enumerate those ten divine attributes of God, which are ascribed to the eternal essence as they are found in order on the **Sephirotic tree**, from whose root the eternal rays of a manifold nature or condition descend to fulfill the various forms of the root's will, by which manifold effects are produced in the world.

Thus also God, under this denomination of His, is considered to be the Father of all, and consequently, in this will of His, He is kind and gracious or approachable to His creatures, according to that saying of Solomon:

### OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Member I.

Moses, praying for the restoration of Miriam to her former health, said: *God of grace, I pray, heal her* <note>original: "El na rapha na." This is a famous short prayer from Numbers 12:13.</note>.

The fifth name, ascribed to the fifth branch of the tree, is **Elohim Gibbor** <note>original: "Elohim Gibbor," meaning "God of Might" or "God the Warrior."</note>: and this name is accustomed to send forth malevolent effects and unhealthy influences upon creatures; it causes disturbances in the Universal Element through thunder, lightning, and comets; indeed, it even excites wars, contentions, lawsuits, plague, and fevers upon the earth. The chest or storehouse of its treasure is the star of **Mars**: but the channel or gate through which its rays descend is called in Hebrew **Geburah** <note>original: "Geburah," meaning strength, power, or severity.</note>, because it indicates power, force, and violence. The next branch or arm, that is, the sixth numbering, has for its Lord the name of God, **Eloah**; its outflow or rays are full of life, multiplication, and beauty: and for this reason the trunk or channel through which they are poured into the world is called **Tiphereth** <note>original: "Tiphereth," meaning Beauty or Adornment.</note> in Hebrew; in Latin, Grace, ornament, beauty, and comfort. The sanctuary of these rays is the **Solar body** <note>the Sun</note>, which receives its shapely appearance, beauty, and flashing glory from it: and this is that Spirit intended by Job when he says: *By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens* <note>Job 26:13</note>. And Sirach: *The sun that giveth light looketh upon all things,* <margin>Ecclesiasticus 42:16.</margin> *and the work thereof is full of the glory of the Lord.*

The seventh Kabbalistic numbering, or the branch of the Sephirotic tree, has for its Lord the title of God **Jehovah Sebaoth**, as if to say the God of hosts, and the God of jubilation and perfection. Therefore, the attribute, gate, or channel through which its rays or brightness exit is called **Netzeth** <note>original: "Netzeth," usually Netzach, meaning Victory or Eternity.</note>, as if to say Triumph, victory, and also justice, charity, and love; wherefore the influences of generation, multiplication, and delight proceed from this emanation: the treasury chest of this among the celestial bodies is the star of **Venus**.

The eighth name, by its property, is **Elohim Sabbaoth**, or God of hosts, and the gate through which its rays pass is called by the Hebrews **Hod**, that is, praise, honor, and beauty. The celestial storehouse, which is ordained to receive and reserve its influences, is the star of **Mercury**.

The ninth name, which is assigned to the ninth branch of the tree, is **Elchai**, that is, the living God, or **Shadai**, that is, Almighty God: and its numbering or gate is **Iesod** <note>original: "Iesod," usually Yesod, meaning Foundation.</note>, that is, basis, foundation, rest, and redemption: the celestial **Moon** receives the outflow of this, which is like a small earth, receiving all the aforesaid influences in general which descend from on high: and this is the reason why she is subject to so many mutations or alterations, the effects of which are seen as much in generation and corruption as in the rising and falling of the sea <note>the tides</note>.

...to produce effects both in heaven and on earth, it follows from the aforementioned testimony of the Psalms that there are as many Angelic vehicles, which transport those ten influences into the lower world, as there are Sephirotic gates <note>The "gates" refer to the Sephiroth, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>: and consequently, as many different properties as there are in the divine will, there are just as many varieties of vehicles by which they are conducted to lower things. For I would wish every wise man to understand that the Hebrew Doctors <note>Referring to Rabbinic scholars and Kabbalists</note> judge the nature and property of any title or attribute assigned to God by Holy Scripture through that very effect which He brought to light immediately after its pronouncement. This is no different than how a Philosopher is observed to predict the nature or temperament of a man from the gaze of his Physiognomy, or as one predicts coming effects from signs seen in the sky—namely rain, winds, thunder, and so forth. Now indeed (as has been said), if there is a divine influence of light which animates and informs every Angelic spirit, it must follow of necessity that every one of those Angelic conductors or vehicles of divine influences is distinct or diverse from the others in its property. Since those formal influences that animate them are diverse from one another, they will consequently be prone and ready by natural inclination to carry out the will of the Creator according to that property of emanation or rays of influence which they receive from their Sephirotic gate. Therefore, concerning those Angelic receptacles or vehicles which are ordained to receive various species of divine influences or irradiations, it is my purpose—for the reader’s better understanding—to set forth in the first series the Sephirotic gates or Channels. Next, I shall recount the orders of Angels, from whose number those Angelic vehicles exist which receive those irradiations; and then afterwards, I shall name the celestial stars, which are the heavenly storehouses or sanctuaries of those super-celestial influences; and in the final place, I shall speak of the effects which these influences produce in the Elementary region, having been poured down from the stars into the air, as well as the waters and the earth. We spoke of the divine attributes as well as the holy emanations with their peculiar properties in the preceding chapter; but as for what remains, I would have the reader know that those ten particular emissions of rays from the ten Sephirotic gates or channels into the vast cavity of the world—made for the fulfillment of the Creator's will—have their own peculiar charioteers or conductors. For those most skilled in Theology agree on this: that just as the higher orders of Angels receive their lights and most splendid emanations immediately from God, so indeed do they emit and manifest them to the lower orders of Angels. And

Therefore it is said, and not without counsel, that he was that divine Universal emanation called Eternal Wisdom, which for that reason is said to be created before all things, and by which all things were afterwards created. Thus **Cheter** <note>original: *Cheter*, commonly spelled Kether, meaning "Crown"—the highest of the ten Sephiroth</note> is sent forth into the supreme order of Angels, called the **Seraphim**. By reason of their proximity to the Throne of God, they are said to burn and be inflamed with fiery love. It is from this that this order is adorned with such great excellence and beauty, specifically because of that primary and most brilliant emanation, which is filled with the abundance of the so lovely and benign Father of Light. From here, therefore, this powerful Angel conducts these lucid outflows into the cavity of the ethereal heaven and preserves them there as if in its universal sanctuary. Soon, the spirit of this light is animated and quickened by its presence, so that by the admirable reason of its own action it is called the **first mover of the heavens** <note>The *Primum Mobile*, the outermost moving sphere in classical astronomy</note>, in which the first movable thing is moved; by its motion, the remaining celestial orbs that constitute the natural world are carried from east to west in the space of 24 hours.

From these things, therefore, it is clear what the **World Soul** <note>The *Anima Mundi*, a vital force connecting all living things</note> is: namely, that holy emanation thus clothed in the spirit of the heavens, a Divine irradiation penetrating through the second gate, **Hochma** <note>Chokhmah, meaning "Wisdom"</note>, which is sent forth from the divine name **Iah**. It passes through the orders of the **Cherubim**, who signify the fullness of knowledge and the abundance of the gifts of wisdom. The influences of this irradiation <margin>i</margin> are said to be received by the Archangel **Zophiel** <note>Jophiel, meaning "Beauty of God"</note> (for this name denotes beauty), insofar as he is filled with infinite particular rays of life. There are, however, others among the Kabbalists who call this conductor of these rays **Raziel**, who directs them immediately into the Firmament or the starry heaven, and especially into that Zone of the heaven called the **Zodiac** and the sign-bearer. He argues by the etymology of his own name <note>Raziel translates as "Secret of God"</note> that the rays of this gate, hidden within him in a folded manner, ideally outline the infinite species of particular creatures, all of which he later depicts realistically and explicitly in the Elementary region.

The third outflow of rays occurs through the gate **Binah** <note>Meaning "Understanding"</note>, over which the divine name **Elohim** presides, and it descends immediately into the order of the **Thrones**; from this, one may infer the severe property of God, full of judgment. These rays are received by the Archangel **Zabkiel**, or as others would have it, **Zaffiel**, signifying the Spirit of great wrath. This spirit conducts these influences to the **Sphere of Saturn**, which he fills with Spirits or Intelligences of his own nature, called Saturnines, or **Bene-Elohim** <note>Sons of God</note>; finally, these pour forth influences or subtle spirits of their own nature into the Elementary world—namely, the air, water, and earth.

The fourth emanation is conducted through the Channel **Chesed** <note>Meaning "Mercy" or "Kindness"</note>, over which the holy name **El** presides. It is received by the Archangel of the order of **Dominations**, who asserts power against malignant spirits and assigns life and breath to creatures. This Archangel is called **Zadkiel**, which signifies the spirit of justice; and this spirit, according to the nature

of the influence which he conducts, is a friend of true justice in the proportion of life and the Elements: and consequently a favorer and Patron of the life of creatures. He carries these rays downward into the orb of **Jupiter**, filling it with infinite spirits of his own nature and condition, which are called Jovial Intelligences. These rain down a portion of their influence upon the sublunary creatures subject to them, by which they live, multiply, and are preserved.

The fifth emission of rays occurs through the gate **Geburah** <note>Meaning "Strength" or "Severity"</note>, whose president is the divine name **Elohim Gibbor** <note>God of Might</note>. These rays are said to descend to the order of **Powers** <note>Potestates</note>. The Archangel to whom these rays are committed is called **Samael**, or as others prefer, **Hamael**. He is the Spirit who brings terror; and this Intelligence conducts these rays into the Sphere or orb of **Mars**, filling it with spirits or Intelligences of his own nature. By the fiery heat of his condition, he kindles the Martial star, from which Martial influences are poured into the Elementary region, and especially upon the creatures subject to it.

The sixth emission of divine rays occurs through the Sephirotic Channel **Tiphereth** <note>Meaning "Beauty"</note>, whose lord is the Name of God **Eloah**. These descend immediately into the order of **Virtues**. Hence Isidore <note>St. Isidore of Seville, an influential early medieval scholar</note> says that the Angels of this order receive illumination, purification, and perfection from God. Under the leadership of the Archangel **Michael** (whose name signifies "Who is like God?"), they are conducted into the **Sphere of the Sun**, and from there they distill to the lower parts for the quickening, multiplication, preservation, and adornment of creatures.

The seventh extension of rays occurs through the gate or Channel **Netzeth** <note>Netzach, meaning "Victory"</note>, over which the name **Jehovah Sebaoth** <note>The Lord of Hosts</note> presides. From there they pass to the order of **Principalities**, from which they are carried by the Archangel **Anaël** to the **Sphere of Venus**, from which they then descend to the creatures subject to it in the Elementary world.

The eighth emission of rays occurs through the gate **Hod** <note>Meaning "Splendor"</note>, and the name **Elohim Sebaoth** presides over this. These descend into the order of **Archangels**, where they are conducted by the Archangel **Raphael** into the **Sphere of Mercury**, and from there are sent into the creatures in the Elemental world subject to them.

The ninth emanation of light occurs through the gate **Iesod** <note>Yesod, meaning "Foundation"</note>, over which the name **Sadai** <note>Shaddai, meaning "Almighty"</note> presides. This descends to the order of **Angels**, and there they are received by the Archangel **Gabriel** and conducted to the **orb of the Moon**, from which they descend to the lower parts for the animation and quickening of the creatures subject to it.

The tenth and final extension of rays occurs through the Channel **Malchut** <note>Malkuth, meaning "Kingdom"</note>, which is dominated by the name **Adonai** <note>Lord</note>.
