### SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Member I. ###

...the elemental world. These are the intentions of the Kabbalists regarding this mystery of Angelic irradiations.

Through the continuity of these individual, opposing emanations from God to the principal Angels, and from them to the **Olympic spirits** <note>In Renaissance magic, these are seven spirits—such as Aratron or Bethor—who govern the planetary spheres and their influences</note>, and from those to the **sublunary** <note>original: *sublunares*; referring to the region below the Moon, which includes the Earth and its atmosphere</note> spirits, we can gather several points. First, that God alone works all things in all beings. Second, that according to the variety of His will, He acts in diverse forms within this world. Consequently, we must understand that His will is multiform in its properties, since things are brought about both in heaven and on earth according to a multiform operation, as is right to conclude from their effects. Therefore, if God works all in all, it is necessary that the diversity of that work proceeds from the multiplicity of His will.

<margin>*Asclepius*, book 4</margin>
For this reason, Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many esoteric texts are attributed</note> says: "The will of God is the supreme perfection of things, which necessity follows; and necessity is accompanied by the effect." Consequently, he concludes that God is accustomed to complete both His will and its effect in a single moment of time. But what He does not wish to exist, that thing cannot be. Therefore, whatever exists in the nature of things, of whatever property it may be, is brought about according to the will of one of these divine attributes. "Nor," says Hermes, "is it credible that what has pleased God will later displease Him, since He knew both that it would happen and that it would please Him 
<margin>Wisdom 11</margin> 
long before." Thus Solomon says: "How could anything have remained, unless you had willed it?" <note>original: *Ecquid mansurum fuisset aliquid, nisi tu voluisses?*; a reference to the apocryphal Wisdom of Solomon 11:25</note> Third, it is according to the variety of the divine will that all things were created, of which one either spiritually **Sympathizes** <term>Sympathy: A natural attraction or harmony between two things based on shared spiritual qualities</term> in affection with another, or both **Antipathize** <term>Antipathy: A natural repulsion or discord between things due to conflicting spiritual influences</term> between themselves, by reason of rays of a contrary condition, according to either the concordant or opposing nature of the Angelic irradiation or the emanation of rays from one spiritual creature to another. This contrariety of conditions proceeds from the variety of properties that exist in the will of the one eternal essence. In this manner, all the creatures of this world, both spiritual and corporal, were composed; and in this way they were quickened and animated by rays, of which one is contrary to another in condition, or joined by reason of their concordance and similarity of nature. They rejoice greatly when the rays of a single influence look upon one another. We must know, however, that although every creature has its radical information from these emanations, yet in their generations and multiplications they can vary and differ from the condition of their created or generated parents, by reason of the union of two different irradiations at the hour of birth. Hence it happens that a son can be unlike his parents in both form and condition: for example, a horse might be more

<column-break/>

furious or more mild than its sire; or a plant or fruit might be more loose, watery, and unhealthy than the tree from which it was taken as a cutting. Consequently, through the application of Angelic rays of contrary strength at the birth of a human, the irradiation or emission of rays from a plant, flower, or beast, etc., can perpetually **Antipathize** with that person. For instance, I knew a noblewoman whose nature was so contrary to the irradiation of a rose that by its mere contact while she was sleeping, a blister was raised on her face. Furthermore, another person held such hatred for a cat, and another for a duck, that by their mere sight they were accustomed to fall into a state of **lipothymia** <note>original: *lypothymiam*; a medical term for fainting or a sudden loss of strength</note>. And while the opposition between the Elements is manifest in respect to that contention and strife between discordant natures—namely, cold and heat, and so on—so that in this case the root of such Sympathy and Antipathy, or rather the opposition of the Elements, is well known to everyone (specifically the reason for the enmity between water and fire, or between air and earth), it must nevertheless be understood from what was said above that there is an even more latent and internal cause of true Sympathy and Antipathy in things. This is ascribed by some to the hidden natures of the stars, when in truth it proceeds from those Angelic influences of contrary strength which emanate invisibly and in a hidden manner from creatures that were born under contrary and discordant emanations.

<margin>Reuchlin, book 2, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*</margin>
Reuchlin <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar who introduced Greek and Hebrew studies to his country and wrote extensively on the Kabbalah</note> describes this excellently from these principles: "It is proven," he says, "to the Peripatetic philosophers <note>Followers of Aristotle</note> that every spherical heaven, besides its essential form, has an assistant intelligence as the mover of its orb, which is called an Angel. For this reason, having been sent to this office, understanding and willing, it completes the commands of the Creator as a middle power between God and nature. From this intelligence come operations in things which their nature either had not made, or had not made in such a way—operations which some say proceed from an 'occult property' and others 'because it is so.'" These are his words. From this, it is clear that the hidden Sympathy and Antipathy of things, both in celestial and terrestrial matters, proceed and are derived from the mystic and secret actions or irradiations of Angelic Spirits. These spirits first receive those properties from the peculiar influences or emanations that descend from the **Sephirotic gates** <note>The ten channels or attributes in Kabbalistic thought through which the Divine is revealed and acts upon the world</note>, or from the eternal fountain. But since it is not the office of the Astrologer to immerse himself so deeply in those mysteries which belong to the **aeonial world** <note>original: *mundum ævialem*; the world of eternal or everlasting duration, higher than the temporal world</note>—inasmuch as it is his job to make the celestial stars the fountain and origin of those effects that descend to work through both Sympathy and Antipathy in lower things—I wish now, in the Astrological manner, to indicate how both Sympathy and Antipathy arise from the manifold influence of the stars.

### CHAPTER IV.

-> Where the astrological reasoning for Sympathy and Antipathy is explained; where it is also proved that, since all lower spirits receive the influences of their natures from above, and since Elemental creatures are nothing but images of celestial ones, it must necessarily follow that, just as there are both Sympathetic and Antipathetic aspects or irradiations between two or more celestial bodies, there must also be a similar emission of rays from one Elemental body to another, which, according to the nature of the emanation, are either Sympathetic or Antipathetic. <-

**Having established the foundation** with the Hebrew mystical and Kabbalistic <note>original: *Cabalisticis*; referring to the Jewish tradition of mystical interpretation of the Bible</note> theologians regarding Sympathy and Antipathy, it remains now for us to reveal their secrets in an Astrological manner. We shall do this by taking the visible instrument as the representative of the invisible agent—that is, the external form of a creature for its internal Angelic virtue, and the influence of the stars for the hidden and central emanation of divinity. This divinity (as has been said) is poured into those spirits or "intelligences" that inhabit and illuminate the stars. From them, it sends forth the influences of that light into the Elemental world to animate the winds—according to the fourfold change of the common Universal Element—and to produce multiform "meteors" <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning</note> and perfectly mixed bodies.

It is necessary, therefore (speaking Astrologically), that there be a manifest opposition or agreement, not only in respect to the manifest Elements or winds, qualities or natures which are discerned to be in both the fixed stars and the wandering ones (for the watery signs of the zodiac are contrary to the fiery, the nocturnal to the diurnal, the eastern to the western, the masculine to the feminine, and so on), but also in a more hidden respect. For those more skilled in Astrology have noted that, just as Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon are joined in friendship with Saturn, so Mercury, Mars, and Venus are his enemies. Again, all the planets except Mars are friends to Jupiter. Furthermore, regarding the others of the Sun and Moon, except for Venus alone, who is a friend to Mars, the Sun and Mercury are his [Mars'] greatest enemies. Jupiter and Venus are also friends of the Sun; conversely, Mars, Mercury, and the Moon are the Sun's enemies. All planets are said to love and cherish Venus except Saturn. Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn are friends to Mercury, while his enemies are the Sun, the Moon, and Mars. The friends of the Moon are Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn; her enemies are Mars and Mercury. The friends to the Head of the Dragon <note>original: *Capiti Draconis*; also known as the North Node, the point where the moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic</note> are Jupiter and Venus; its enemies are Saturn and Mars. Finally, the enemies of the Tail of the Dragon <note>original: *caudae Draconis*; the South Node</note> are Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus, while on the other hand its friends are Saturn and Mars. 

Besides these, it should be noted that there is another kind of friendship and enmity among the planets, namely, when one of them is in its "exaltation" <note>A position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is particularly strong</note> in the house of another; in this case, the thing subject to the influence of the one will lovingly re-

<column-break/>

-ceive the "aspect" <note>The angular relationship between two celestial bodies</note> of the other. On the other hand, the "detriment" <note>original: *detrimentum*; a sign where a planet's power is weakened because it is opposite its home sign</note> of one in the house of another will cause the spirit of a creature born under that planet which is in detriment—and through the bad aspect of the other who is in its own house where the detriment occurs—to look "Antipathetically" upon anything subject to the dominion of the other. In this way, I say, the presence of a thing born under that planet will be unwelcome and hateful to the other, whose birth-dominion finds its detriment in that same house. 

Conversely, it should be observed that two creatures will sympathize with each other and look upon one another with joy and gladness when the Lords of their births agree in nature, hidden virtue, and strength. For example, if Mars is the Lord of one's birth and Venus of the other's, these two planets agree by a certain natural instinct. Likewise, Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, and the Moon harmonize with each other. Furthermore, we ought to know that a sign of the zodiac which possesses many "dignities" <note>Astrological strengths, such as being in its own House, Triplicity, Face, or Exaltation</note> of a single planet—such as its House, Triplicity, Face, Exaltation, or Term—will sympathize and agree excellently with the "nativity" <note>The birth chart or horoscope</note> of that planet. 

On the other hand, a sign or some fixed impression of the firmament that is opposite in condition to the planet, or full of misfortunes (for example, if a planet were in its "fall" or "detriment"), creates a certain hidden hatred by means of its rays. Moreover, the manner of the "ejaculation" or casting of those rays from one another usually brings about a quite wonderful alteration between two creatures or subjects. For as the rays of the stars related to one another at the birth of an animal, so that true aspect of rays will remain and be expressed in the thing born or the vegetation produced. Therefore, I intend to express the nature of those rays or secret irradiations that accompany the influences of the stars in an even broader and fuller way, since the Astrological secret of Sympathy and Antipathy in lower things consists within them.

### SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part I.

...which cannot be found so completely in any other thing in which the emission of rays is contained. Just as the stars themselves are different in nature, the rays in these various stars are of different natures: for every star has its own position in the **world-machine** <note>original: *mundana machina*; a common Renaissance term describing the universe as a complex, divinely-ordered mechanism</note> that is different from all others. From this, it necessarily follows that every star obtains a different relationship—or **aspect** <note>The angular distance between celestial bodies that determines their astrological influence</note>—to all others, and to all things and places contained within the world. 

A variation in aspect varies the effect of the rays, just as the other properties of the stars themselves vary. Thus, it happens that every star works differently and produces different results in diverse places and things, no matter how small or slightly they differ. This is because the entire operation of the stars proceeds through rays, which change within themselves at every different aspect. For the ray that proceeds from the center of a star to the center of the Earth is proven to be the strongest in the operation of its **nature** <note>original: *specie*; here referring to its essential character or form</note>; however, those rays that are slanted from the center of the Earth are weakened in their effect in proportion to that slant—unless they are strengthened in those same places by the concurring rays of other stars. 

Indeed, every star pours out its rays into every place, and because of this, the diversity of rays fused together into one varies the contents of all places; for in every different place, there is a different "tone" of rays derived from the total **celestial harmony**. Furthermore, because this harmony is continually changing through the constant motion of the planets and other stars, it continuously moves the Elemental world and all its contents into different conditions, bringing them into action according to the requirements of that specific time's harmony—even though to human senses, the other things of the world may seem to remain the same. 

It is clear, therefore, that all different places and times constitute unique individuals in this world. The celestial Harmony achieves this through the rays projected into the world, which are continually diversifying themselves. From this, it is evident that the irradiations of all stars have different operations on the things of this world according to the diversity of the properties of those things, insofar as all things exist and are derived from the emanation or emission of these rays. 

Furthermore, it should be noted that the condition of celestial harmony is such that, since all stars are of different natures, and for that reason all their rays have different effects in the Elementary world, it happens that their radial operations may assist one another in the same matter or subject, or conversely, may hinder one another. It must also be observed that over any thing of this lower world, a **predominant star** is ordained, and there is likewise a certain celestial sign that presides over its work and property. From this condition of stellar rays among themselves, such a great difference and diversity of things arises that one can hardly find 

<column-break/>

two or more things in the world that are similar to each other in every respect, even if human sense is sufficient in some cases to perceive their difference. 

They conclude, therefore, that celestial harmony works so differently in various places and times that it sometimes produces similar things and sometimes dissimilar things, both in shape and in property. Even now, it produces similar things through similar motion, and sometimes dissimilar things through dissimilar motion—namely, through slow and fast motion. 

When these things are well-weighed, and since it is evident that the Elemental world was made after the pattern of the celestial, so that whatever is contained in the elemental world contains within itself the image of the celestial, we ought by no means to doubt that all things in this world—whether they be **substances** or **essential accidents** <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, a "substance" is what a thing is (like a tree), while "accidents" are its non-essential properties (like its height or color)</note>—emit their rays toward one another in imitation of those stars under whose dominion they were born. For otherwise, it would be impossible for them to encompass within themselves the figure of the starry world. 

This is confirmed clearly and sensibly in certain things: for fire emits heat to its neighboring parts, and likewise, the earth exhales rays of its coldness in every direction. Even medicines, whether taken internally or applied externally, eject rays of their virtue into the body. We also observe that by the collision of two solid bodies, sound is produced by the pouring out of rays in its own manner. Again, colored things extend their rays, by means of which they are perceived by the eyes; and fragrant things also emit rays of their virtue everywhere so that they may be perceived by their scent. 

Since this is so, we can boldly assert that every thing in this world that has actual existence emits its rays in every direction in its own manner, filling its surroundings. For this reason, **Al-Kindi** <note>original: *Alkindus*; a 9th-century Arab philosopher and scientist known as the "Philosopher of the Arabs" who wrote extensively on the "radiations" of things</note> testifies that every place in this lower world contains the rays of every thing that actually exists in it. And just as every thing differs from another, so also the rays of any subject differ in nature and effect from the rays of all others. Hence it happens that the operation of the rays of all things upon any diverse thing is varied and distinct. 

So far, I have explained the opinions of the most learned Astronomers on this matter—namely, concerning the irradiation of the heavens—by which they seem to make known to us that every creature of this Elemental world is not only shaped by these celestial rays but is constantly preserved by the mediation of their successive influences. Consequently, all things that exist within such celestial influxes are **types** or images of those celestial spirits by whose rays they were formed. Therefore, it must follow by Al-Kindi’s rule that if they are typical icons or images of the celestial figures that shaped them, then it is necessary that they, in a similar way, [emit] rays...

...their own [rays], though they emit them invisibly: not otherwise than the stars, from which they draw the influence of their very existence. For we ought to know (as was said in our fundamental inquiry) that the essential rays descending from God into the custody of the Angels, and communicated by the Angels to the stars, and descending from the stars into creatures, are continuous, because they are indivisible. For there is no formed power gushing from God that can in any way be divided or distinguished into parts, or separated from its source. Since this is so, it must necessarily follow that in the bodies in which they reside, they shine out to others, and look upon the rays of other subjects or creatures: not otherwise than one celestial star looks upon another in this or that **aspect** <note>The angular distance between celestial bodies that determines their astrological influence</note>.

Therefore, I wish you to observe with diligence and attend seriously to those things said by me above, namely: that every star in heaven has its friend and its enemy; and that the reason for this opposition, both among Angels and celestial stars, is a diversity of property in the divine will. From this, so many various attributes of God have arisen among the **Cabalists** <note>original: *Cabalistas*; practitioners of Kabbalah, a Jewish mystical tradition often adapted by Renaissance philosophers to explain the names and powers of God</note>.

I proceed therefore in this manner, and say that if it happens in the celestial harmony that there is some aspect or powerful ejaculation of rays which concurs with the rays or emanation of that star which is the Lord of Life of the thing born, and that the star strongly beholding it is an enemy to the Lord of Life whose rays it looks upon, then the spirit of the creature so born or increased will be subject to discordant passions, such as fear, anger, sadness, and suspicion. This is especially true if the enemy to the Lord of Life, being stronger or more powerful in the celestial **Scheme** <note>original: *Schemate*; a horoscope or astrological chart</note>, makes its application to the Lord [of Life] when he is greatly weakened by misfortunes and especially by a bad aspect. In this way, there happens to the spirit of the thing born a certain insensible species of **Antipathetic** <note>original: *Antipatheticæ*; relating to Antipathy, a natural repulsion or "suffering against" something</note> disturbance between the one born and the thing which is naturally subject to a star of the opposite condition. 

Also, if the thing or creature produced begins its birth when the enemy of its Lord is most powerful in heaven and their rays touch at the same time: then it is necessary that the creature born under the enemy's dominion behaves in **Antipathy** with that creature born under the prior Lord or star, by reason of the emission of rays of contrary strength and nature. This is because the **Genius** <note>The guardian spirit or the essential indwelling nature of a person or thing</note> of the former is terrified and as if excited to hatred at the sight of the other, since its star was an enemy to the first star and stronger in heaven. Therefore it is necessary that those two terrestrial creatures subject to the two aforementioned stars, being present to each other and looking upon each other, are affected **Antipathetically** by the emission of their contrary rays, and the one whose Lord is stronger will prevail: not otherwise than the matter stood with their stars in heaven. But, you ought to observe that, although stronger rays are **Antipathetic** to weaker ones, it does not follow that the weaker ones are **Antipathetic**

<column-break/>

to the stronger: since it always happens that the stronger passion is in the weaker, just as the stronger action remains in the stronger. 

But indeed, if a subject or creature under some star in heaven presents itself before a subject or creature whose Lord in heaven is an enemy of the aforementioned star, if there were no malevolent aspect in the birth of the former between those stars, an evident **Antipathy** from their irradiations would not follow between those two objects. And yet, their rays would be all the more inclined toward actual opposition if at the time or hour of their meeting, these celestial enemies look at each other, or make a malevolent aspect with their rays. 

**For example**, if **Jupiter** <note>original: *Iupiter*</note> is the Lord of birth or production of a thing, and **Mars** looks at him in a **quartile** <note>original: *quadrili*; an astrological aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered tense or challenging</note> or opposite aspect, and before that creature (let it be a man, if you please) there presents itself a cat whose Lord of birth was Mars—claiming more **dignities** <note>In astrology, "dignity" refers to the strength or "honor" of a planet based on its specific position in the zodiac</note> for itself in heaven than Jupiter—then indeed the sight of this cat will be extremely unpleasant to that man. Besides these things, the cat can be animated in this **Antipathetic** aspect by a certain fixed star to which it is radically subject, against both the fixed and wandering star of the other.

But on the other hand, if the rays of two planets, or signs, or several, concur in one and the same generation or production of a creature; where the star which has greater Dominion is the Lord of the creature or thing (whether it be animal, vegetable, or mineral) and those planets and fixed stars are mutual friends, then if some subject presents itself that arises under the Dominion and rays of another of those planets: these two subjects emitting their rays here on earth will love each other; and will be joined by the bonds of **Sympathy** and friendship. And the concord will be all the greater the more they agree among themselves in nature, property, and the benevolence of the aspect at the instant of their births or productions. 

**For example**, if **Jupiter** is the Lord of human birth and has an aspect with **Venus** in **sextile** <note>An auspicious 60-degree angle</note> or **trine** <note>An auspicious 120-degree angle</note>, and Venus is more powerful in heaven at the time of the birth of a dog, cat, or similar animal—that is, she enjoys more dignities—and has a relationship through her rays to Jupiter in a good aspect, then I say there will be a reciprocal affection in **Sympathy** between these two creatures. Also if a similar friendship existed in heaven at the moment of production of some vegetable, both the man and that beast will be delighted in the presence and enjoyment of that same **vegetable simple** <note>A medicinal plant or herb used on its own</note>, and if they eat it, it will agree with them perfectly; and if it is fragrant, they will be greatly affected by its scent. 

And all this is to be understood in things which from their creation were not created with an opposite manner and contrary condition—that is, between which **Antipathy** was not ordained from the beginning, such as poisons and the like, which nonetheless successively from this kind of celestial irradi[ation]...

This suppresses and blunts their malice and malevolence. These good angels likewise have their dwellings in the air or the universal Element. ### SECTION II, BOOK II. Part I.

...their messengers are spread everywhere throughout the Universal Element <note>original: *Elemento Catholico*; in this context, "Catholic" means universal or all-encompassing, referring to the air and atmosphere that surrounds the globe</note>, namely in the air, in the water, and across the face of the earth. <margin>Tedec lev. book on the 10 Numerations [Sefirot].</margin>

Thus, we see that there are good irradiations and benign spirits which extend themselves by secret emanation from the "Angles of the winds" into the open air—namely, those which emanate in a secret and arcane manner from the benign attributes of Jehovah, such as *El* through Jupiter, *Eloah* through the Sun, *Shaddai* through Venus, etc. And then Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Uriel, through the mediation of their legions, execute the divine will. Besides these, there are evil and corrupt spirits of a contrary strength in the winds, who have their origin from the attributes *Elohim*, *Elohim Gibbor*, and *Adonai* <note>These names of God were often associated by Renaissance occultists with the more "severe" or "judgmental" aspects of the divine hierarchy</note>, whose celestial storehouses are Saturn, Mars, and the Moon. <margin>Ezekiel 37.</margin>
aforementioned Archangels. For the Prophet, by divine command, said: *Come, spirit, from the four winds and breathe into these slain, that they may live again.* By which the Prophet recognizes that there is but a single life-giving spirit in essence

which completes all this, and consequently, that the four opposite properties in the four Angels who are the presidents of the winds are essential influences or rays of one and the same Spirit of Life in its essence. By reason of these spirits of contrary strength in the air, good and propitious events sometimes happen to the creatures of the lower world—namely, when the good spirits have dominion and the salutary winds blow, which usually occurs when benign stars hold dominion in the heavens. At other times, when the evil and pernicious spirits are observed to blow with a privative and destructive outcome, they are governed by depraved and malevolent spirits. <margin>Joseph Gikatilla, book on the Gates of Light.</margin> 
"From the earth," he says, "even unto the Firmament, there is no empty space, but all is full of forms; some of them are pure; some are capable of grace and mercies; and below there are many foul, harmful, and tempting effigies, all dwelling and flying in the air. By these words, he argues that the entire sublunary element <note>The region below the moon, i.e., the Earth and its atmosphere</note> is filled with spirits, both good and evil. Therefore, it is beyond all controversy that there is a constant war and conflict between these spirits of contrary strength in this elementary region. Some of these combatants are ordered under the veil of the Prince of Light and Life (the "positive" side), and others under the wings of the Prince of Darkness, Privation, and Death. These latter are most ready to perform the pleasure of their dark prince, and are quite familiar with the nature of moisture or water, which is the "matter" of the world and the offspring of the dark Chaos or abyss. And therefore, by a natural instinct, they have great dominion over it. For this reason, because of its own inclination toward darkness, the material world is very easily seduced away from the society of light. Hence we understand from the Scriptures that the material world, the flesh, and the Devil are joined to one another by the tightest bonds. Thus, every pious Christian is warned to be on guard against these three. Hence also, Satan is called by the name "Prince of the Air," which is the more spiritual part of the lower waters from which the substance of the material world arose. But the good spirits attend to the Prince of Light and Life, their Lord, who is the Spirit of Wisdom proceeding from the most lucid Word of eternity.

In the spirit of the greater world and its creatures, stupor, freezing, discord, irritability, fear, hatred, and finally <term>Antipathy</term> <note>a natural repulsion or aversion between things</note> are brought about by the contractive disposition of the worldly soul. All these passions either affect creatures for the better, leading to the solace and happiness of the vital spirits, or they weigh down their spirits and make them unhappy by means of dark and contracting clouds.

Then, afterward, I recounted to you that from this root or unity in essence, a twin branch or double member was derived. This expresses, typically and explicitly, the contrary effects and natures of those properties that were "folded" within the Ideal root: namely, Darkness, which is the fruit of His privative *Noluntas*, and Light, which is the true character or the indubitable sign of His Will. Next, I proved that these two were the principles of all things. Behold, therefore, the two immediate principles of Sympathy and Antipathy, derived from a single stem or root. Now indeed, the passive portion from which Alterity was made is called the created moist nature, or the "natured" matter of the world. # SECTION TWO, BOOK II. Member I.

...is inclined toward motion and life: For these are the words of the Philosophers: that matter is, by itself, ineffective for motion, as it is a dull degeneration from the soul itself. Therefore, it willingly—and from its twofold disposition—clothes itself in the condition of its mother, <term>Chaos</term>, or dark <term>Hyle</term> <note>original: *hylæ*; a term from Greek philosophy referring to the "prime matter" or the raw, formless substance of the universe</note>, which is prone to rest, immobility, darkness, coldness, thickness, and freezing. For this reason, watery matter suffers the impressions of both opposites: namely, sometimes it inclines toward darkness, and then it is rendered thick, opaque, cold, fixed, and heavy. In this property, it tends downward toward the cold center or the seat of darkness, which serves as its mother; in this state, it is rendered rebellious and most opposed to light, motion, and heat. Thus, it is rendered <term>Antipathetic</term> <note>repelled by or naturally opposed to</note> to the actions of light and life. 

We see this in the air and the <term>Spirit of the World</term> <note>original: *spiritu mundano*; the vital breath that animates the physical universe</note>, which is clear, <term>Diaphanous</term> <note>transparent or translucent</note>, thin, mobile, and tending upward; it receives all of this from the descending heavenly light. Yet, on the other hand, by the approach or arrival of the northern cold—which is the offspring of dark Chaos—that spirit is suddenly changed. It is frozen and rendered opaque, thick, immobile, and fixed, to the point that it condenses into snow, frost, ice, hail, and the like. Thus, by the Antipathetic arrival of such darkness and cold, it is made discordant and turns away from that lovely union and <term>Sympathetic</term> approach which it shares with the region of light. 

On the other side, however, the lucid form of the soul—which is the essence of that eternal emanation—gives the air spirit, life, action, motion, heat, lightness (or thinness), and transparency: or, as the Apostle says, "life, breath, and all things." And we ought to note that the closer the spirit approaches the nature of light, the firmer are the bonds or knots of its Sympathetic concord. For, as Sympathy consists of things of a similar nature, so the more the spirit approaches the form, the firmer is the bond of its Sympathy or concord, and the stronger and more effective is its power. For the more a created spirit is illuminated, the less it remembers that natural inclination and love which it had for its obscure and deformed origin. Thus, by means of such a purified exaltation, it seems to approach the nature of divinity itself. 

Therefore, it is the opinion of Plato that if the "middle spirit" of the internal man—that is, the one situated between the mental ray and the dark spirit of the body—clings more to the mind than to the <term>Elemental</term> spirit of the body, it will then migrate into the nature of a Good <term>Daemon</term> <note>original: *Dæmonis*; in the ancient sense, a "daemon" was a guiding spirit or lesser deity, not necessarily an "evil" demon</note>. But if it looks downward toward the dark Elemental spirit of the body, it will then be converted into the condition of a <term>Cacodæmon</term> <note>an evil spirit or "bad daemon"</note>, and will be as close as possible to the nature of its dark parent. We are also taught by the Scriptures that by adhering to this divine light—namely, 

<column-break/>

the Spiritual Christ—we shall at last be transformed into the same image. This occurs if our internal "middle spirit," by neglecting lower things (that is, by rejecting the lusts of the flesh), raises itself to the joys and purities of the higher realms. 

But to return to the Soul of the Greater World: If the aerial spirit is delivered into the power of darkness and its prince, it becomes corporeal and is converted into the image of an opaque body—namely, into frost, snow, hail, etc. However, if the effect of heat and the formal act of light prevails over the stupid cold of darkness, then the aforementioned body (whether of snow or ice, etc.) will cast off its opacity and be rendered Diaphanous and transparent. That is, it will be reduced from a fixed and opaque earthiness into a watery, limpid, and flowing state. And again, through another degree of approach to the Dominion of Light, it will be further dilated, so that it is reduced from a visible watery state to an invisible and aerial state. 

Furthermore, by a third degree of approach to the light, it will be purified into the state and condition of fire. Finally, by a fourth degree, it will migrate into the nature of an ethereal or celestial substance. In this state, it loses all appetite for change and is now entirely forgetful of the private stock from which it originally sprang. In this state, it also transcends the limits of corruption and clothes itself in an incorruptible condition, being now least of all subject to mutations. At last, through a fifth degree, it transcends the temporal world and migrates into the <term>Aevial</term> <note>pertaining to "the Aevum," a state of existence between time and eternity, often associated with angels</note> or Angelic state; for it now holds itself in a condition equal to the <term>Empyrean</term> <note>the highest, most fiery part of heaven, believed to be the dwelling place of God and the angels</note> substance. 

Thus, it is exalted more or less in dignity, according as it is more or less obedient to the formal act of the eternal or <term>Catholic</term> <note>original: *Catholicæ*; here used in its original sense of "universal" or "all-pervading"</note> influence. For we must understand that the entire inclination of the eternal emanation is to lead this offspring of darkness back from the confused worldly multitude to the unity and life of the eternal light, so that its effort might turn in the opposite direction from the region of potential darkness. The entire end of the action of the creating light tends toward connecting all things in the world that are divided and contrary to one another into unity, using the "Symphoniac" bonds of friendship and unity. That is, it aims to make the "Universal Son of Darkness" like itself, so that, with Antipathy finally banished into everlasting exile, the world and its Supreme Mind may sympathize with one another in eternal love and friendship. 

Nevertheless, darkness resists this most excellent intention of the light with all its might, so that the duality of unity might perpetually remain in the world. By this duality, the bonds of concord are violated by the hatred of discord, and the laws of Antipathy are maintained among worldly things to the detriment of friendship and peace. From these things, it is clear that the subject matter, redeemed from the bowels of the obscure and deformed Chaos by the mediation of the emanation of light, now remains like a middle substance between those two extremes, namely, [light and darkness].

Universal Matter <term>Materia Catholica</term> <note>the "universal matter" or primal substance from which the universe was shaped</note>, namely water, which was originally drawn from the dark abyss (from which the heavens and earth were previously extracted and built by the power of the divine word), occupies all that space between both extremes. By the spagyric <term>Spagyric</term> <note>an alchemical term meaning to separate and recombine; here it refers to the divine process of creation as a form of cosmic alchemy</note> power of that holy emanation, it was disposed and divided by number, weight, and measure into the upper and lower waters. ### SECTION II, BOOK II. Member I.

...or the attribute of <term>Beauty</term> <note>original: *Tiphereth*; the sixth Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, associated with the Sun and harmony</note> as it ascends, from which it receives such grace, beauty, and life-giving virtue. It is the Father not only of life, but also of growth, multiplication, and preservation. It further penetrates other material things down to the very center of the Elemental world and its creatures, so that they may likewise be animated and vivified by the power of its rays. Consequently, the spirits of darkness are weakened by the glorious sight of that face.

It is as if a string were stretched from the fountain of light reigning at the summit of the heavens to the center of the dark abyss or the terrestrial globe; that string, when struck, would yield a unison. But if it is pressed in the middle, each half-part will sound an <term>Octave</term> <note>original: *Diapason*</note> to that unison, proving a double perfection proceeding from the universal radiant emanation. One of these perfections imparts life, growth, and every other virtue to the lower waters; the other creates a sympathetic concord in the higher realms. 

Now, since the Solar body and the substance of the Ether is a spiritual matter of a consistency halfway between the "waters," it is clear that it is a subject very easily altered by both <term>Sympathetic</term> <note>attractions and harmonies</note> and <term>Antipathetic</term> <note>repulsions and discords</note> passions. Otherwise, it would not be the immediate receptacle of those opposite and contrary emanations that descend from the different attributes of God. We find the opposite to be true from the effects: for some stars are friendly and harmonize in nature with certain sublunary creatures, while others pursue one another with hatred, and consequently emit contrary effects into the lower world, which excite contrary passions or impressions in the vital spirits or souls of certain Elemental creatures. 

Furthermore, we find that animal life consists of opposite actions—namely, in <term>Contraction</term> <note>original: *Systole*</note> and <term>Expansion</term> <note>original: *Diastole*</note>. Contraction is produced by spiritual matter, and expansion is produced by the act of formal light. Thus, the nature of matter works through contraction from the circumference toward the center, but the condition of the formal essence is to expand and emit its rays from the center to the circumference. Philosophers and physicians also testify that in sleep and rest, the vital spirits tend to contract from the circumference to the center, according to the condition of dark chaos and the North wind, whose attractive faculty causes the agile

<column-break/>

and volatile spirit (or air) of the lower world to be rendered quiet, fixed, and condensed. Likewise, sleep is brought about by the contraction of the rays of the spirits. Conversely, in the waking state, they conclude that this happens through the emission of rays or spirits from the center to the circumference. This is indeed a proof of two contrary effects of the "verifying firmament" <note>the boundary that makes things real/actual</note> operating within the souls or spirits of sublunary creatures. Yet, by reason of the equality of every action and passion, they possess a composite disposition toward one another, according to how they agree among themselves in the natural operation of life that descends from above. Hence, it is evident that <term>Sympathy</term> and <term>Antipathy</term> descend radically from the starry heaven.

As for what pertains to the Elemental world, it is certain that it abounds with the manifest effects of these two contrarieties. Therefore, lest some continuous supernatural disturbance should follow—which would ruin the intended outcome of this great "formal architect" <note>God as the shaper of form</note>, whose goal was to place peace and concord in the machine he had formed—He distinguished every region of this sublunary heaven proportionally; that is, by number, measure, and weight. In this way, a friendly sphere was placed like an indifferent friend between two extreme enemies. 

To the heavier portion of the lower waters, He assigned the smallest measure of "form" <note>light/spirit</note>, so that by reason of its weight it would fall to the center of the entire fabric and remain fixed there; this was called **Earth**. Then, to the second portion of the lower waters, He imparted a double proportion of formal light, so that by means of it, it might be elevated one degree higher. From this it happened that the sphere of the **Water** nearest the earth was made thinner, lighter, and more mobile than the earth. For a double proportion of light would cause the frozen and fixed water to melt slightly and be rendered fluid and transparent. Thus, partly because of the continuity of its substance with that of the earth, and partly in respect to its coldness, it is a temperate and indifferent friend to the earth, and a friendly mediator between the earth and the **Air**, which are most hostile to one another. For it is not as cold as the earth, nor as moist as the air. 

Next, the radiant agent of the world assigned to another portion of the lower waters (or the Universal Element) three parts of its light. Thus, that portion was converted into an existence thinner and lighter than the sphere of visible water; and this sphere is called **Air**. By reason of its triple proportion in formal light, it was hotter and more expanded than water. Therefore, while water was cold, yet not

...not as cold as the earth is, and moist; but not so moist as air: just as air is indeed hot, but not so hot as fire, and moister than water. And air, acting as a friend to water and fire (which are otherwise most opposed to each other), is placed between them in the role of an amicable mediator and moderator, preserving them in peace. Finally, fire is the mediator between the two enemies, air and earth, and keeps them in peace. From this it is clear that this Spiritual Christ (as the <margin>Hebrews 1:1</margin> Apostle says) carries and sustains all things existing from the watery mass by the power of his word; and, as <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with alchemy and wisdom</note> says: "Moist nature, by the power of the word, is arranged into Elements in a Harmonic manner"; so that by that power every manifest effect, whether Elemental or Sympathetic, is produced in the Universal Element, concerning which the wise man said: "The elements were changed among themselves, as in a musical instrument the sound of the quality is changed, and all things kept their place." <margin>Wisdom 19</margin> But when this Harmonic order or Symphonic proportion is violated, then the enemies clash among themselves and rage against each other to the disturbance of the entire sublunary fabric. For air contends with earth without any watery obstacle, and water violently invades the dominion of fire without the mediation of air; thus the enemies wage a cruel war against each other, unless a friend of both extremes establishes concord and friendship between them. Here you can see how Sympathy and Antipathy have their cycles in the Elemental kingdom, and by what means, through the loosening of the "friendly knot" of the Elements, their friendship is turned into hatred: namely, when it is in the mind of <term>Jehovah</term> to send out the winds and his altering influences so that, through them, he may strengthen and excite his sublunary ministers of wrath and vengeance against the creatures of the earth.

Indeed, I shall now proceed to prove that all Sympathetic and Antipathetic effects proceed secretly from the action of the spirits administering this world. That there is a great discrepancy among the Angels

<column-break/>

is not doubted by those of sound mind. For although all Angels were originally annexed to the divine unity, yet by reason of the rebellion and ambition of <term>Lucifer</term>, that bond of union was corrupted and violated. Then occurred the division of the waters into "lower" and "upper," so that by this means the good, peaceful, and obedient Angels might be separated from the evil, contentious, and rebellious ones by the interposition of the <term>Firmament</term>—acting like a <term>Diaphragm</term> <note>original: *Diaphragmatis*; used here as a biological metaphor for a dividing membrane or partition</note> or transverse wall. Thus, the dark Angels were enclosed in the lower and dregs-filled waters, while the bright ones had their seat in the upper waters, which were illuminated on all sides by eternal light.

So you can see that the Angels of heaven (insofar as they are created from a purer or more subtle air—the spirit of moist nature—as their external form, and the bright emanation of unity as their internal essence) are subject, in respect to their material substance which participates in both extremes, to affections or passions both Sympathetic and Antipathetic, as well as to the "accidents" found in the spirits of Elemental creatures. Consequently, by reason of the variety and contrariety of their properties, it is in their power to produce both Sympathetic and Antipathetic effects. For example, we will compare the Universal Sympathy and Antipathy of the <term>World Soul</term> <note>original: *anima mundi*</note> with those particular spirits or the soul that is in man; since every particular thing was formed from the universal. We must therefore understand that the entire essence of the human soul or spirit, however invisible it may be, extends and manifests itself through its virtues and faculties. For through its <term>irascible</term> virtue, it despises and hates; through its <term>concupiscible</term> virtue, it appetites and desires; and through its <term>rational</term> virtue, it distinguishes and discerns between the two. And indeed, the entire effect of the soul's essence consists in these three powers: the first refers to the action of the lower waters, which are prone to discord and disturbed by commotions, insofar as they are the seat or mansion of strife and the prince of darkness; the second is compared to the nature of the firmament, which is the region of life and salvific love; and the last has a relation to the heaven of the good Angels or the "upper waters," which they call the <term>intellectual heaven</term>, whose role is to discern among the things subject to it. From this it is evident that all sense-perception dependent on the human soul proceeds from its rational property, just as every effect, motion, or passion of the soul arises from the other two. Now, there are four well-known affections of the soul, two of which emanate from its concupiscible power—namely, joy and hope (for in that which we love, we are affected by joy, or we have hope and expectation of that thing which will make us rejoice)—while the other two are derived from its irascible faculty, namely, pain...

For I would not have you be ignorant of the fact that, since the soul of man arises from the eternal emanation dwelling in this worldly tabernacle, it must necessarily follow that the Soul of the Great World possesses all the same faculties within itself as those with which the microcosmic or human soul is endowed. For it is a well-worn axiom of the Philosophers: **"That which makes something a certain way, is itself even more that way"** <note>original: *Quod facit tale, est magis tale*</note>. Indeed, all the aforementioned virtues or properties in the human soul proceed from the soul of the macrocosm and the divine Mind that animated it. From this it follows that there is both rationality, as well as <term>concupiscence</term> <note>the faculty of desire</note> and <term>irascibility</term> <note>the faculty of spirited anger or defense</note> in the soul of the greater world, even if they are not made manifest to us. We prove this first because God possesses the attributes of Irascibility and severity within Himself: for from the attribute of the divine name **Elohim Gibbor** <note>Hebrew: "God the Mighty," associated with divine judgment</note>—namely through the gate of **Geburah** <note>The Kabbalistic sphere of Strength or Severity</note>—the fires and flame-vomiting rays of divine wrath are emitted, with the Archangel **Samael** as leader, into the sphere of **Mars**. These are the authors of Anger and Bile in creatures, and consequently the origin of the irascible faculty in the greater world. From this it happens that, by these sorts of influences, angry and fiery effects are produced in the Elemental world, such as thunder, lightning, comets, and all wrathful occurrences. Wherefore, as sacred scripture testifies, these are arguments of divine wrath and vengeance; for their effects are frequently war, plague, famine, etc. For they not only turn spirits toward an angry nature, but also disseminate within them bloody and grim effects and imaginations: malice, ambition, violence, distrust, betrayal, robbery, and others of that kind. Furthermore, the name of God **Elohim** also pours its influences through the gate of **Binah** <note>The Kabbalistic sphere of Understanding</note> into the Sphere of **Saturn**, and from there into the sublunary region; this is the cause of fear, hatred, suspicion, sadness, and malevolence in both the great and the lesser world. Behold here the roots of the irascible faculty and its twin affections: namely, pain and fear. Conversely, the name of God **Jehovah Sabaoth** <note>Hebrew: "The Lord of Hosts"</note> pours forth "concupiscible" <note>desiring</note> rays through its gate **Netzach** <note>The Kabbalistic sphere of Victory or Endurance; written here as "Netzeth"</note>, with the Archangel **Anael** as leader, into the globe of **Venus**. For this reason, Philosophers and Astronomers—taught by experience and observation—have made that star the ruler of the desiring faculty.

Also, that there is an irascible property in the Elemental region is testified by that enmity which exists between water and fire, and between air and earth. That there is also love and desire between things in the world is made evident because **"like rejoices in its like"** <note>original: *simile gaudet in suo simili*</note> and "nature delights in nature." Therefore, any thing is moved and turns itself toward its like through a certain natural inclination as much as possible. Thus we see that fire is inclined to move toward fire, water toward water, and earth tends toward earth. But above all, the vivifying spirit of any living thing—which is celestial and therefore exceeds the place and seat of the Elements—ardently affects and yearns for its like, and delights in its presence and society. For this reason, the passion of any creature shall be all the more **Sympathetic**, and the Sympathy between things of greater power shall be stronger, the closer they are in nature and kinship, whether the things are present, absent, or distant. For example, if both are of the same mineral or substance in number, or if they are specific individuals differing only by number—such as **Urine**, fat, or human blood of one man—one can Sympathize with another at a distance. A **Magnet** from one mine can, in a Sympathetic manner, affect the iron of another at a distance. And the reason for this thing, both radical and immediate, I have recited in the preceding pages: namely, because both natures belong to a single divine influence. That is, they proceed from Angelic rays, or an irradiation emitted from one and the same star, whether fixed or erratic. For it has been said: there is no animal, vegetable, or mineral upon the earth or in the sea that does not have its own peculiar star in heaven, from which it draws its virtue and influence of life, growth, preservation, and multiplication. Now indeed, every Angelic nature has its appropriated rays from some emanation of the divine attributes, which is transferred into a certain stellar sanctuary; from there, by the act of the **Olympic spirits** <note>Planetary spirits believed to govern the world</note>, it is poured out and imparted to those spiritual ministers subject to them in the elemental region. And yet, they will nonetheless agree and sympathize in nature with each other to a greater or lesser degree, according as the rays of any planet looking upon each other in this way grant them permission. This is also confirmed, quite wisely, by Agrippa: *In things, there are occult properties that are not from an elemental nature, but are implanted from heaven, hidden from our senses, and scarcely known even to reason; these indeed proceed from the life and spirit of the world through the very rays of the stars, which can be tracked by us in no other way than through experience and conjecture. You ought to know, therefore, that every single thing moves toward its like and inclines toward it according to its whole power.* 
<margin>Agrippa, *Occult Philosophy*, Book I</margin>
So he says: by which he seems to argue that the **Universal Angelic spirit** <note>original: *Catholicus Angelicus spiritus*</note> which gives life to the world, consists in its more divine part of the power or potency of all the divine **Sephirotic** <note>Referring to the *Sephirot*, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> attributes. In this spirit also (as 
<margin>Ezekiel 3:7</margin>

It is that principal and most eminent actor who, by his diverse subdivided emissions of varied rays into and through his stellar organs, works all those hidden inferior effects which cannot fall within the sphere of the capacity or intellect of common or vulgar men, however much experience confirms that they behave in this or that way. Thus, there is not a particular ray emitted by him that does not have its own secret act or property, varying from 

<column-break/>

another in no other way than as we are taught by ocular experience that their effects differ among themselves. For whatever was originally decreed in the secret counsel of the **Archetype** <note>The divine "first pattern" or blueprint of the universe in God's mind</note>, that was brought about or disposed from generality into many specialties, and from every specialty into infinite individuals or particularities. Thus, an age-old effect is the image of an eternal idea, and the temporal world is an age-old likeness; and again, in the temporal or **typical** world, every stellar effigy is a pattern of an **Angelic idea**, and again, elemental things are the shadows of the spiritual **Icons** <note>spiritual images or forms</note> in heaven. Therefore, just as God sends forth his emanation, the image of which is the Angelic world in a diversity of modes and a multiplicity of respects, so the Angelic spirits pour out their different and distinct lights to the inferior orders; and every superior sphere pours into the inferior ones. And thus, from the stars—which also apply their lights to each other through various aspects—these things are rained down step-by-step into and upon creatures, down to the very center of the earth. These creatures, according to the patterns of their stars, shoot out both **Sympathetic** and **Antipathetic** rays toward each other, albeit invisibly. Nor truly ought we to doubt that such rays are concordant and discordant in inferior things, since in the very source of unity from which all things emanate, we observe an opposition of properties: namely, a privative **No-Will** <note>original: *Noluntatem*</note> and a positive **Will** <note>original: *voluntatem*</note>. And it is to be believed in no other way than that the passive spiritual matter of the **Soul of the World** <note>original: *anima mundi*</note> is that subject through which and in which that divine unity is accustomed to excite joys and delights with the fulfillment of the appetite of spiritual matter, by abundantly pouring out loving and positive (that is, Sympathetic) passions and life-giving rays of life. Thus, it now holds its natural root—namely its mother, **Chaos**, or the dark abyss—in oblivion, and is converted into a child or son of light through adoption. And therefore, in this state, it seems to participate and sympathize with those golden showers of nourishing and life-giving light which are rained down from the beneficial attributes of God; and it now begins to hate all those privative influences and avoid them with fear, which are poured out from the severe, unhealthful, and destructive attributes of God. In no other way do we see light shrink from the sight of darkness and delight in the presence of its own likeness, or life be shaken with terror by the death and evil of its opposite. From this, therefore, it follows that the children of light, who are founded upon or grafted into the illuminated Universal Spirit, flee from and avoid the children of darkness as if they were a plague, and hold their works in horror and hatred.

### OF THE SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Member I.

...and hate: And the reason for this matter is that this created moist spirit, already sensing the delight, pleasure, and happiness of its illuminated state, greatly fears lest the privative emissions of darkness, or the unhappy emanation of divine wrath, should cloud its acquired light and darken the splendor of life. That is to say, it fears lest its **Sympathetic** passions—namely joy or gladness—be turned into **Antipathetic** storms of sadness and grief. This occurs by drawing back the beautiful, pleasant emanations of love from the circumference to its center, thereby depriving the spirit of that healthy and life-giving irradiation of life and concord. This is, in effect, the "hiding of the face" or the withdrawal of the lucid act of God, which He had sent out from the center of the creature to its circumference to refresh and gladden it, according to that saying of <term>Moses</term> <note>The Hebrew prophet and traditional author of the Torah</note> in the person of <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible</note>:

<margin>Deuteronomy 31:17</margin>

<margin>Psalm 104</margin>
And David says: *When God hides his face from the wicked, they are troubled; if he takes back his spirit into himself, they wither away; but when he sends forth his spirit, they are recreated with good and life, etc.* This same principle can be understood as much regarding the Catholic <note>Here meaning "universal" or "all-encompassing"</note> macrocosmic spirit as it is of the microcosmic human spirit, and even of other creatures, all of which have their origins in the macrocosmic spirit. For when that divine nature which animates the celestial Sun was angered by the death of the Savior of the world, at the moment of His passion, it contracted its rays from the circumference of that most noble creature toward its center. From this it happened that the Sun immediately lost its light and beauty and—contrary to the common custom and laws of nature—was rendered black and dark like pitch. Thus, that pleasant **Sympathy** which it imparted to the lower creatures and even the celestial ones by its presence was, by such an accident, changed into **Antipathy** for a space of time. This, therefore, was a privative passion <note>A "privative passion" refers to an experience caused by the absence or withdrawal of a positive force, such as light or life</note> in the heart of the macrocosm, and a sort of fainting fit (*syncope*) of the same, when that most beautiful attribute of God, <term>Eloah</term> <note>A Hebrew name for God associated with His majesty</note>, withheld for a time the pouring out of his shining effluents through the beautiful gate of <term>Tiphreth</term> <note>Tiferet is the sixth Sefirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing Beauty, Compassion, and the Sun</note>. Even the palpable darkness that occurred in Egypt was a privative passion in the air, which happened by the contraction of divine light from the circumference to the center. Similar passions will happen to the Sun, Moon, and Stars toward the end of the world. For, if the world was made by the emission of divine emanation (for by the Spirit of God the heavens are adorned with light), it follows that by its withdrawal all things will again be turned into their primordial state—that is, into privative darkness or utter nothingness and deformity. But the production of these kinds of good and **Sympathetic** passions from the center to the circumference, and likewise

<column-break/>

of evil and **Antipathetic** passions and effects which oppose the life of **Sympathy**, is best detected and explained by an examination of the vital actions in man. For two active virtues are observed to be in the human spirit, one of which is voluntary. In the same way, I say, the first mover in the microcosmic fabric is the Mind, or the divine ray, or the Word, which (according to the testimony of <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic corpus of wisdom is attributed</note>) is the head of the human soul. The other virtue in the vital spirit is involuntary, since it is commanded and governed at the pleasure of the intellectual or rational ray. It is not unlike how the lower spheres are forced to move according to the will of the First Mover in the *Primum Mobile*. Thus, the vital action in man is just one of those branches which is involuntary and is subject to the mental will, just as the starry heaven (which is the seat of life, since the Sun, which is the heart of the world, has its residence there) obeys the commands of the Empyrean heaven. Now indeed, as we find that according to the will of the divine essence, an efflux or effect—so lovely and delightful as to excite pleasures and joys in the creature—flows into the celestial region and consequently into lower things from the positive or expansive property of Unity, so too do sad and hateful effects proceed from the privative and contractive power of the same, in which God turns the face of His kindness away from the creature. (And from this, both the desirable or **Sympathetic** passions, and the hateful and angry or **Antipathetic** ones, are produced in this world.) Thus indeed are we taught, as much by experience as by the observation of the most learned philosophers and physicians, that vital action is governed according to the mind of the superior will. It is either dilated by the expansive will of the First Mover, opening the sanctuary of the heart to produce those good passions in the vital spirit which **Sympathize** with life and light—namely hope, confidence, Love, mercy, and mildness—or it is contracted. By closing the chambers of the heart, it gathers the spirits within it into one place, whereby evil and privative passions are generated in the vital spirit, which are accustomed to feel **Antipathy** toward those good things that affect the joy of life. For from the contraction of the heart come sadness, cares, despair, fear, hatred, anger, fury, shame, etc. Just as from the good passions the spirit, through dilation, looked upward even to the lucid fountain and was affected with wonderful joy by the sight of its pleasures and delights, so indeed from the evil ones, the spirit, through...

### CHAPTER VI.
### How Harmony is proved by proportions; what Sympathy is, and what Antipathy is.

<margin>2 Peter 3.</margin>
We have said in the preceding sections that every alteration in the universal Element of water is brought about by that all-working spirit which fills heaven and earth, as that without which they cannot exist; whence Saint Peter says: *The heavens were of old, and the earth consisting out of water and through water by the Word of God.* We have also proved that all those alterations and diversities in the universal waters arose by means of <term>rarefaction</term> <note>The thinning or expansion of matter</note> and <term>condensation</term> <note>The thickening or contraction of matter</note> effected by the act and virtue of the aforementioned spirit. We have also asserted that all these things were performed in various forms by number, measure, and weight—indeed, by a contrary reason (so the Creator willed)—so that from then on, things might vary and be distinguished from one another. Whence the Text says: *God made all things in pairs, of which one is contrary to the other, nor was anything made that is defective.* From this, therefore, comes concord and discord; from this, Sympathy and Antipathy. All of this we can indicate exactly and precisely by this musical demonstration. We see in the macrocosm that the medium of all sound is the air, from whose various measures and proportions various tones or voices are produced, which are either consonant or dissonant with one another. What, I ask, is more unpleasant to the ears of a refined musician than a tone

<column-break/>

in a discordant Symphony? Or what is more welcome than a consonance? We see, indeed, that the tones produced by a pipe are accustomed to differ according to the proportion of the spirit or the mundane air; so that from the same breath of the Musician, it produces sounds that differ greatly from each other—indeed, even sounds that are discordant. 

For if we cause two pipes of the same dimension to sound together, sometimes their voices agree in due proportion and delight the soul of the listener, and sometimes they disagree in a hateful manner, making the teeth of the listeners, as it were, grate. In like manner, all spirits in creatures are proportioned by more or less air, with one and the same spirit of life always acting and working, no differently than we see in the activity of the pipe. And thus, according to their concord or discord, they either agree or disagree with one another—no differently than the <term>Pythagorean hammers</term> <note>Refers to the legend that Pythagoras discovered the ratios of musical intervals by listening to the different weights of hammers hitting an anvil</note> were proportioned or disproportioned in their corporeal substances. Likewise, a string stretched over two <term>monochords</term> <note>A scientific and musical instrument with a single string, used to measure mathematical ratios of intervals</note> of equal magnitude produces sounds that are either concordant or discordant according to its larger or smaller divisions: For example:

Where string A <note>original: "chorda A"</note> of one <term>monochord</term> <note>A scientific instrument with a single string used to demonstrate the mathematical relationships of musical intervals</note>, when struck, produces a discordance with the sound of string B, D, or F of another monochord; yet if A is struck on one, it will harmonize with the portion of string C or E on the other. From this it is clear that, although both strings are of the same width, nevertheless, regarding their shortness or length, the air—observed through both proportion and the arrangement of <term>rarefaction</term> <note>The thinning of air</note> and <term>condensation</term> <note>The thickening of air</note>—is found to produce various sounds upon them, both dissonant and consonant. For a shorter string of the same tension, by its greater and stronger vibration, thins the air more and consequently renders a higher pitch; conversely, a longer string of the same tension, such as A, produces a lower and shorter tone, because the air in such a soft 

<column-break/>

motion is less thinned, and consequently the voice is lower, deeper, and as if "suffocated" by the density of the air. Finally, whether in low sounds, high sounds, or mixed ones, the proportion and weight of the air is the cause of <term>Symphony</term> <note>Harmony or "sounding together"</note> or <term>antiphony</term> <note>Discord or "opposing sounds"</note> through the mediation of the activity of the <term>Universal Spirit</term> <note>original: "spiritus Catholici"</note> within it. We compare this spirit to one blowing into a pipe or striking a string, for without these, the voice is rendered neither concordant nor discordant in the aforementioned instruments. From these things we conclude that the medium in which and through which the Divine Spirit acts—both <term>sympathetically</term> and <term>antipathetically</term>—in this world is the air or spirit, which acts in creatures no differently than air acts in a pipe or any other musical instrument.

But alas! ...nion. But I respond that the matter cannot be so, since experience testifies that iron, by its own power, enjoys its own poles just as much as the magnet does; and, as it desires, it seeks them out through proper adaptation, and by its own natural instinct, it converts and directs itself into the proper station of its poles. Into this same opinion of **Marsilio Ficino** <note>A famous 15th-century Italian scholar who blended Platonism with Christian theology</note> falls **Peter Peregrinus**, who, following the rules of **Friar Bacon**, sought the magnetic direction from the poles of the heavens. Also **Cardano** <note>Girolamo Cardano, a polymath who wrote extensively on subtle forces</note> maintains that the immediate cause of the variation in this stone's power arises from the star existing in the tail of the **Great Bear** <note>Ursa Major</note>. **Luca Gaurico** also seems to support them in this matter, but he adds to this business the power of **Saturn** and **Mars**, and even says that the primary constellation in the Zodiac contributing to this—under whose influence this stone is subject—is **the Virgin** <note>Virgo</note>. **Albertus Magnus** <note>A medieval German bishop and philosopher known for his scientific observations</note> concludes that the magnet itself, and even the iron itself, is directed toward the **Pole Star**, and he says that they follow it no differently than the **Heliotrope** <note>A plant famously known for turning to follow the sun</note> follows the sun. **Bessard** made his own opinion on this stone differ from the others, for he thought that the pole of the **Zodiac** was the source of the magnetic power. Again, the **College of Coimbra** <note>A group of influential Jesuit scholars in Portugal</note> places the cause of this thing in some part of the heavens not far distant from the Pole. But truly, **Martin Cortes** thinks that this attractive power descends from a place beyond the poles or the moving heavens. On the other hand, **Gaudentius Merula** seems to assert that the magnet draws iron to itself with the intention of directing it to the **North Pole**, because it is a higher order of iron, associated with the constellation of the **Bear**.

I confess, therefore, that the rays which are spread out to redeem their captive brothers and restore their liberty, and to direct them to their own fatherland, are most ready and inclined by fraternal piety. But I cannot understand the sayings of Merula in this sense. Others think that the heavens in general are the origin of this stone's power: For **Paracelsus** <note>The famous Swiss physician and alchemist</note> says there are stars which, being full of magnetic power, attract iron to themselves, etc. And this opinion would seem probable, since iron moves to its own poles even in the absence of a magnet (as has been said). **Fernel** seems to hesitate, suggesting the cause of the action is hidden, and at times—namely elsewhere—he makes the heavens the causes of this action. **Scaliger**, approaching closer to the point of truth, assigns to this action or power a certain celestial cause entirely unknown to him, asserting that the terrestrial magnet is not derived from stellar globes or mountains, but from that essential power or essence that was their builder, which governs in that portion of the heaven that hangs at the northern point. And to this opinion **Plato**

<column-break/>

seems to adhere, as one who recognizes the magnetic essence to be a divine power. And certainly they speak well in this matter, but in a sense so broad that their assertion, well considered in itself, appears to their disciples like explaining the <term>unknown by something even more unknown</term> <note>original: "ignotum per ignotius"</note>. For, in such general terms, we can affirm that all things are from God.

But we shall now descend from their celestial speculation and look back to the humility of those who, being more cautious and attending to that old proverb, <term>Do not seek high things</term> <note>original: "Noli altum sapere"; a biblical warning against intellectual pride</note>, look more downward, since they regard only the earth and its effects. Of this series is **Fracastoro** <note>Girolamo Fracastoro, an Italian physician who studied contagion and magnetism</note>, who, inquiring into the reason and original cause of the magnetic attractive power, imagines that the **Hyperborean mountains** <note>Mythical mountains in the far North</note>, which abound with crags of this stone, attract iron subjects of this kind to themselves. And this fiction of his seems so plausible and agreeable to reason to certain learned men that they follow it in their astronomical writings as well as in their geographic tables, descriptions of the world, and sea charts. Nevertheless, if this were true, they would more easily draw toward themselves ships passing in the Northern Sea. **Olaus Magnus**, and several others who uphold his tradition, maintain that this sort of attractive force comes from certain northern islands which abound in such magnetic material. 

But committing these fantasies of theirs to the empty wind, I proceed to the opinions of others in this matter. **Lucretius Carus**, a certain poet of the **Epicurean sect**, seems to dream that the attraction of iron proceeds from an efflux of atoms from the subject: For, just as (he says) according to the opinion of the Epicureans, subtle atoms emanate from any thing, so likewise atoms, like magnetic seeds, are emitted from the iron through a certain union of it with the magnet into the interposed place or space between them; and through the union or entanglement of both bodies, the iron is attracted, etc. Toward this opinion **Alexander of Aphrodisias**, **Johannes Costeus**, **Plutarch**, and even **Thomas Aquinas** are observed to lean. Whereas in the truth of the matter they ought to know that no attraction is made by emission from the center to the circumference—that is, by dilation and dissipation—but on the contrary by attraction and introduction from the circumference to the center; just as we see in a **syringe**, by whose attraction water is drawn into its concavity; by the emission of its "tongue" <note>the plunger</note> by the hand moving it, water is emitted as if from a center, etc. Wherefore it follows that the emission of rays or atomic seeds cannot be the cause of the iron's union or motion to the stone. Rather, it must necessarily be the magnet which has the faculty of attracting to itself rays or spirits from the iron: For it appears evidently that the iron does not attract itself to the stone, but by the...
