And therefore, although in generalities they have spoken nothing but the truth, yet in words so spread out, they seem to express nothing in particular. I will now conclude with the final opinion, which is the most vain and ridiculous of all: **Franciscus Rueus** seems to doubt the power of the magnet. For they do not hesitate to think that all effects of this kind—being beyond their grasp—are "cacomagical" <note>Derived from evil magic or demonic influence</note>, that is, derived from the imposture and subtle delusion of an **Evil Spirit** or the **Devil**. For this man [Rueus] does not speak as they do, determinately and without further risk of doubt, but only doubtfully.

And according to the opinion of the **Kabbalists** <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism who believe the physical world is a reflection of divine emanations</note>, superior things rule over inferior things to such an extent that just as a thing exists below, so it was first made above. They receive it fundamentally from the source of **Elohim Ruach** <note>original: "Elohim Ruach"; the Spirit of God</note> through the attribute of **Binah** <note>The Sephirah of Understanding, representing the "Great Mother" and the principle of structure and restriction</note>, which is accustomed to coagulate and thicken by means of contraction and the central attraction of effects. This process turns what was once rarefied, transparent, thin, and bright into a thick, opaque, and heavy existence—just as is manifested in frost, snow, ice, and hail, through the operation of the Northern act or the property of the **Word of Elohim**.

And each branch, illuminating itself, divides into many formal shoots or various rays, and these into infinite actions that do not differ from the property of the head or radical emanation. For example: the influence descending from **Elohim** falls into the sphere of **Saturn**, under whose dominion are infinite creatures—namely, those which from their first creation are subjected to his influences, such as all things imbued with an earthly condition: specifically cold, dry, styptic, attractive, and retentive qualities. But leaving this Kabbalistic and Astrological path of proof, I will now descend to such testimonies as **Sacred Philosophy** has granted me.

In the preceding sections, I related that the eternal unity—which is eternally one in essence—transformed or ideally formed and described the **Archetypal** or internal world by dividing itself through its properties into a divine **Trinity**. He then explicitly outlined and fashioned the typical or external world according to that pattern. From this, it must necessarily follow that if the typical or natural world was made in the image of the Idea of the internal or mental world, then the parts and properties manifested to our capacity in this world were also the same in the Archetype; for that which makes something a certain way is itself even more that way. There was no house that an Architect intended to build which was not first ideally outlined in the mind of the builder, then afterward depicted on paper, and finally built in reality from stone or brick and wood. So also **David** confesses that he possessed the temple—which **Solomon** later constructed—ideally depicted by the "finger of God." Now, when God in His secret counsel had outlined and ordered the Ideal world within Himself, so that He might compare that spiritual world explicitly and realistically to human sense, He emitted Himself from Himself (without any division of His essence occurring in the meantime) in the form of an **eternal emanation** (which was called His image and **Wisdom**). By means of this Wisdom, this general world, along with every one of its particles, was fashioned according to the effigy or ideal pattern that was in Him. Since this is so, and since the divine essence cannot be divided into parts in any respect—however much it seems to vary in property—it follows that every particular ray, which is emitted in various forms from this Universal emanation for the creation of various things, is one and indivisible with the radical emanation of the essence. And the reason is this: because the mind in man is nothing but a single unity, and hence it is defined elsewhere as a certain divine and indivisible substance. <margin>Al-Kindi, chapter on rays.</margin> Al-Kindi <note>original: "Alkindus"; Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD), a famous Arab philosopher and scientist</note> reasons in the astrological manner thus: If it were granted to someone to comprehend the whole condition of the **celestial harmony**, he would fully know the world of the elements with each of its contents in any place and at any time, just as an effect is known through its causes. If he also knew any single thing of this world in its total condition, the condition of the celestial harmony would not be hidden from him; rather, he would grasp the cause through its effect. For every thing, however small, acting in the world of the elements, is an effect of the whole celestial harmony. These are his words. By these words, this man—deeply versed in the mysteries of nature—seems to assert that, just as there is a descent from unity into multiplicity, so indeed that explicit multiplicity is folded within the radical unity, so that this unity fills every multiplicity. In this way, the unit or **1** is in **2**, and **2** is in **3**, and **3** is in **4**, and **4** is in **5**, etc.; and yet that unity, which is the beginning, is also the end and the middle, and the all-in-all of any number. In this manner, light informs the **Angelic creature**, the Angelic informs the **stellar**, the stellar informs the **Elemental**, and the Elemental informs the **composite** <note>A "composite" refers to any physical object or living being made of the four elements</note>. Yet there is always only one indivisible light, which acts and operates centrally in all of these. Therefore, let the composite creature be opened and the elements inspected; let them be divided from the pure, and we shall find the nature of the stars, or the **quintessence** <note>The "fifth essence" or ether, the pure substance of the heavens</note>. And if that stellar substance is opened, we will perceive that subtle "otherness" of the Angelic nature, in which consists the divine act or ray immediately from God. In this work, therefore, there is a concurrence of the separation of the earlier sensible appearance from the later intellectual intuition; so that you may observe how all things are in any one thing, and any one thing is in all things. And hence **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermeticism and alchemy</note>, speaking mystically and not according to common sense, says: *He who constructs the furnace with our vessel, melts a new world.* But what need is there for more words, when we find all of this to be true by ocular demonstration? For we know that the **Magnet** is nothing but a small portion of the general earth, and yet it comprehends in itself all the circles of heaven and earth with both their poles; indeed, even that very nature in every respect between both poles and circles which the general earth possesses, whence it is called by some a **Terrella** <term>Terrella: Latin for "little earth," a spherical magnet used to demonstrate how the Earth acts as a giant magnet</term>. And thus even the whole earth can be called a "small world" <note>microcosm</note>, insofar as it has within itself two poles, circles, and even the astral and elemental natures of the **Great World** <note>macrocosm</note>, no differently than the Great World in all these respects repre-

<column-break/>

-sents the **Archetype** <note>The original divine blueprint or pattern in the mind of God</note>, which is delineated intellectually by the **Spirit of Wisdom** or the sacred emanation operating in all things. Indeed, to immerse ourselves even more deeply into our diminutive inquiry: if a portion of an iron rod, which naturally looks toward the North and South, is broken off, that tiny portion will likewise have a regard for the North and South along with its whole; and consequently, it will possess its circles no differently than the whole does. And nevertheless, the rod itself will observe the North and the South just as before. This same thing will be found in the Magnet, as will be declared below.

But, so that you may approach even closer to the explanation of this Mystery, it must be understood that this eternal irradiation is the essential and spiritual root from which the Great World in its kind, and then afterwards every particular thing in it, was formed and figured in its own kind. This happened first according to the ten general **divine emanations** <note>The Sephiroth of the Kabbalah, through which God reveals Himself and creates the universe</note> and their properties, which the pagan philosophers seem to refer to in a way as their ten **categories** <note>Aristotle’s "Predicaments" or fundamental classes of being</note>. Then it happened according to their subalternate species of many degrees and orders of dignity, all of which were afterwards made manifest through infinite individuals. These individuals were produced from their genera according to those various rays of the manifold will of God, which that eternal and radical emanation poured into them. All these particular rays, whether greater or lesser, since they were not separated in essence from the universal emanation or Spirit of Wisdom (which made all things and which is their root), are the power of that **spiritual Cornerstone** <note>original: "lapidis illius Angularis"; a reference to the foundation stone, often equated in this tradition with Christ or the divine Logos</note>, upon which every creature, both general and particular, formally and essentially consists and is built up. And that Cornerstone is that most internal and central essence in every thing, which, as it imparts life to it, is indeed the all-in-all of that thing which it actuates and makes to live. And therefore the soul, whose center is this Cornerstone, is said to be in the whole and in every part. But I shall cease now to speak of the activity of this essence in other creatures, so as to speak only of our subject, which is the earth and its progeny, among which we count especially the **Female Magnet** and the **Male Iron**. True and sacred philosophy teaches us that the globe or heavy mass of the earth is sustained by that Cornerstone, and consequently has its multiform powers from it.

Behold here an axiom of divine philosophy proposed by the Creator Himself! Oh God! We always find that when the air enclosed in the top or head of the glass becomes colder—namely, when **North winds** are sent out into the world—it will be more contracted and thickened, and consequently, by the motion of its contraction, it will suck up to itself or lift on high the water below.

By these things is also manifested the reason why one pole allures another to itself and is attracted by the other in a **Magnet**: namely, because of the continuation of the **spiritual axis**, which is produced and forged from one <term>Cornerstone <note>original: "lapis Angularis"; referring to the divine foundation mentioned in the previous page</note></term> or essential

But, since demonstrations of this kind seem too intricate and obscure to common folk—specifically those who are ignorant of the nature of the **central Sun**, which Philosophers call the **Archaeus** <term>Archaeus: In Hermetic philosophy, the vital "master-craftsman" or spirit that governs the functions of a living body or the world.</term>—it will also be difficult for them to conceive what the axis of the earth is, or what the poles are. And again, because the use of the **Magnet** and the practical application of the looking-glass instrument <note>Likely a reference to Fludd’s weather-glass or thermoscope.</note> is entirely unknown to many: I shall proceed to a certain kind of proof and application of this matter which is familiar to men of every condition.

It cannot be denied that man and also all other creatures, both vegetable and animal, are composed of a **living soul**, which is their internal part, and a **body**, which is their external part; the same must be judged of the earth: since it possesses an internal spirit, by means of which it operates in diverse ways. And again, just as there is no animal or vegetable that can exist without air—since it is by this medium that any thing exists and lives through breathing, for by the vehicle of this medium the **celestial influence** is introduced into them—so indeed the **Airy Element**, by means of its influences, nourishes the internal spirit of the earth. For the air from above conducts the celestial influxes into the terrestrial body, which is the matrix of minerals and vegetables. I have recounted to you in the preceding pages that all lower things, with their operations, are **types** and likenesses of higher things: that God animates the Angels, and the Angels inform the stars, and the demons or stellar Intelligences (or Olympic spirits) emit their influences into the **winds**, and the winds animate the universal Element of air in a four-fold way—that is, according to the nature of the **four winds**. This four-fold information gives or assigns names to the four Elements. And although in the universal Air there is but one single substance in essence, yet it is varied in its nature according to a four-fold condition, following the will and property of that unique spirit, who is the sole actor or sufficient agent in this kind of **Protean transformation** <term>Protean: Named after the sea-god Proteus; meaning the ability to change shape or form constantly.</term> from one nature or form into another. <meta>This page continues Fludd’s exploration of the "Catholic" or Universal Spirit. Having previously discussed the magnet as a physical model for divine action, he now explains how God, through the four winds and the properties of the Sephirot (specifically Binah), governs the contraction and expansion of the elements—turning air into solid ice or fiery lightning.</meta>

### ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.

He transforms one form into another through the breath of his nostrils (to speak in the allegorical manner of the Scriptures) or through those windy emissions or Angelic emanations which He sends forth from the four corners of the earth. Thus, by means of His spirit from the Northern quarter or corner, He exercises His attractive, contractive, retentive, and aggregative property, by which He flees and contracts from the circumference to the center; in this way, He freezes, coagulates, thickens, hardens, and fixes soft spirits through the contraction of those parts which were previously porous and dilated. 

But some will perhaps reply and say: "How is it probable that the emanation or emission of spirits from the gate of *Binah* <note>original: "Binah"—The third Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing 'Understanding' and often associated with the restrictive or feminine principle of creation.</note> under the name *Elohim* <note>A Hebrew name for God used in the creation narrative.</note>, or the irradiation or emission of spirit from the North Wind and its two collateral winds, can harden soft things through contraction, or flee back to itself and draw spirits from the circumference to the center, when their emissions are directed from the North toward the South, and they make no reflection by which any such contraction from the circumference to the center might occur?" 

**I answer** that this is accomplished in a wondrous way, to be observed by the more refined intellects. We ought, therefore, to consider in the first order that the property of the attribute *Binah*, over which the name *Elohim* presides, was ordained before every beginning to take on the negative or contractive nature of the Will, or the eternal darkness of unity. For, when God does not wish to emit the light of His countenance, He reflects the heat and power of His light back into Himself (to use the words of **Mercurius Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure, the purported author of the Hermetic Corpus, which Fludd frequently cites as being in harmony with Moses.</note>, which do not disagree with the Holy Scriptures in this matter); that is, He contracts from the circumference into the center, and by this reason the creature is deprived of light and life. 

This property of God is antipathetic to those parts of the world, and also to those creatures, which have life from natural heat, which draws its beginning from the benevolent act and emanation of God, in which He emitted His will or positive virtue from Himself—that is, from unity to multiplicity, as if from the center toward the circumference, or toward the creatures. It follows, therefore, that although the emission of the winds from the North is direct, nevertheless their essential property, proceeding immediately from the Angelic organs of God, is contractive and attractive from the circumference to the center, insofar as it is an emission which, through the animation of the divine spirit and action in the nature of *Elohim*, is rendered cold, dry, coagulative, freezing, and disposed toward rest. 

Therefore, it is antipathetic to and fights against the disposition of the air, which is naturally hot and moist, and consequently animated by that dilating act which the Universal Spirit <note>original: "spiritus Catholicus"</note> exhales or emits from its heavenly Sun and other life-giving stars, such as **Jupiter** and **Venus**. And for this reason it happens that when the Northern spirits are emitted into the air, it must necessarily follow that upon the antipathetic contact of those cold spirits...

<column-break/>

...the natural heat or life of the air flees and contracts itself from its circumference toward the center. Thus the air is frozen—partly through that contractive motion within itself caused by *antiperistasis* <term>Antiperistasis: A philosophical concept where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat concentrating in a cellar during winter.</term> or the clash of its opposite, and partly through the mixing of the earthly form with it—and it is cast down to the earth as if dead and immobile in the form of snow, hail, frost, or ice. 

The retrograde motion of the warm life of the air from the circumference to the center through the violent contact of Northern cold is clearly demonstrated by an experiment of this kind: For if you desire the best **spirit of wine** <note>original: "vini spiritum"—high-proof alcohol or brandy.</note> extracted without fire, let a barrel full of wine be exposed to the open air while the greatest inclemency of cold and Northern winds rages in the sky, and frost and ice cruelly dominate the earth and waters. Within a few days you will find the outer part of the wine squeezed together by ice; but if you wish to pierce the center, you will see the finest spirit of the wine flow out. 

By this it is evident that the life of the wine, at the contact of the most vehement cold, flees from the circumference to the center of its body, as if to a place more remote from the seat of the cold's action and domination. Similarly, one may also see that the aerial life in other creatures—whose formal existence consists in the dilating property of God—is forced by the inclemency of cold to fly from the circumference to the center, leaving the exterior parts frozen and rigid and subject to mortal congelation and lethal rest. 

We observe this indeed not only in animal creatures, but also in vegetables, when their blood (so to speak) or sap, turning away from the Northern cold in winter time, is frozen in their center, so that they appear as if dead, until the Vernal Sun revives their spirits (which were slumbering, resting, and as if dead in the center) by resolving the "Northern knot" and calling them back to the circumference, where they may again exercise their vital and vegetative function. 

For this reason, therefore, it is clear that in truth there is only one **Universal Element**, which is partly subjected to the privative, dark, and consequently contractive property of God, and partly capable of putting on His positive, lucid, and dilating disposition. And it is evident that this common subject is the spirit or air of the sublunary world; for by a lesser thickening or contraction made by the West winds, it is reduced into water; but by a greater compression and constriction made by the North winds, it is reduced into an earthly nature. 

Conversely, by a lesser dilation and rarefaction made by the South winds, it becomes vapor or smoky air; and by an even greater rarefaction and subtilization under the dominion of the East winds (and that especially in summer time), fire or lightning is produced, as was related before. ...and they pertain to the same spirit, as we have said. Certainly, this demonstration can deceive no one, insofar as even irrational creatures are moved by a certain natural instinct either to sympathize with and rejoice in the mercy and consolation of one property, or to flee and avoid the severe assaults of the other, since these latter are antipathetic to their natures. But, to return to the heart of our proposal: it is manifest from what has been said that the Boreal <note>Northern</note> spirit is contractive, attractive, and thickening, prone to darkness, immobility, and rest; and that the Meridional <note>Southern</note> spirit—or rather the wind blowing from the equinox—is contrary to it in nature, insofar as it is prepared to destroy those effects which the Boreal winds have produced. That is to say, it resolves frozen air—turned into snow, frost, hail, and ice—back into water, and refines water into air, making the opaque transparent and the dense subtle. Therefore, between these opposite properties, there is no more sympathy found than that which I demonstrated exists between the equator of a Magnet and its Pole, which cannot agree with one another. And yet again, that both these opposite natures proceed from one and the same divinity or Universal Essential Spirit <note>original: "spiritu essentiali Catholico"</note>, whose work it is to operate all things in all places, and consequently to confirm this testimony of true Philosophy in the earth as well as in the heavens. With God 

<margin>Psalm 147.</margin>
sending (as the Text says) his word to the earth, it runs most swiftly; He who sends snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes, casts down ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold? He sends out his word and melts them; as soon as he blows with his wind, the waters flow, etc. By these words it is manifest that the same word or spirit of God freezes through one property and dissolves through another; and consequently, just as God is of one essence, so indeed is it the same spirit that effects these fourfold alterations within the single spirit of the world. These alterations the ancients called the distinct Elements, because until this day they have hardly been able to determine what the essential form of the Elements might be. But, if they had well considered the four Elements about which they made so many words—though (it seems) they understood them with little essential insight—or if they had rightly perceived that the heavens and the earth

Furthermore, they would see that the fourfold shaping of that spirit was effected by a single secret essence which shapes this Universal <note>original: "Catholicum"</note> Element in many ways through a fourfold emanation. These effects were derived first from the air or invisible waters by thickening them by one degree into visible water, and by thickening that water through another degree into a more gross, solid, and fixed substance, namely the dry earth, as is declared from the doctrine of Moses. This is done not to be joined with its like, but to be separated from its contrary. Magnetic attraction, I say, behaves otherwise: For, just as in Antipathetic attraction there is an irascible separation from the rays of the looking enemy, and an exact contraction from without to within without any attraction—or rather with a certain expulsion of the pursuer—so, on the other hand, in this kind of Magnetic attraction, there occurs an emission of rays from the center beyond its own circumference, so that it might congratulate the arrival of a friend. Whence it embraces its like even beyond the dimensions of its own body, and is courteously received by its like in a reciprocal manner, and finally attracts it to its own lodging—not to pursue it with hatred, but to affect it with friendship and natural joy, and to make it glad, according to that saying of the Philosopher:

I cannot indeed better describe the meeting or embrace of these two than by the example of a certain singular friend, long absent from another friend, whom—as soon as the master of the palace, looking from the gate, perceives him coming from afar—he suddenly goes out, receives him amicably, and leads him by the hand to his house; or, as if a woman should meet her husband, similarly absent for a long time on the road, and receive him to herself with many preceding embraces. And I, by my own experience—namely, in the **Chemistry of the Elements** <note>original: "Chymia Elementorum"</note> or the separation of the parts of **Wheat**—have noted that the "female" in the Wheat, which by Magnetic virtue attracts celestial influences similar to itself, is a certain tender and volatile salt derived from a purified or aerial-terrestrial substance, but is exceedingly rich and bubbling with celestial fire. And therefore, it is rendered volatile by the union of both extremes: So much so, that this "female" is that which allures and magnetically draws down the rays from above, and retains them to multiply its own nature—hardly differently than a bird-catcher uses a captive bird to allure other birds of the same species into his nets. 

But indeed, as for the female mineral nature, insofar as its body is more solid and compact and not easily corruptible, she, by that very same reason—namely, through the attractive virtue of her styptic <term>Styptic: A substance that causes tissues to contract; here referring to a binding or drawing-in quality of salt.</term> salt—allures to herself the essence of the rays of iron (as if from the star of its own nature) to console and redeem her own spirits; and consequently, by the mediation of her spirits, the **masculine body** <note>Referring to the iron</note> flees toward and is attracted to her. For one cannot be properly divided from the other; and when she has attracted it, she retains it firmly, partly for the sake of consolation and corroboration, and partly to multiply her own essence. And therefore, those Philosophers are deceived who deny that the **Magnet** is nourished in an occult manner by the formal spirits of iron, and who say that, although its virtue was increased by its immersion or burial in iron filings, yet, since they found the Magnet neither increased in measure nor the iron diminished in its weight, they conclude it is not nourished. But they ought to know that formal rays in the air add no more weight to it than the light of a candle adds to the glass or the water which it illuminates; and yet it is formally nourished, and the formal essence is multiplied,

<column-break/>

even if not in material substance or quantity. Finally, just as external cold makes the heat in the formal air contract itself and retreat from the circumference toward the center to avoid the assaults of its adversary, so also external cold constrains it into a narrower space, mediated by the action produced by the penetration of the **Boreal** <note>Northern</note> cold. 

But in the Magnet, the Spirit is **Saturnine** <term>Saturnine: Relating to the planet Saturn, which in this philosophy represents cold, contraction, and the North Pole.</term>, and in no other way, by drawing in its like, it introduces it also through the assistance of the Saturnine body, animated by a dryness of a **Martial nature** <note>original: "naturæ Martialis," referring to the planet Mars and the metal iron</note>. This nature is also ascribed by some to the North, but besides this, it affects its like in iron. And therefore, through affection and **Sympathetic appetite**, it is all the more animated toward the work of attraction. And beyond all these things, it would appear that there is also an attractive faculty in the body of iron, which draws to itself the spirits of the Magnet—no differently than the male, or Mars, in his nature desires Venus. But since the female, by reason of her coldness, most greatly affects and lusts after the society of the male, the spiritual rays of her attraction seek with greater fervor and desire, and consequently more greatly attract and allure to themselves the male, who is hotter and of a more perfect nature. Truly, this is best observed in the disposition of iron, which I consider to stand for the male: For although he himself, without the assistance of the Magnet, turns his poles by a natural inclination toward the poles of the world, yet we observe this happens more slowly, sluggishly, and with less appetite, and consequently with an affection that is more formal than material.

I gather, therefore, from those things which were said before, that two like things, which are of an **Equinoctial** nature and of the temperate Zone, affect and embrace each other through a **Sympathetic emission** of rays, from the center even to the circumference. And such is the love of those creatures which live by the property of positive emanation, such as animals of a hot disposition (whether they be dry or moist); and therefore, they do not sensibly draw one spirit to another, but they work through union, which is made by the conjunction or concurrence of lights after the emission of their formal rays. And they have a relation of this kind to the property of that spirit which is emitted by the East or South winds, whose nature it is to dilate from the center, and therefore not to contract from the circumference. 

On the contrary, two similar natures which embrace the property of the poles and the cold Zones love and embrace each other by way of **contraction**—namely, by attracting and drawing in by the nature of one and the other from the circumference of both to their center. Just as we see in a single Magnet divided through the middle: its single part will attract and draw the other to itself, and both tend with a wondrous struggle to be joined to each other in the equinoctial place...

A Mercurial liquor, existing from a stony terrestrial or **Saturnine** <note>Pertaining to the planet or metal of Saturn (lead/heavy earth).</note> nature, is still in its "first matter" and as if in its shell; it exists as a close neighbor to the Mercury of Mars. And so these two natures appear to be joined together by a certain close contiguity and almost a continuity; so much so, that this composition obtains a middle nature between Martial metal and Saturnine stone. It is not unfitly called **Mercury** transmuted in an imperfect way, or a species of **Saturnine Hermaphroditic Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurij Hermophroditici Saturnini"</note>, into which the Martial Sulfurous spirit enters as a metallic form. It receives those Martial spirits and preserves them in its womb like their own passive Mother: and by this means, that mass is coagulated into a stony body.

And because **Venus** is called the friend and female companion to **Mars**, she imparts to the Magnet a desire—a concupiscible fountain—for the attractive faculty of the Magnet; for this reason, she restrains and depresses the irascible and hateful property in Mars with her feminine embraces.

Since in the circulation of the Elements, the earth, in respect to its dryness, consents and sympathizes with fire. Moreover, **Ptolemy** also ascribes the influences of Mars to those Northern winds, which are violent. Furthermore, it appears clearly from **Euphorbium**, **Scammony**, **Spurge**, **Spearwort**, and hot corrosive poisons that the Martial spirit is the cause of the attractive virtue in any corrosive salt, and also in the herbs and gums subject to it: for simple substances of this kind (as **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note> teaches us) are subject to the power and constellation of Mars. Hence, experience testifies that vitriol is cold, acid, and styptic in its exterior, and yet hot, caustic, and corrosive in its interior. And again, Iron, which is called **Mars**, insofar as it is subject to the influences of Mars, is vitriol or Copperas in its interior; just as copper is also known to obey the influences of **Venus**, whence it is also frequently called Venus.

...the temple of God, a limb of Christ, and a dwelling-place of the Holy Spirit (as we are taught by the Apostle), it is certainly not to be imagined that God wished to choose a residence for Himself in an unworthy place. Therefore, in the consideration of this subject and in the investigation of a secret matter of such great importance, we have need to proceed with our most exact discretion and judgment from the visible things in man to his invisible things. That is to say, we must penetrate into the marrow of his secret, mystical, and internal existence with the sharper edge of our intellect by way of **demonstration from effects** <note>original: "demonstrationis à posteriori"; a method of reasoning that works backward from observed effects to their causes.</note>, namely from the external man. Wherefore we proceed in this manner: Since man is—not without justice—handed down by **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary sage to whom the Hermetic corpus is attributed.</note> as being the "son of the world," just as he called the world itself the "son of God," insofar as it is fabricated in the image of the **Archetype** <note>The original model or divine blueprint of the universe.</note>; and for that reason he is called the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: from the Greek "mikros kosmos," meaning "little world"; the idea that man contains the entire universe within himself.</term>; it will be worthwhile to understand that he himself also, in the manner of the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm: the "great world" or the universe as a whole.</term>, is divided into heaven and earth. Consequently, he includes within himself his own circles, heavens, poles, and stars in a proportion fitting to him, no differently than the Macrocosm does. And also, as we find, the spiritual icons of the heavens with their circles and poles are even delineated upon the earth of the Macrocosm and in every particle of it—just as one may see in the **Magnet** and in iron. In this very way, the character of the internal man is delineated and expressed in the external man: no differently than we are able to judge the shape of a sword from the proportion of its scabbard, or the form of a kernel from its shell.

Regarding the discovery of the worldly poles within man, no small controversy has arisen among the Philosophers. **Plato**, **Pythagoras**, and **Aristotle** assigned the right hand of man to the eastern region; their reasoning was that the daily motion of the heavens, which proceeds from the "first mover," is carried out from the east to the west. Therefore, by this reasoning of theirs, the western region must correspond to the left side, and in arranging a man according to that position, his face must look toward the North, and his back toward the South. **Empedocles** seems to oppose this opinion, asserting that the Summer Solstice, or the **Tropic of Cancer**, is assigned to the right part of the world; it then follows that the station of the winter sun, or the **Tropic of Capricorn**, is dedicated to the left, and according to that direction, the human face must look toward the West. But the sentiment of my mind is entirely opposed to these opinions of theirs: because I am persuaded, both by theological reasons and those collected from the Sacred Scriptures, that the human face ought to be matched by its natural position to the rising of the sun, or the eastern region. Then his back will look toward the West, and consequently his left hand will indicate the **North Pole**, just as the right will indicate the South. This position is proved first by sacred testimony: for the Patri-

<column-break/>

-archs, Prophets, and Apostles, in their greater devotion, turned their faces toward the East. This was indeed an argument that that region of the world was divinely dedicated to the front part of man. <margin>Matthew 24</margin> Furthermore, we read in the Gospel that the lightning comes out of the East and passes into the West. <margin>Numbers 35</margin> And elsewhere it is said: "Measure out toward the Eastern region, and toward the Southern region, and toward the Western region, and toward the Northern region, etc." It is as if he had said: "Measure the fields in front of you, and to your right, and behind your backs, and to your left." <margin>Job 23:8</margin> And in Job we find: "If I go to the East, he will not appear; if to the West, I shall not perceive him; if to the left, what shall I do? I shall not lay hold of him; if I turn myself to the right, I shall not see him." Or, as **Fransiscus Vatablus** and **Santes Pagninus** <note>Two influential 16th-century biblical scholars and translators.</note> interpret it: "If I turn myself to the North while he is working, I will still not see him; he hides himself in the South, and I shall not see him." But **Tremellius** <note>Immanuel Tremellius, a Jewish convert and leading Hebraist of the Reformation.</note> interprets it thus: "Behold, if I go forward, he will not be there; but if backward, I shall not notice him; when he acts on the left, I still will not see him; he will cover the right region, nor yet will I look upon him, etc." Thus, while Pagninus makes the East the "corner of the world," Tremellius calls it the "face" or "front part" of the world, etc. 

From this, without further controversy, I believe it will appear that the direct arrangement of man according to the situation of the greater world is such that his face is matched to the eastern corner of the earth. For this reason, his two eyes (and those of other creatures) are arranged in the frontispiece of his structure, so that after the long shadows of the night, they might look upon the Eastern sun with delight and desire, so that in its presence they might richly adore the Creator dwelling within it. In the sun's golden aspect is the power to expel the dominion of the dark night, and consequently to greet it as a type of the eternal and invisible sun, who also (as the Scriptures teach us) will appear from the east on the last day to renew and purify the corruptible world with fire. It follows, therefore, that the right part of man must look toward the South, just as his left portion looks toward the North. This whole matter appears all the more certain the more it agrees with philosophical reasoning: for the **liver** <note>original: "hepar"</note>, having its position in the right region of the body, commonly seems to **sympathize** with the Southern nature, insofar as by its own power it generates airy and hot blood, and sends it out through the venous channels everywhere into the earth of the Microcosm, so that it may thrive by means of it. This is no different than how the Southern wind produces warm and moist rains to irrigate the earth of the Macrocosm, so that from this the plants and herbs which grow upon the earth may be nourished, increased, and multiplied abundantly. Though he acts on the left, yet I shall not see him; he covers the right region, and yet I shall not look," etc. Thus, where Pagninus makes "East" a corner of the world, Tremellius calls it the "face" or the "front part" of the world. 

Whence, without further controversy, I believe it will appear that the direct arrangement of man according to the situation of the greater world is such that his face is adapted to the eastern corner of the earth. For this reason, his two eyes (and those of other creatures) are arranged in the frontispiece <note>The forehead or front face.</note> of his structure so that, after the long shadows of the night, they might look upon the Eastern sun with delight and desire, so that in its presence they might adore the Creator dwelling richly within it. In the sun's golden aspect is the power to expel the dominion of the dark night; consequently, they greet it as a type of the eternal and invisible sun, who also (as the scriptures teach us) will appear from the east on the last day to renew and purify the corruptible world by fire. It follows, therefore, that the right part of man must look toward the South, just as his left portion looks toward the north. All of this appears even more certain because it agrees with Philosophical reason: For the <term>liver</term> <note>original: "hepar"</note>, having its position in the right region of the body, seems to sympathize commonly with the Southern nature, insofar as by its own virtue it generates airy and warm blood, and sends it out through the venous channels everywhere into the earth of the Microcosm (the body) so that it may thrive by its means. This is no different than how the South wind produces warm and moist rains to irrigate the macrocosmic earth, so that plants and herbs which grow upon the earth may be nourished, increased, and multiplied abundantly. The left portion of the human body, however, not unsuitably...

...can be most fittingly referred to the Northern region of the world or the **Arctic pole**. For, just as in that corner [of the world] the air, water, and earth are exceedingly cold and dry, apt for freezing, and of a stinging and contracting or restrictive condition; so too do we find that the **spleen**, whose position is in the left part of the body, is the receptacle of **Melancholy**, or of cold, thick, acidic, and earthy humors. Similarly, just as the **Boreal winds** <note>The North winds.</note> of the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> are usually seen to darken and hide the most beautiful Solar light, and by this reason provide darkness and obscurity to our Hemisphere: So also in the <term>microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," meaning the human being.</note>, the windiness and vapors exhaled from the spleen are observed to contract the ventricles of the heart. In place of good, bright, and pious passions—such as gladness and joy, love, charity, hope, and so on—they usually produce wicked and dark passions or disturbances, such as sadness, fear, despair, and others of this kind, and they cause the heart to suffer syncopetic <note>original: "affectus syncopeticos"; referring to "syncope" or fainting, here meaning a sudden weakening or "sinking" of the heart's vital force.</note> affections. 

Thus, it is right to choose two opposite poles in the microcosm which exactly concur in effect with those in the macrocosm, by numbering the Southern pole from the Equinoctial. For if we divide a **Magnet** in the middle, between its two poles, that equinoctial part which is closest to the Arctic pole will serve and remain in the place of the Southern pole. And again, if that half is divided at the location of the Tropic of Cancer, that division near the Tropic will be the Southern pole. 

But, so that we may look even more intrinsically into the lesser world, we shall surely find that it is built upon that spiritual **Cornerstone** <note>original: "lapidem Angularem"; a reference to Christ as the foundation of creation.</note> by which the greater world was made, and its earth sustained. Consequently, in that Spiritual stone, the world and every particle of it was ideally delineated from the beginning, before it was formed into the image of the earth, which is said to be full of the spirit of wisdom. Hence, therefore, man (or the microcosm) is called the **Temple of God**, the body and members of Christ, and the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, as was related before. For this cause, it must be believed that there are secret poles, circles, and stars—as much Spiritual as corporal—assigned to the human composition. This is no different than how we find them exactly and without any risk of doubt in the earth and in every magnetic portion of it: so that in man there are the properties of the Winds of the Macrocosm, and consequently passions can be procreated in him, and produced from him, which are as much antipathetic as sympathetic.

Now, if in the second place we consider the nature of the Magnet in a due manner and with diligence, we shall be seized with no small admiration in the observation of its properties:

<column-break/>

Indeed, we shall find that it almost exceeds human grasp and reason that a mineral stone, however deaf, immobile, and stupid, should nevertheless possess such **Spirits**. These spirits insensibly penetrate through the hardest rocks, the firmest woods, and the most solid metals—which are not breathable according to human conception—indeed, even through glass, which is nearly impenetrable, and other such compact substances that have no sensible breathing-holes or porosities. It can work upon itself and upon iron, and it can gaze so constantly at the Arctic pole at such a remote distance (scarcely imaginable to us), namely from the earth all the way to the eighth heaven where the pole star is—a length that is almost incommensurable. 

I dare to boldly pronounce that the entire school of the **Peripatetics** <note>The followers of Aristotle, who sought to explain nature through purely physical and logical categories.</note>, which professes to give a reason for every thing and to know all that pertains to the nature of the most hidden and intimate secrets, will find itself greatly disturbed and entangled in a labyrinth of fantastic imagination and Chimera <note>A mythical monster made of disparate parts; here used to mean a wild, illogical delusion.</note>, before it can discuss this cloudy business or penetrate to the guts of so profound a riddle—that is, before it can reach the desired goal of this inquiry. For it is judged by the finger of a truer and more Divine Philosophy than that of the Heathens, the origin and formal principle of whose entire action and virtue is that **Universal Cornerstone, Jesus Christ**, in whom is the fullness of divinity, as the Apostle teaches us. 

Is it not a thing worthy of admiration that this Magnetic spirit is accustomed to pass through and penetrate just like the celestial human spirit, even where air is denied entry? Is it not an evident argument that it is of celestial progeny, since such effects are produced notwithstanding the solid bodies interposed between it and the iron? Therefore, let **Plutarch** <note>A famous Greek historian and philosopher (c. 46 – 120 AD).</note> not boast and glory so triumphantly as he did in that place where he attempts to untie that intricate **Gordian knot**, regarding it as a disgrace and a defect in learned Philosophers that, though versed in such a mystery, they have not dived into its depths; for he himself finally reveals a great error in his own strict inquiry. Indeed, his conclusion is that the insensible emanations or emissions or effluxions which come out of the Magnet and produce such attractive effects are "gross and windy." But if he had considered this business with a slightly more mature judgment, then he would have perceived that even the most subtle and exceedingly rare air cannot find any way or porosity through flat woods or wooden tablets, polished stones, or plates of silver or gold; and much less could "gross and windy" spirits...

# CHAPTER IV. #

-> On the double attractive disposition in man, one of which agrees with the nature of the *Magnet*, while the other differs from it; in this chapter also, the reason why the corpse of a dead man is endowed with *Magnetic* or attractive power is clearly explained. <-

Just as in the measurement of the *Magnet* multiple species or modes of attracting are observed (for its attractive faculty is affected differently around its poles—namely, perpendicularly—than at its equator, which draws iron to itself in a prone and prostrate manner), so also is a great difference found between the effects of that attractive power found in man. For the <term>spleen</term> <note>original: "lien"; in early medicine, the spleen was thought to govern the "melancholic" humor.</note>, having the nature and property of the Northern Pole, directly attracts its like—namely, Melancholic and earthy juices—by a power that is, as it were, Saturnine <note>Referring to the planet Saturn, traditionally associated with coldness, weight, and melancholy.</note>. But the <term>gall bladder</term> <note>original: "cysta fellis".</note> receives its faculty of attracting from a Martial <note>Referring to Mars, the planet of fire and war.</note>, Sulphurous property or fiery earthiness; and the <term>liver</term> <note>original: "hepar".</note>, through a southern or equinoctial expansion, disperses and pours out the blood (which it previously made red) through the whole **Microcosmic** earth <note>The human body.</note> by means of the venous channels. But in the first place, through porous organs, it attracts the chylous <note>The "chyle" is the milky fluid of digested food.</note> substance of food from the intestines. It would never exercise all these faculties of attracting and expanding unless it were animated for that work by the incitements of <term>natural heat</term> <note>The vital warmth thought to be the engine of life in pre-modern medicine.</note>.

And although that heat, by its nature, dissipates more by expanding than it contracts by attracting, it nevertheless incites and animates certain bodily instruments which are ordained by nature to perform such work—namely, to suck and draw to themselves through contraction, and again to dilate through relaxation. For this reason, the Heart, Stomach, intestines, veins, etc., are formed and compacted from direct fibers for the sake of attraction, transverse fibers for the sake of retention, and oblique fibers for the sake of expulsion. 

Again, the attraction of air through the windpipe and nostrils could not be completed without the help and aid of the lungs, which could by no means work or move without the animation and incitement of expanding and vivifying heat. Thus, in this case, all attraction of external air—which occurs through pores into the fleshy parts, and through the lungs into the Left Chamber of the heart—proceeds immediately from the dilative action of natural heat and is completed by means of the instruments, especially the lungs and heart. It is just as we see a <term>Syringe</term> <note>original: "Syringam"; here used as an analogy for a mechanical pump.</note> or tube: if its internal part is pulled out, it draws a little air or water to itself; but if that internal part is pushed back, it again emits or expels the air or water introduced by attraction.

<column-break/>

Yet both these opposite natures in a single instrument proceed from a single operating human Spirit. We must therefore understand (as said before) that man is composed of matter, which is his "patient" <note>The passive element acted upon.</note>, and form, which is his "agent" <note>The active force.</note>. And as matter previously proceeded from the watery subject of the dark abyss emerging from chaos, it is therefore of itself prone to a Northern and privative disposition—namely, rest, cold, mortification, and immobility. Indeed, it is this matter that causes contraction both in the heart (and consequently in the motion of the pulses) and in other parts of the body; that is, the natural inclination of matter in man is to contract the Spirits from the circumference to the center. 

Conversely, the "form," which is derived from light, is occupied in expansion and therefore in the animation and agitation of matter, which without such an agent would remain sluggish and as if dead from the Northern cold of its mother. And this is the reason for <term>Systole</term> <note>The contraction of the heart.</note> and <term>Diastole</term> <note>The expansion of the heart.</note> in the motion of the heart, which arises from that action and passion—or operation and resistance—which occurs between the light, heat, or equinoctial form, and the dark, cold, or polar matter in the human composition. 

Hence it is evident that just as the <term>greater world</term> <note>The "mundus major" or universe.</note> is said to be forged from strife and friendship, so also the <term>lesser world</term> <note>The "mundus minor" or man.</note> is not unjustly said to be composed of contraries—namely, from the offspring of light and that of darkness. Now, in this, the attractive faculty of a living man seems to differ from that of a *Magnet*: because a *Magnet* does not appear to human sense to be as alive and agile as a man, but seems in a certain way dead, insofar as it is divided from its ferruginous <note>Iron-bearing.</note> vein. 

Furthermore, the magnet itself [attracts] not by an evident expansion proceeding from vivifying heat through an organic substance, but by a contractive power, partly earthy and partly central, which first sent out its rays by expansion and only then contracted by drawing them back to itself. For this reason, its greatest power of attracting consists in the pole. But the attraction of a living man proceeds from the expansion of vivifying heat from the center toward the circumference, which causes the material instruments to perform their duties for attraction as well as retention and expulsion. Sometimes it operates chiefly toward contraction—that is, it moves from the circumference toward the center—namely, by the divine will of a privative emanation... <note>The text cuts off here, continuing the thought that life or light is being withdrawn.</note>

...receives the rays: Just as when the heart contracts, from which it happens that wicked passions—such as sadness, melancholy, envy, despair, fear, etc.—arise, concerning which we have previously reported. Sometimes also the native heat <note>original: "calor nativus"; the innate warmth believed by ancient physicians to be the source of life.</note> reflects its rays internally toward the rest of the solar senses, as can be seen in the act of sleep, which is the image of death and darkness. But in truth, it dilates itself from the center to the circumference when it wishes for the <term>animal spirits</term> <note>original: "Spiritus animales"; not "animal" in the modern sense, but referring to the "anima" or soul—the subtle fluids that were thought to carry instructions from the brain to the muscles.</note> to be awake and active.

By these things, therefore, we can imagine that the attractive faculty of the **Magnet** is first from the outside to the circumference, and from there to the center, in such a way, however, that the bodily matter of the desired Spirit is retained by the retaining Spirit and by the center contracting at the circumference, as can be seen in iron attracted by a **Magnet**, and straw by <term>Amber</term> <note>original: "Carabe"; an old term for amber, which exhibits static electricity when rubbed.</note>. For that is the reason for a like thing to attract its like to itself in iron and steel—which iron substance, regarding its purification from heterogeneous stony Mercury and the homogeneity of its now purified nature, is compared to a living man, who is animated by his own expanding living spirits. For I would wish everyone to understand that there is no creature on earth that does not have its own **Astrological** or stellar influence; which (although we may not know how to discern it with our eyes) shines forth, and does not make its "aspect" <note>An astrological term for the relative positions of stars/planets.</note> except toward those species similar to itself—namely, toward such creatures that share the condition of the stars whose influences distill upon them. But if two creatures are mutually discordant and contrary in nature, then one of them, in an *Antipathetical* <note>original: "Antipathetico"; a natural repulsion, the opposite of "Sympathy."</note> manner, will turn away and reflect its rays from the other. Therefore, *Iron*, meeting the Magnet like a vivifying male, very easily emits the rays of its love to it; the Magnet, by the power of its internal *Martial* spirits <note>referring to Mars, the planet associated with iron.</note>, attracts and introduces those rays so greedily to its own center. And by this attraction of the formal rays of the iron, it also carries and leads the body of the iron along with it, as long as it possesses stellar or *Martial* influences. In a similar respect—namely, of concupiscible appetite—the Magnet, strong in virtue, can be held in the place of a female toward the weaker, namely, that in which there is not such a great appetite. Nor does the matter stand differently with a living man and the corpse of another: For although many bodies seem to be dead, nevertheless the *Natural Magician* <note>original: "Magus Naturalis"; a scientist who studies the hidden, "occult" forces of nature like magnetism.</note> understands that in its flesh and bones, and even its blood, there lurk wonderful spirits that can perform miracles no less—indeed, even greater—than those of the Magnet. And for that reason, I would wish that anyone who is perverse regarding the Mysteries of God in the nature of the creature, and too blinded by his own imagination, should be better instructed by experience before he asserts with such audacity and without hesitation that there are no spirits in the amputated members of a man, nor in the corpse of a dead man—indeed, they even think the Devil himself can confer nothing of 

<column-break/>

spirits upon them. For I warn such bold and rash judges to know that, just as the Magnet (though it appears to the eyes as a dead mass) is observed to suck in and allure radiant spirits centrally with a living appetite along with the body of another Magnet—and the whole Magnet, and any portion of it divided from the whole, will perform this same thing according to its proportion—so also I can prove and confirm by ocular demonstration that by the proper application of flesh taken from some member of a corpse to the flesh of a living man for several hours, the man to whom it is applied will be rendered weak and feeble. And yet, shortly after the removal of that bodily Magnetic <term>Mummy</term> <note>original: "Mummiæ"; in Hermetic medicine, "mummy" refers to the vital essence or "balsam" remaining in a body after death, used in sympathetic cures.</note>, he will recover his former strength. But, lest this report of mine seem a figment to adversaries (insofar as they can allege that the application of such things might work more in the imagination of the living man than in his body, and that he persuades himself he is weak without a true foundation, and that no external effect can be produced that could prove this), I respond that this application is of such great efficacy that it is observed to extract the Spiritual mummy in a visible form. For by reason of the coldness of the exterior member, the mummy extracted on the surface of the Magnetic body will be condensed, not otherwise than air into a cloud or a cloud into snow. Thus, it can be collected and reduced into a kind of *Panacea* <note>A universal remedy.</note>, provided that the person from whom it is extracted is of a sound complexion and healthy in his body; on the other hand, it must be held as a corruptible and *Antipathetical* medicine where the body is infected by some poisonous or contagious disease, such as the <term>French disease</term> <note>original: "morbo gallico"; Syphilis.</note>, leprosy, and similar things, as will be explained more clearly below. Now, the reason for this act or operation in the Magnetic part of a dead man is that, whereas when the body was alive it was animated by active, bright rays and enjoyed all the properties of that vivifying light (for it was active, mobile, dilating, and finally of an equinoctial or Southern condition), the blood, once the natural heat is extinguished, takes on the property of darkness. For it is mortified by cold, congealed, and its act is rendered potential (that is, immobile and contracting), and (to put it in a word) of the nature of the *frozen zone and the cold pole*. So much so that, where previously while in life it emitted its rays from the center to the circumference and enjoyed the blessings of the vivifying and positive emanation of God, it now, in the appearance of death, takes on the contracting, privative, and mortifying condition and emanation of the Divine property. And yet, nonetheless, I would not want wise men to think that because a living body is converted into a dead corpse, it is therefore entirely void of vital Spirits, since they have it confirmed by the Holy Scriptures,

### SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part II. ###

<margin>Wisdom 12:1 <note>original: "Sap. 12. 1."; a reference to the Wisdom of Solomon: "For thine incorruptible Spirit is in all things."</note></margin>The incorruptible Spirit of God exists in all things, and consequently in the dead as much as in the living. For this incorruptible spirit, according to its property within the four winds, is sometimes in motion from the center of a thing toward its circumference. Through this activity, it gives life to a creature and causes it to act and live by its <term>equinoctial</term> <note>original: "æquinoctiali"; here referring to a balanced or active state</note> or southern faculty. In this way, we are said to live, move, and have our being in God. This spirit moves, I say, in its particular property from the center of the celestial Sun to the animation of all lower creatures—namely, by calling forth their own incorruptible spirits, which have been driven back to the center by the cold of winter, and drawing them from the center back to their circumference. We can see this in vegetables, which appear dead during the winter; this is because the power of the spirit leaves their circumference and hides itself in the center, a place more remote from the assaults of the cold, where it seems to rest. But truly, when this spirit perceives and feels the approach of the "luminous fountain" <note>the Sun</note>, whose rays provide comfort and aid, it begins little by little to emerge from its central palace. It yearns to visit the circumference of the plant once more, and, united with the celestial rays sent down from above to help, it attempts with all its strength to expel the dark deprivation and freezing cold from its tabernacle, so that it may proceed more freely to the act of growth and multiplication. This is clearly seen in wheat buried or sown in the earth. In no different a way, I say, is the nature of the **Martial Magnet** <note>original: "Magnetis Martialis"; "Martial" refers to Iron, governed by the planet Mars</note> stirred and incited when its **Saturnine spirit** <note>original: "ſpiritu Saturnino"; referring to the principle of cold, contraction, and lead</note>—originally contracted into its center—flees with equal joy toward the formal rays of iron, from whose **Sulphurous Martial spirit** those rays originally gushed forth. In just such a way, the spirit of a **Corpse**, forced from the circumference to the center by the mortifying cold and remaining there in rest and without action, renders the body and every part of it fixed and immobile. But indeed, when it faces or is applied to the circumference of its own living species, it then arises from its center to the circumference (as if it were being oppressed by hunger while in the center). With a greedy appetite, it draws toward its center the "Spiritual Mummy" <note>original: "Mummiâ Spirituali"; the vital essence or "balsam" believed to reside in the body</note> of a living man—which dilates itself and darts out through the pores in a radiant manner to bring help—so that the corpse may be clothed in the life it lived before and be refreshed by that presence. But the oily spiritual mummy of a

<column-break/>

dead man, filled with light-spirits and thickened by the cold upon the surface of a living man, is suddenly congealed; it can then be reserved for private use. This cannot be better confirmed than by the example of the contracting, restricting, or congealing power of the smoky growth of salt contained in the bones of the dead. For by the application of that substance—namely, <term>Usnea</term> <note>original: "Vzneæ"; a lichen (specifically *Usnea cranii humani*) that grows on the skulls of those who died violently, highly prized in early modern medicine</note> or the moss growing upon the skulls of the dead—to a burst of blood in a living man, the warm blood in the living man moves backward, as if moved by an **Antipathetic** affection, and is denied an exit by the operation of this "Boreal" <note>northern/cold</note> congealing and astringent growth. 

But setting aside for a time such conclusions regarding the **Mummial Magnet** of a dead man and its virtues, what will you say if there is a **Microcosmic Magnet** that can be collected from a living man without any detriment to his life or body? Its virtues are revealed both in its natural and "monstrous" generation and birth—derived as it is from dissimilar parents and even from substances differing in species, much like a mule—namely, being compacted from earthy **Mercury** and the human spirits of **Choleric Sulphur**. It operates both by the spiritual attraction of the "Mummy" from a living man and also (which is even more wonderful) by its own transplantation into both animal and vegetable species in a strange and admirable way, working both **Sympathetically** and **Antipathetically**. 

Indeed, I know that these new things will immediately be reckoned as diabolical acts and illicit ways by those who are prone to unjust and unfair judgment, insofar as these things exceed the sphere of their capacity. And yet, I understand for a certainty that they are true, and have been experienced by several people, not without the wonder of many. Indeed, we are not ignorant of this **Microcosmic Magnet** nor its use. When its acts and the effects of those acts are proven by wise men, they will appear quite natural; however much their effects, even when well-pondered, may seem at first glance wonderful, foreign to human capacity, and exceedingly obscure. But truly, if those things which I have previously recited are rightly understood and seriously weighed, their cause will not appear so obscure as to exceed the limits of nature. Concerning the action of this Microcosmic Magnet—both sympathetic and antipathetic—I have proposed, God willing, to discourse more in the following pages, namely in the last book of this work.

### CHAPTER V.

->*In this chapter is explained the secret cause why, and the manner how, the Magnet—both the Microcosmic <note>the human "small world"</note> and the Macrocosmic <note>the universe or "great world"</note>—is accustomed to operate at an instance; indeed, even across an unknown dimension or an indeterminate interval.*<-

Foster, in a certain book of his titled *The Sponge to Wipe Away the Weapon-Salve* <note>original: "Hoplocrisma spongus"; a 1631 treatise by William Foster attacking Fludd's belief in magnetic healing</note>, more than sufficiently expressed the thinness of his own Philosophy therein. He claims that since the lights of the Sun and stars cannot penetrate dark clouds or opaque bodies, the formal essence of man is therefore unable, in its motion or course, to move toward some distant goal without the hindrance or opposition of mountains, castles, groves, and the like. 

But, if he had immersed himself a little more deeply into the vitals of true Philosophy, he would then undoubtedly recognize that the "ethereal sperm" <note>original: "sperma æthereum"; the celestial seed or life-force</note>, or stellar influences, are in their condition much subtler than are the vehicles of visible light. Indeed, they are refined, exactly spiritual, and remarkably mobile; they are so penetrating and alive that they are powerful enough to—and indeed perpetually do—penetrate to the very vitals or center of the earth without any manifest obstacle or resistance, and there they generate metals of all species according to the condition of the influence. 

All Philosophers, both ancient and modern, bear witness to this fact. Plotinus, following the mind of Plato, seems to explain the subtlety of this Spirit in these words: "So great is the thinness of the Ether, that it penetrates all bodies of the universe, both above and below; and being joined or folded in with them, it does not make them larger in the least, because that interior spirit nourishes and preserves all their works with a very small mass, receiving no increase at all." <note>original: "Tanta est Ætheris tenuitas..."</note> 

And by reason of the purity and subtlety of this celestial nature, the heaven is called by mystic Philosophers and Poets the husband or spouse of the earth (whom they called Vesta). Indeed, the very stars of heaven—among whose ranks the Copernicans count the earth—are likened to the wives of heaven; for they are drawn out from it in no other way than Eve was from the side of Adam. For they define stars to be the denser parts of their own orbs, whence it happens that they are considered the members of heaven. 

There is nothing so thin, subtle, and penetrating as that spirit from which reason itself comes. This is why the true Alchemists tell so many wonderful things about their "Heaven," which they also call the *quinta essentia* <note>the "Fifth Essence" or quintessence, a refined substance beyond the four elements</note>; they argue that by reason of its purity and subtlety, it can penetrate all things. And the Philosophers say that this Fifth Essence is that nature of theirs which they define as a certain infinite power in things, permeating all beings, generating them all, and increasing and nourishing them, and

<column-break/>

<margin>Job. Psalm. 2 Peter 3. Wisdom 12:1. Wisdom 7. Wisdom 1.</margin>
procreating like from like. 

And certainly, if anyone wishes to consider realistically those things I have previously alleged, he will remember me saying that the Angelic virtues flow from the archetypal emanation, and are types of the Divine Ideas; and also that the ethereal spirit is filled with Angelic influences, which have their essential root from God and in God. Thus, in truth, it is not the stellar Light which penetrates so deeply or operates so universally, but that eternal, most central Spirit, which by its divine and irresistible essence penetrates and permeates through all things, both in the heaven above and in the earth and waters below. 

All of this seems to be confirmed by the Mystic Philosophers (albeit obscurely) when they call Saturn—who was the Father of Jupiter, or the head, or the <term>Cheter</term> <note>original: "Cheter"; the Hebrew "Kether" or "Crown," the highest Sephirah in Kabbalah</note> of the universal emanation—the father of heaven and earth. From this they argue that in the emission of the spirit of wisdom, He created and informed the heavens, according to that passage in Job: "By your Spirit you have adorned the heavens." <note>original: "Cœlum ornasti Spiritu tuo."</note> And David: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their power by the spirit from his mouth." And Saint Peter has it: "The heavens were of old, and the earth consisting of waters and through waters by the word of God." 

It is certain, therefore, that the entire essential act in the ethereal spirit is the act of divine emanation, or the "bright incorruptible spirit of God," to use the words of Solomon. And therefore it necessarily follows that this Spirit—which deserves to be the immediate vehicle of such an irresistible and most powerful influence—must be conformable to that very nature in purity and subtlety which informed it. This Spirit is said by Solomon to be more mobile and subtle than any thing, and to reach everywhere because of its cleanness, and to renew all things and fill the round world. 

This, then, was what compelled some even among the Christian Philosophers to break out into this speech: "God is nature, and nature is God." <note>original: "Deus est natura, & natura; Deus."</note> By this they seem to mean that "naturing nature" <note>original: "natura naturata" (likely a typo in OCR for "naturans")</note> which radically informs, was that eternal emanation which made and informed the "moist nature" of the world; for this reason the world is called "natured nature" <note>original: "natura naturata"</note>—namely, by the presence of that "naturing nature" itself, or the Divine Spirit of God, which moved over the waters. It imparted a fiery vigor or virtue, as can be seen partly by the testimony of Holy Scripture and partly by the assertion of Saint Augustine. It is necessary, therefore, that we [give] these things their due...
