### SECTION II, BOOK II. Part II.

...with the consideration of the things we have alleged, we know that if the <term>influence</term> <note>the flow of spiritual power from the heavens</note> is fully animated by the incorruptible spirit of the Lord, then it must necessarily be imbued with the properties of that Divine spirit's nature. Consequently, it must be the most subtle, agile, mobile, and penetrating of all spirits. In that respect, it will be more powerful in penetrating all solid things without any hindrance or resistance, and also better suited and prepared for generating, increasing, and nourishing all things. And if it is incorporated or specified into a body, it is accustomed to procreate similar individuals from similar ones. Furthermore, in respect to human capacity, it has an infinite extension in the emission of its rays; therefore, it is impossible for it to be limited.

I shall demonstrate all of this through experience or ocular demonstration of this kind. We find in the practice of magnetism that the <term>Magnet</term> <note>original: "Magnetem"; here referring to the lodestone but also the spiritual principle of attraction</note>, by the power of its subtle Spirit which animates it internally and centrally, is rendered so powerful in its attractive virtue that it can transmit the rays of its activity through the hardest stones, thick wood, the most compact metals, and even through glass (which is almost impenetrable) without any resistance. This is the most evident proof that this spirit is of a nature far more penetrating and subtle than the <term>sublunary air</term> <note>the common air below the moon</note>, insofar as the air is denied passage even through a thin piece of paper or a small skin. 

By the same reasoning, the internal celestial spirit of man—which is the vehicle for that vivifying ray—is so subtle in itself that nothing can resist it when the internal mental ray aims at any goal, however remote from the man or inaccessible to human capacity. For, since that celestial spirit in man is formed according to the pattern of the Divine Spirit, it is necessary that he should not limit it in such an action. Now, the subtlety of the Divine act in the human spirit is expressed by <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermetic philosophy</note> in this way:

<margin>Pimander, 4.</margin>
> Whoever is supported by this nature of God, they embrace within their intelligence all things that are on the earth and in the sea, and whatever else is above the heaven; and they raise themselves up so far that they even behold the Good itself, etc.

By these words, he seems to mean that every sufficient act of God in its penetration and migration through all things consists in the mental ray. Because this act is not resisted, celestial influences penetrate and work everywhere on the earth and in the sea without any resistance or intermediate hindrance. From these things, therefore, it is evident that just as every lower specific creature is endowed with this essential spirit and consists in it—and builds upon it as the real foundation of its truth or its true cornerstone—so also the emission of its rays is not to be terminated by any "sphere of activity," as certain

<column-break/>

indiscrete philosophers (who are more sensual than intellectual) have not blushed to assert. Since, as a crowd of the wisest philosophers testifies, that spirit is defined as an infinite force in things, and consequently it is not defined or determined. For, as far as the celestial star itself emits the rays of its activity from its center, so far can that central spirit on earth and in its creatures extend the diameter of its own emanation. 

Thus, just as the radiant influence of a celestial star penetrates downward even to the center of the earth, in exactly the same way every "terrestrial star" <note>Fludd’s term for the spiritual essence within a creature</note> penetrates by ascending up to the center of its own celestial star from which it was radically derived. The more opulent, rich, and highly exalted that stellar form is in a creature, the more closely it approaches the nature of a more worthy and hidden star in heaven; and consequently, it makes the extension of its rays (or the semi-diameter of its emission) longer and stronger. 

Now indeed, we see every astral influence in a creature looking toward its celestial source (the star from which it first arose) by a certain natural instinct and in a **sympathetic** manner. Likewise, we see that celestial star, with a kind of paternal regard, emitting its influences downward to its earthly son (to cherish and nourish its "filial form" or fire within the creature), so much so that both seem to rejoice mutually in each other and receive each other in a reciprocal embrace, according to that saying of the Philosophers: **Nature rejoices in nature and nature contains nature.** **O celestial nature of truth, mutually multiplying the natures of God!** 

So also the species of creatures, which are clothed in one and the same influence, are accustomed (by reason of their similarity to each other) to ejaculate sympathetic rays—that is, rays consenting by nature—with which they meet in concord and love. And for this reason, the axiom of the Philosophers previously alleged is this: **Nature is accustomed to procreate from likes.** And this is the reason why every specific form is observed to rejoice in its like, and to procreate its like without overstepping the limits of its species. For example, human nature produces a human, equine nature a horse; fennel seed produces fennel, a bean a bean, a grain of wheat produces wheat, and so on. 

Furthermore, the nature of a thing so created is most friendly to its like, and emits lovely rays of sympathy so that they may meet and concur with the rays emitted by its like, so that both natures may agree and mutually embrace. This can be seen in the <term>Magnet</term> with the <term>Magnet</term>, and the <term>Magnet</term> with iron. For if one magnet finds or encounters another, both will look upon each other by the virtue of the **Saturnine Sulphurous Spirit** <note>In Fludd’s alchemy, a "Saturnine" spirit refers to a heavy, contractive, or magnetic force associated with the planet Saturn</note> and will mutually embrace each other. For by their proper application to one another, and by the emission of rays from the center to the cir-

This is also observed between iron and the <term>Magnet</term> <note>original: "Magnetem"; referring both to the physical lodestone and the spiritual principle of attraction</note>. For, since iron is subject to the same constellation as the Magnet and enjoys its own central star, which corresponds to that of the Magnet in every respect—for because of that essential kinship <note>original: "consanguinitatem," literally "blood-relationship"</note>, they are always found in the same mine or terrestrial vein—they are therefore observed to love one another and receive each other with such great appetite. For we are taught by experience that the female stone <note>the lodestone</note>, quite like a lustful harlot, attracts and desires the male iron; and it is not the other way around, as <term>Averroes</term> <note>a 12th-century Islamic philosopher</note>, <term>Scaliger</term> <note>a Renaissance polymath</note>, and <term>Cardinal Cusanus</term> <note>a 15th-century mystic and mathematician</note> erroneously and falsely believe. Indeed, it is their opinion that the iron itself draws the Magnet to it as if to its origin and womb, from which it arose. For by this reasoning, the North Pole in the Magnet would move by itself and by its own proper inclination more quickly toward the <term>Pole Star</term> <note>the North Star, Polaris</note>—which is the source of the central influences of both—than the Magnet itself would. But all of this is proven false by experience.

Now, however, to confirm the infinite efficacy of these central rays in these two bodies (namely, the Pole Star and the Magnet or iron), it is necessary that we first be led by a suitable theory, so that we may afterward descend into practice with an easier method. "A ray," says Alkindus <margin>Alkindus, *On Stellar Rays*</margin> <note>Al-Kindi was a 9th-century philosopher who wrote on the mathematical power of starlight</note>, "which proceeds from the center of a star to the center of the earth, is proven to be strongest in the operation of its species," etc. By which he seems to argue that the hidden ray or radiant influence of a star operates and acts at an immeasurable distance, even within its image or likeness on earth. For elsewhere he says this: "It is clear that stellar rays constitute diverse individuals in this world," etc. Again, regarding the central stars or stellar influences of inferior bodies and their radiant extensions, he says elsewhere: "The <term>Elemental World</term> <note>the physical world of the four elements</note> is an image of the Sidereal World <note>the world of the stars</note>, so that whatever thing is contained in it contains the likeness of that world itself; it is manifest that every thing in this world produces rays in its own way, after the likeness of the Stars, otherwise it would not fully possess the form of the Sidereal World; but this is also manifested gradually in some things." For fire transmits rays of heat to nearby places, and the earth transmits rays of cold. Therefore, assuming this as true, we say that everything which has actual existence in the world of Elements emits rays in every direction, which fill the entire Elemental world in their own way. Furthermore, the distance of one thing from another makes a difference in the effect of the rays in the things of this world. Thus he spoke. By this speech, he makes us more certain: First, that there is nothing in the lower world which does not have its likeness in that upper world from which it receives...

<column-break/>

...rays and influence of its essence. And again, that just as that celestial star shoots its rays even to the center of the earth, and therefore has such a wide sphere of activity that it searches every portion of the entire concave world, so also those stellar sparks or radiant rays, which it emits to the creatures subject to it—since their stars are one and the same in substance and form with their source and consequently are continued with it, and not at all indivisible from it in spirit and light—search all the corners of the sublunary region. Nay, they even tend to penetrate back to their celestial source, from which they receive their power of life, as will be demonstrated below. This is indicated all the more clearly because any portion of a large Magnet, however small, claims its own distinct poles and circles, just like the large or whole one from which it was cut. By these things, then, it is made apparent that the action of any elemental thing is effected as much at a distance as when two bodies are joined together by mutual contact. 

But the action of elemental things, while they are separated from one another, is completed by a due application and the infusion of radiant influences into each other; this would seem scarcely credible because of the hidden nature of the action itself, were it not that experience teaches us this through the observation of the attraction of iron by the Magnet at a distance. Furthermore, we also notice that the images of things are discerned from afar in optical mirrors. Nor was it the least of the skills among the <term>Pythagoreans</term> <note>followers of the Greek philosopher Pythagoras</note> and some Christian Philosophers to express their minds or intentions to others living in distant places or regions far away, by means of reflections through mathematically prepared and arranged glasses onto the disk of the moon. 

But indeed, our "external" Philosophers <note>those who rely only on physical senses</note>, who wish to be governed by sense alone, dream of a certain determined sphere of activity, and they do not blush to assign limits to this spirit or "mythical nature." For example, because a Magnet attracts iron, for the most part, only at a distance of half a table or one <term>cubit</term> <note>about 18 inches</note>; therefore, they think and conclude that the vivifying act of its power cannot penetrate further or extend itself in the air. Consequently, led only by the eyes of the body and not of the intellect, they wish to terminate the spiritual extension of the Magnet by this external observation. But if they were willing to close the physical eyes of their inquiry and, in the manner of the most skilled Philosophers, look into the marrow of such an abstruse action with the mental light, they would perceive that the extension of the radiant Spirit in the Magnet is equal to the radius of its own celestial star, since both are of one and the same essence. And likewise, there is a similar spirit in iron and any portion of it, but there are many things which can hinder the evident effect in the Magnet;

By the same reasoning, we must grant that there is a similar sympathetic meeting of hidden rays between iron and the **Magnet**, since each of them possesses within itself "central Stars" <note>original: *Stellas centrales* — Fludd's term for the internal life-force or "spark" within matter</note> or radiant influences of one and the same nature or essence descending from a single source. Their hidden emanations travel to a distance unknown to us, even if their effects do not accidentally appear to us any more than those celestial influences which descend from heaven upon minerals, plants, and animals. 

Nevertheless, if we give any credit to histories and accounts, we have learned from **Serapion**, **Olaus Magnus**, and the **Moors** themselves that among the Indians, toward the North Pole, there are certain rocks of magnetic consistency that draw ships to them from a great distance. Indeed, so great is their power of attraction that they sometimes even pull iron nails out of the wooden structure of the ships, so that the sailors are forced to build their ships and boats with wooden pins instead of iron. 

And again, what should be said regarding the opinion of that most learned physician and philosopher **Fracastorius** <note>Girolamo Fracastoro (1478–1553), an Italian scholar who studied magnetism and contagion</note>? If this were true, it would follow that such magnetic rocks could operate from the equator to the frozen point of the North Pole. For we are taught by experience that sailors use the magnetic needle even as far as the equatorial line to explore the altitude at which they sail. 

Yet, although this will seem foreign and impossible to some, there are indeed those skilled in the geographic art and highly versed in the composition of sea charts who firmly adhere to this opinion of Fracastorius. Through them, it can be seen that the idea of a limited "sphere of activity" assigned to the Magnet's power by the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy</note> and Christian academics appears to be vain and of no consequence.

Good God, what a commotion the enemies or adversaries of the **weapon salve** <note>The "weapon salve" (*unguentum armarium*) was a controversial 17th-century medical treatment where the ointment was applied to the weapon that caused a wound rather than the wound itself, based on sympathetic magic.</note> would make at the sight of such a spectacle! That an unfeeling branch of a tree, divided into a fork at its end, could detect the seat of silver or gold metal, and consequently be able to penetrate 600 fathoms <note>original: *orgyas* — a Greek measure of length roughly equal to a fathom or the stretch of a man's arms</note> into the bowels of the earth by means of its invisible rays, even through crags and stony veins? Is this possible—that a vegetable nature, which is less active, mobile, and warm than an animal nature, could perform such an act? For they assert it is entirely impossible for a radiant influence or animal emanation to cooperate with its like at a remote distance because of the obstacles of castles, mountains, rocks, groves, mists, and the like. Without doubt, such superficial philosophers will conclude that this mystery is either not true at all, or if it is, then it cannot be performed without the work of the **Devil**. For since the animal spirit does not know how to complete a union of this kind at such a distance, is it probable that an unfeeling vegetable could perform this by itself and from its own inclination? Such, I know well, will be the judgment of those who are very ready to judge before the matter is understood as it truly is. In truth, there is a proportioned harmony in all lower creatures which corresponds to the celestial or rather Divine influences within them. These draw their origin from a single, primary, universal, and eternal emanation, which pours its rays—both essential and <term>sympathetic</term> as well as <term>antipathetic</term>—immediately into every stellar globe. And these globes likewise rain them down into the elemental world, creating through this communion a **Harmonic consensus** between these two regions. And therefore **Alkindus** <note>Al-Kindi (c. 801–873), an influential Arab philosopher and scientist known in the West for his work on the "stellar rays" that influence the earth.</note>
<margin>Al-Kindi on stellar rays.</margin>
says: All things that happen in this world and occur in the world of the elements are translated from the heavenly Harmony. It is certain, therefore, that the metallic rays meeting in their ascent with the radiant influences of the 

<column-break/>

I know it will seem strange to such men that a metallic substance should emit rays from its veins. But if they were as well-versed in the living natures of metals as those craftsmen who work in the mines of the mountains of Tyrol and Hungary, they would be made certain by ocular experience that metals sometimes emit lightning and thunder into the hollows of the earth. These are very dangerous to the workmen, so that unless they exit the mine immediately after the signs are given, or lie flat on the ground, they suffer the worst extremity. I received this from noble Germans worthy of trust, some of whom were eyewitnesses. But to proceed with our purpose, there is likewise among the lower creatures a certain **Antipathetic** aspect, just as there is among certain special stars of heaven, both wandering <note>planets</note> and fixed. One creature’s aspect is known to shrink from another’s, so that in the application of their rays, one is observed to turn away and reflect from the other with an angry, fearful, or hateful aversion.

# ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY. Fol. 118.

Rodiginus <note>Lodovicus Celius Rhodiginus (1461–1525), a Venetian scholar often cited for his encyclopedic knowledge of natural history.</note> asserts that a snake is struck with terror by the sight of a naked man. It is well known and confirmed by many authors that the **catoblepas** <note>A legendary creature from Ethiopia, described by Pliny as having a heavy head it always looks down with; its gaze was said to be lethal.</note>, which is but a small animal, can nonetheless kill a person from a thousand paces away by its gaze alone. Even a man affected by **bleary-eyedness** <term>lippitudo: a chronic inflammation or watering of the eyes</term> is capable of infecting another person at a considerable distance through a certain secret emission of contagious rays, even making that person bleary-eyed as well. We see that an onion can draw tears from a person at a distance, and this by the mere ejaculation of its rays. Furthermore, it is a known fact that, just as a healthy thing usually receives its like in a healing manner, so a corrupted thing, through an **Antipathetic** <note>In Fludd’s philosophy, "Antipathy" is a natural repulsion or disharmony, while "Sympathy" is an attraction or harmony.</note> manner, infects and poisons its like at a distance, even if it was previously healthy. We observe this when the eye of one man affected by **ophthalmia** <term>inflammation of the eye</term> infects no other part of another man’s body except the eye. So too, one who is **consumptive** <term>phthisicus: suffering from tuberculosis or wasting of the lungs</term> or has ulcerated lungs wounds and damages the lungs of another person with his breath even at a suitable distance; this happens by the application or meeting of two irradiations of the same nature, one of which is affected in an Antipathetic and poisonous way, whereby it tends to contaminate the other to which it is applied.

But to return to our **Magnetic** goal, which is as much Spiritual as it is physical, I affirm that there is such a great Spiritual regard of Sympathy between one creature and another that the beloved, in a marvelous way, attracts and allures the Spirit of the lover to itself. I myself saw this same thing wonderfully performed by my water dog: For on my journey toward **Lyon in France** <note>original: "Lugdunum Galliæ"</note>, I lost my traveling bag which was hanging over the bow of my saddle (in which, besides other necessities, my **letters of exchange** <note>original: "literæ Camby" — documents used by merchants and travelers to claim funds, similar to modern traveler's checks.</note> were enclosed). When I attempted to turn back to search for it, I could by no means compel my post-horse to go backward, contrary to its usual habit. Thus, I was forced by necessity to send my dog to search for my lost goods and bring them back to me. The dog departed, and after being absent for nearly half an hour, he brought that bag back in his mouth. This was indeed admirable, considering I was on horseback and thus he could not have sensed any track or scent of my feet; nevertheless, he hurried directly to the bag, which I had lost as if in a "Tantalean gap" <note>An allusion to Tantalus; Fludd likely means a place where the bag was visible but unreachable or simply lost in a void.</note>, and perceiving my scent upon it, he recognized the item immediately and brought it to me at a swift run. But to come closer and more pertinently to this point: A certain friend in my company at that time lost his water dog in the city of London at night. Meanwhile, we both entered a certain private house where he had hardly ever been before. While we were having a 

<column-break/>

private conversation in a room of that house with the door closed, a little after half an hour the dog returned and came to the gate, scratching it vigorously with his claws so that it might be opened, in order to reach his master. From this it is evident that the rays of the dog's affection, although his body was absent from his Master, nevertheless did not desert the sight of his Master’s rays; thus it happened that they led him so directly to that unknown place.

Is there not also that admirable Sympathetic emanation from the pigeon called the **carrier pigeon** <note>original: "columba tabellaria"</note>, by which and by whose light it is accustomed to head so directly across so many miles to the home where it was born and raised? For that reason, it loves and is affected by that home so dearly that, even if it is carried 500 miles away shut in its basket, it will nonetheless fly directly back with letters hanging from its neck. This is indeed clear evidence that the bird is governed directly on its way by the rays of its affection, which are continued and united in a certain Spiritual way, and are not separated from the place in which it takes the greatest delight. What shall we say of two persons, one of whom loves a male and the other a female, and is affected without any reason; and therefore pursues the beloved with rays of affection, even though she, on her part, abhors him, neglects him, and cannot receive him with a reciprocal degree of affection, but turns the rays of his love into hatred? But truly, where two receive each other with mutual affection and Sympathetic union, there indeed the power of the action produces its effects at a much greater distance: Not otherwise than when two stars of heaven emit their rays diametrically and meet in one and the same Harmonic point of affection.

Indeed, as we see taught by experience, there is a great Antipathy between the contracted Spirit of a murdered man and the murderer; so much so, that the vital Spirit of the dead man, contracted in its center by the contact of cold after death, is observed to move again from the center to the circumference through a certain irascible, Antipathetic passion. This causes the congealed blood to flow back again and move toward the murderer, as if it wished to resist the fertile assault of its enemy, or as if it sought to take vengeance against him. Thus indeed we must recognize and confess that where one Spirit meets another of similar nature through a Sympathetic reason, there the power must be greater; and consequently, its action can exercise its force at a longer distance, as is clearly demonstrated in the hidden operation between the blood-stained cloth, the **weapon salve** <note>original: "unguentum armarium"</note>, and the wounded person. I have spoken many words about these things in that hostile encounter that occurred between **Foster the Priest** <note>William Foster (1591–1643), an English clergyman who published a pamphlet in 1631 titled "Hoplocrisma-Spadacrus," attacking Fludd’s use of the weapon salve as witchcraft.</note> and me.

### SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part II.

...namely in that book of mine written against his book called **THE WEAPON-SALVE SPONGE** <note>original: "HOPLOCRISMA SPONGVS." William Foster’s 1631 work attacked the "Weapon Salve"—a medicinal ointment applied to the weapon that caused a wound rather than the wound itself—as being magical or diabolical.</note>, or a sponge for wiping away the weapon ointment, the title of which book of mine is *The Squeezing of the Priest Foster’s Sponge* <note>original: "Spongiæ Fosterianæ Presbyteri compressio." Fludd published this rebuttal in 1631.</note>. Of the core of that book I shall say more at the end of this discourse, God willing.

Foster’s argument consists in the impossibility of the ointment’s operation, or rather, the impossibility of the flow of living blood or the emission of influences toward dead and congealed blood at such a remote distance as some have proposed. Indeed, if such an "impossibility" were true in the animal kingdom—which is more expanded and less bound by bodily chains than the other two kingdoms <note>The three kingdoms of nature: Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral.</note>—I wonder why it is not considered even more impossible in a mineral body? A mineral, by reason of its firm and constricted solidity, is consequently less fit for containing and retaining influential rays than a body that is more loose, soft, and porous. Furthermore, the body of a living animal is warm and fiery, and consequently readier to expand and emit its rays further; whereas a mineral is cold, and therefore less active and powerful in the ejaculation of its rays. 

And yet, nonetheless, we are taught by experience that the Magnet respects the Pole Star and emits its Spiritual gaze toward it. Likewise, that star shoots its rays toward its mineral goal at a distance almost immeasurable, as has been demonstrated in the preceding pages. Since this is so, why, I ask, can the "Animal Star" <note>Fludd refers to the "vital spark" or "spirit" within a living creature as a "star" because he believes all life derives from celestial light.</note> derived from the Stellar or heavenly source, not also pour its rays or influence into the blood congealed in its unctuous earth (namely, infused in the ointment), or into the invisible Spirit of the blood absorbed into the pores of the wounding instrument? This is especially true of iron, by reason of its attractive, sulfurous nature. For experience confirms that, even if no bodily blood is found upon a Sword or a dagger and the like, if the place on the weapon that caused the wound is smeared with the ointment, it still effects a cure by reason of its Sympathetic gaze. Indeed, rural or rustic Surgeons have discovered through experience that when they do not dare to examine a deep wound with an iron probe, they can very easily discern how deep the weapon penetrated the flesh by placing the Sword in a fire. For that portion of the weapon or Sword which caused the wound changes its heat, and will appear darker or bluer than the rest. By this observation, I say, they understand how deep the wound is. And therefore, this is an excellent argument for the entrance of the blood-spirits into the substance of the wounding instrument; and consequently, it is clear that there are essential Spirits which emanate or go out from the blood as it leaps from the body.

<column-break/>

By these things it is argued against Mr. Foster that, if the coarser Spirits in the blood are strong enough to penetrate the firm substance of steel, it is probable that their thinner Spirits can permeate all other things, however compact, like an influence without any resistance. Nor can these things now seem to me either miracles or at least impossibilities, since experience also witnesses that this same effect exists in the mute and deaf (or insensible) mineral. For a needle or Steel, by the mere contact of a Magnet, is accustomed to drink in its spirits; these Spirits, thus absorbed by the iron, penetrate through its whole being, and consequently are present in every portion of it. For this Axiom, from the most excellent Philosophers well-versed in the mystery of the Magnet, is as follows:

<margin>The Problem</margin>
If an iron bolt, or a portion of thick iron wire, is touched magnetically at one end, the Magnetic vigor will permeate the whole iron, and it will have a contrary virtue in each end or pole of that axis—namely, one Northern and the other Southern—and half of the axis will be of one nature and the other half of the other. <margin>Ridley: *Tractatus Magneticus*, chapter 6.</margin> <gloss>Where **a.** has a Northern nature and **b.** a Southern nature. This is their general rule.</gloss> <note>Mark Ridley (1560–1624) was an English physician who wrote extensively on magnetism, following the work of William Gilbert.</note>

But indeed, I shall come closer to my purpose and transfer my demonstration from the mineral to the vegetable, so that by this means I may better and more clearly express "like by its like" in our animal subject. My intention, therefore, is to dwell upon a grain of wheat which, when it has died and putrefied in the earth, is raised again from death by the radiant influence of the Sun. For "like," by a certain magnetic virtue, attracts its "like" to itself, and "like" is accustomed to rejoice in its "like," and "like" is raised and quickened by its "like"—that is, it is called forth from its central rest by its "like" which calls, entices, and embraces it. In this way, the radiant substance (or atoms of solar influence) lying idle and doing nothing in the grain of wheat, is now—in the center of that same grain dissolved by corruption—aroused by its external "like" to act and work for its redemption from the elementary filth or the viscous bonds of the elementary composition. And therefore, just as the Spirit of life in the wheat was contracted into the center by the external circumferential cold, so now, by the presence of fresh Solar irradiation descending from above, it is raised as if from death to life. In this way, by the assistance of the heavenly rays, it rises beyond the limits of the corrupted grain and penetrates the surface of the earth, hanging outside and above it in the open air, and with the greatest effort attempts to ascend into its solar fatherland from which it descended. But in its upward motion, it is surrounded on all sides by the sublunary substance (as if by elemental chains which enclose and bind it everywhere) and by the volatile salt of the air...

<margin>Psellus on demons.</margin> Nor would I wish for anyone to reject my assertion, since it is certain that in the very stones and "deaf" minerals <note>Minerals were called "deaf" or "mute" because they lacked the obvious senses of animals.</note> there is a concupiscible passion <note>An "appetite" or "desire" for something else; here referring to magnetic attraction.</note>, as can be seen in the Magnet and iron. The spirit of iron, even though it is mineral, is also of the same condition in its universal nature as all other spirits. Therefore, I would not want anyone to wonder at what I have said: that a mineral spirit affects that of the animal and vegetable. Indeed, I shall bring forward a sufficiently probable demonstration to prove this. 

There is a most noble Earl of England, called *The Earl of Bridgewater*, whose gardener cruelly wounded his hand with a scythe while mowing grass. A great quantity of blood was shed, and the hemorrhage could not be stopped. This was announced to the Earl, and they implored his help in this matter, as they knew he possessed the weapon salve <note>original: "unguentum armarium." A powder or ointment applied to the weapon that caused a wound to heal the patient through "sympathy."</note> and was very well practiced in its use. He immediately ordered that the scythe be knocked from its wooden support or handle and brought to him. When the wounded man heard this, while he held his wounded hand, the Earl struck the iron blade with a fairly strong blow of a mallet. At that instant, without any other remedy, the blood stopped; nor did he lose a single drop after that blow. It was as if the mineral spirit, which contained the animal spirit, was terrified by that blow and a certain fear, and the spirit of the wounded man was struck, and consequently lost its entire faculty of attracting and retaining the spirit of the striker. Or perhaps the spirits of the wounded man, soaked into the iron, consenting in harmony with the spirit of the wounded man, seemed to rejoice in that act as a kind of vengeance which the wounded man took upon the iron or weapon. For it must be known that there is a sympathetic and antipathetic irradiation equally between animals and minerals, as there is between animals and animals, or minerals and minerals. 

But observe, I pray, this experiment concerning the weapon salve. Sir Bevis Thelwell <note>original: "eques auratus" (a knight). wounded by an axe. He had been treated by surgeons before, but without any mitigation of the pains, so that he could not sleep for four or five nights. He then anointed the axe and, as is the custom, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and immediately the pains were mitigated so that he began to sleep. Hearing this—and specifically so that he might test the thing reported to him by many—he removed the linen cloth from the axe and scraped the ointment from a single corner of the anointed axe with a small knife. Once this was done, he was immediately informed that the wounded man complained greatly of a pain suddenly arising from a single corner of the wound. Whereupon, he immediately smeared the bare and scraped portion of the axe again, and the pain was instantly settled. This done, she dipped the part or end of the stick smeared with blood into the ointment, and gradually their pains ceased. Among the others, a certain woman from the neighborhood, of a reckless and contentious disposition and quite prone to speaking scurrilous insults, was also vexed by the pain of teeth, and was finally cured in the same way as the others. 

Nevertheless, a few days later, she gave reproachful words to that noblewoman’s maidservant, nor did she spare her benefactress the Lady with her malevolent tongue. When these things were brought to the noblewoman, as she was of a humorous disposition, she said laughing: "Then I shall try the experiment related to me by the giver of this ointment." And she immediately went to the box of ointment, pulled out the stick belonging to this woman, and threw it into a basin full of water. Once this was done, the reckless woman’s pains returned, and she was only cured a second time after a reconciliation was finally made. Having observed these accidents with diligence, I noticed that the primary comfort of the enclosed spirit consists in its preservation from external cold; and that if the ointment is removed from it, the chilly air (which is hostile to the activity of the blood spirits) will be powerful enough to congeal them. ### SECOND SECTION, BOOK II. Part II.

And that same spirit, according to the testimony of *Ezekiel* <note>original: "in duabus proprietatibus qui stat à septentrione & ab austro." Referring to Ezekiel 37 and the "four winds."</note> (*in the two properties of the one who stands to the north and to the south*), encounters an imbalance in the Spirit that is enclosed and congealed within the weapon. This occurs through the effect of the weakening of the drawn-out rays, and, as if by a certain confirmation, acts upon the wound of the sufferer. Furthermore, we must consider that any separated blood possesses within itself the character of the *Microcosm* <term>Microcosm: The "little world," a Renaissance concept that the human body is a miniature map of the entire universe.</term>: In no different way than a single portion of a *Magnet* divided from the whole possesses within itself all the proportions of the entire *Macrocosm* <term>Macrocosm: The "great world" or the universe at large.</term>, namely the poles, the *Equinox*, and so on. It is just like the whole; so much so, that the Form of the wounded limb exists within the *Spirits* of the emitted blood, and it makes its relation to every part of that same limb. This is no different than how the poles of some portion of a whole *Magnet*, however small, have a relationship to the whole. There is also a similar hidden attraction and emission of rays between a small amount of emitted blood and the entire mass of blood retained in the veins, just as there is between a small *Magnet* cut from a Large one and the whole. I conclude, therefore, that just as the *Spirits* congealed in the severed *Blood*, now possessing the iron by virtue of the homogeneous heat and the oiliness of the ointment, are observed to ripen and gradually exhale through imperceptible breathing toward their source—no differently than a spark of a grain of wheat, preserved from external cold in its earthy shell, strives to breathe out beyond the margins of the earth and tend upward toward the celestial sun—so indeed we see the wound in the injured person gradually heal. And so much for the manner of action between the wound and the weapon-salve or *Magnetic* ointment; now I shall briefly discuss the interval or space located between the wound and the ointment.

The distance between the *Pole Star* and the *Magnet* is unknown, and yet one operates upon the other through the reciprocal emission of their rays upward and downward. From this, it is clear that no "sphere of activity" can be assigned to these actions of theirs. The Sun and the Spirit in a grain of wheat act upon each other in exactly the same way; namely, by the continuity of one and the same nature. Behold, therefore: here the limited and bounded sphere of activity is entirely abolished, since no one can justly determine the extent of the *Solar* influence, in whose essence the grain in the wheat participates. This is no different than how a tiny *Magnet* cut from a Great one similarly enjoys its poles and circles along with that Great one.
<margin>Ezekiel 37.</margin>
Man has a most subtle influence and a most vivid Spirit of life infused into him from on high—that is, inspired by divine breath—in which is located the property of the four winds, as the *Prophet Ezekiel* teaches us. Consequently, he has the "idea" or blueprint of every nature within himself. But the essence of that *spirit* is indivisible; and therefore the vivifying Spirit sent from it into man possesses all the properties of that Spirit which sent or infused it, no differently than

<column-break/>

a smaller *Magnet* (to insist upon this experiment again and again) taken from a larger one acquires the property of the larger in every respect. Consequently, the Spirit of the one is no more divided from the other than the Solar rays are from the Sun. But truly the *Spirit of the Lord*, which fills all things (as *Salomon* says), intensifies the power of its operation more or less in man according to His will. Therefore, He in no way admits that imaginary "sphere of activity" which human wisdom—I mean the subject of *Pagan Philosophy*, which is foolishness before God—has devised. For that reason, *Hermes* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary sage to whom many foundational texts of alchemy and magic were attributed.</note> has these things to say:
<margin>Pimander 11.</margin>
> The Soul, full of mind and God, fills the innermost parts of the world, embraces the outer parts, and provides life to all things; it gives life to that Great animal, the world, and Spirit to all things that live within it.

And he says elsewhere:
> In the nature of the body, nothing is more capacious, nothing faster, nothing stronger or more powerful [than the soul]. Thus, beginning again to meditate from your own self, command your soul, and it will fly away faster than you can command; it pleases, I say, that it should cross over into the Ocean, and it will be there before you have ordered it—never departing from where it now is. Command it again to fly into heaven, and it will need no wings; for nothing shall obstruct its course—not the fire of the Sun, nor the vastness of the ether, nor the turning of the heavens, nor the bodies of the ancient Stars—but penetrating all things, it may transcend even to the supernal body. Indeed, if you wish to cross all the spheres of the heavens and investigate what is above, that too will be permitted to you. Observe how great is the power of your soul, how great its speed.

These are his words. From these two testimonies of *Hermes*, we can observe, first, that the soul in general, and therefore in the species or the individual, is full of divinity. Consequently, that Divine essence, which works all in all, is present in this soul and in every member of the same, as the *Apostle* <note>Referring to St. Paul.</note> testifies. And it is from this that the true Philosopher in the place cited before said that the soul is full of mind and God. Secondly, we see that this Divinity in the created Universal Spirit fills all things in a certain Angelic existence—that is, insofar as it is clothed in the vast mundane spirit as if in a garment. And the sacred page seems to support this, saying:
<margin>Wisdom 12:1.</margin>
> The incorruptible Spirit of God is in every thing,

and therefore it is the essential act of mundane life, just as I proved in the first book of this Section. Whence also the said *Hermes* says elsewhere:
<margin>Pimander 10.</margin>
> All souls throughout the whole world flow from the one soul of the entire world, as if distributed and moving in a circle, etc.

This indeed agrees with that passage of *Salomon* cited earlier: namely, that all souls in this world are certain radiant emanations proceeding from the Universal irradiation, which proceeds from the eternal source of illuminating action—more sparingly to some, and more copiously to others.

Hence, man is said to be a little lower than the Angels in dignity, by reason of the large portion of light granted to him by God. But **Master Foster** with his associates says and repeats that this spirit—which must work into the blood and from the blood into the ointment—is merely natural and not at all divine. Truly, I cannot help but smile at this assertion of theirs: As if someone were to say that this life-giving act, and also all the other faculties belonging to the human Spirit, do not draw their origin from one and the same divine source, when we are taught by the Apostle that in him we live, move, and have our being <note>Acts 17:28.</note>. Again, it is said that the seat of life or the vital Spirit is in the blood. And **St. John** says: "In the Word was life." <note>John 1:4.</note> I will say, therefore, what a certain true Philosopher writes about this point:

> The Soul (he says), being made in the likeness of all wisdom, carries every likeness within itself; it is an intellectual Spirit, ever living, ever in motion, and is called by various names according to the function of its work: It is called Life, while it nourishes; Spirit, while it contemplates; Sense, while it feels; Soul [Animus], while it is wise; Mind, while it understands; Reason, while it discerns; Memory, while it remembers; when it wills, it is the Will: But all these are nothing but the single soul of one essence, however diverse they may be in property.

Thus he spoke. From this it is clear that it is the same essential act which creates life and contemplation, sense and intellect, and which produces memory and reason: finally, it is that which wills and does not will. Since these things are so, do not men burdened with ignorance sin gravely, who claim and maintain that the hidden actions of this concealed Spirit—by which they themselves live, move, understand, discern between good and evil, remember, see, hear, touch, and taste—are the effects of the Devil? And thus the most splendid dignity and honor of the soul itself is violated (by ascribing its secret operations to the Devil) in an irreligious and false manner, instead of the thanksgivings due to it for its assistance, and it is defiled in the eyes of the world. And why, I ask, do they act so absurdly? Because, of course, they do not know how to immerse themselves into the deep marrow of its activity, by which they live, move, and exist. Hence, they do not blush to bound the extension of its activity with limits according to their own pleasure, though (however unknown this may be to them) they receive their life and will from it; by ascribing rash limits to it as judges for their own pleasure, it is infinite in its existence, insofar as it is a Spirit from the emanation

<column-break/>

of the divine, which in its extension is infinite. Therefore it is made evident that this life-giving Spirit emits its actions to any goal in the world from any specific nature, but especially from the microcosmic creature <note>The "microcosm" refers to the human being as a miniature version of the entire universe.</note>, and that all the more quickly and willingly if the goal is of one and the same condition as the vehicle of the spirit—namely, the shed blood—calculating primarily the distance that exists between the wound and the ointment. Furthermore, we shall find this confirmed by other operations of the spirit performed in the same microcosmic mineral, from which it shoots out its rays to an undetermined distance.

For example, it is proven by experience, and that by purely natural ways, with no Devilish delusion or superstitious artifice accompanying it, that if the urine of one suffering from <term>jaundice</term> <note>original: "icteritij"</note> is brought to a doctor or to another person, even many miles distant from the sick person (as has been proven in over a hundred people by the most noble **Count of Mulgrave** <note>Edmund Sheffield, 1st Earl of Mulgrave (1564–1646), a prominent peer and naval commander.</note>, a very just and religious man), and the doctor or someone else makes a paste with that urine and ash-tree ashes, and divides it into 3 or 5 portions, and shapes them into a round form, and makes a small hole in the top of each ball, and fills it with urine with a single grain of saffron, and finally sets these little balls aside in some vessel in a convenient place—the Count himself, I say, with his daughters, testifies that this was true, and that by the power of such a thing he was often accustomed to cure himself, where medicinal experiments were found to be too weak and invalid for this work.

And now I will provide testimony of this matter: In the year 1630, the wife of a Surgeon living near the Tower of London was suffering severely from jaundice and griping pains in her belly. After several doctors applied their efforts in vain, they finally called me; but despite my endeavor, the disease persisted in its strength. Wherefore, hearing me mention the cures performed by that Count, she begged me to send my letters on her behalf to that nobleman. A boy with the letters immediately carried the urine to the Count's house, where he found two strangers acknowledging thanks for their cure from jaundice. For my sake the urine was received, and the servant returned. But I would have you observe the sequel: as soon as the boy departed from her with the urine of his mistress, the sick woman's mind was greatly disturbed by certain talkative and superstitious women, etc., who made her certain that this thing could not have been performed without the help of the Devil or <term>evil magic</term> <note>original: "cacomagie"</note>, and therefore this act would be dangerous for both her body and soul. Upon hearing this, as she was of a sufficiently superstitious, suspicious, and overly incredulous condition, she began to cry out against Magic and sorcery, and became very restless. When I understood this, as she was ungrateful and incredulous, I did not wish to visit her further,

We read in many places of Holy Scripture that the Devil makes use of God’s creatures to carry out his stratagems and wicked machinations against the human race. For example, to take away Job’s fortunes and bring poverty upon him, Satan used God’s winds and called (as the Text testifies) the fire of God from heaven to consume his beasts or herds. Yet God has taught us Christians better than to think those creatures of God should be held as <term>Cacomagical<note>From the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'magia' (magic); refers to "black magic" or magic performed through the aid of evil spirits.</note></term> and Diabolical for that reason, just because God sometimes disposes them to execute His will through the Devil. He even made the Devil the "Prince of the Air," so that it is within his power to stir up tempests in the sea and the elemental heavens; for this reason, the air is sometimes called the "Synagogue of Satan" by some. What then? Must we therefore dread and hold the air and the winds in abomination because the Devil is noted to sometimes commit his crimes by their mediation? Especially since the air is sometimes

<column-break/>

purified and cleared by the agitation of the winds from corruption, as Aristotle testifies. For if the air were not stirred and moved by the winds, it would easily rot, no differently than stagnant ponds. Again, if we were to avoid the air or hold it in horror, by what vehicles or by what Spirit (I pray) would we live, since the seedbed of our life consists in the aerial spirit? <margin>Psalm 121:5.</margin> We also read in the Scriptures that God made the sun to rise indifferently upon the good and the bad, and that the Sun and Moon sometimes bring harm to the earth and men, just as they confer comfort and health to others elsewhere. # ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY. Fol. 121.

...tested in his final manner, he bears witness that it restored [them] to the previous limits of health. He concludes, however, that this mode of curing is commonly found to be certain in those gouts that arise from a sulfurous cause: But (he says) in those that proceed from a false and <term>Mercurial<note>In the medical theories of the time, "mercurial" diseases were thought to be volatile, fluid, or related to the spirit, whereas "sulfurous" ones were inflammatory and heat-based.</note></term> nature, it frequently fails. And therefore, leaving behind that kind of magical way of curing, he prepares himself for that method consisting of topical application.

In that treatise of mine, titled *The Squeezing of the Fosterian Sponge* <note>Original: *Spongiæ Fosterianæ expressio*. This was Fludd’s famous 1631 defense of "Weapon Salve" medicine against the attacks of the clergyman William Foster.</note>, I recited a quite wondrous story about that admirable <term>Sympathy<note>The occult idea that things with similar natures exert a hidden influence on each other across distances.</note></term> which exists between the herb called <term>Rosa Solis<note>The "Sun-Dew" plant (Drosera).</note></term> and the human <term>matrix<note>The womb.</note></term>; and I said how the plant, when placed in plantain water, closes or contracts itself, and that if a part of that water is drunk by a woman laboring in childbirth, and the herb in the water is moved to another house, nevertheless, as her birth-pangs approach, that flower or herb will gradually open and dilate itself, in no other way than the womb of the woman in labor is accustomed to do. This is a truly evident proof that the rays emitted from these two sympathize with one another. I conclude, therefore, that it is manifest that, since the spiritual attractive power in any lower creature descends from the stars of heaven and is of one continuous nature with them—just as solar rays are not,

<column-break/>

on earth, divided from their luminous source—it follows that they emit their radiant influences to one another in no other way than two celestial stars, from which the stars of [earthly] creatures descend, are observed to make their aspects in the open air. Thus, if two stars in heaven are "friends," they are accustomed to sympathize with each other and, as it were, embrace themselves in their meeting or irradiation; but if they are "enemies" to each other, then in their applications they will feel <term>Antipathy<note>The natural repulsion between things of opposing natures, the opposite of Sympathy.</note></term> and will willingly turn away from an embrace. As for the distance they observe in their mutual actions, we ought to imagine it to extend as far as their rays, which make the application, are distant from each other. And I would wish that those who are only occupied with sensible things <note>Things perceptible only by the physical senses, as opposed to spiritual or "occult" realities.</note> should know that the action of these creatures operates secretly through mutual application, even though the effect of that action is not always subjected to the senses. Furthermore, I suggest they conceive that the closer the stars are in heaven in their natural affinity—and consequently those lower creatures which are subject to the spirits of the higher ones—the more effective their sympathizing effects will be, because their rays will shoot out and meet more directly, that is, without any deviation or turning away from one another.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*That the Devil, to perpetrate his stratagems against the human race, makes*<-
->*use of natural things or God's creatures, without which he can perform*<-
->*nothing: And whether those natural things are so <term>Cacomagical<note>From the Greek 'kakos' (bad/evil), meaning "Evil Magic."</note></term>*<-
->*and consequently to be avoided by men, since their hidden*<-
->*effects sometimes conform themselves to the*<-
->*will of the Devil.*<-

We read in many places in Holy Scripture that the Devil makes use of God’s creatures to perpetrate his stratagems and wicked machinations against the human race. For example, to take away the fortunes of Job and bring poverty upon him, Satan used the winds of God, and called (as the Text witnesses) the fire of God from heaven to consume his beasts or herds. God, however, teaches us Christians better than to hold those creatures of God as "Cacomagical" or diabolical for that reason—just because God sometimes disposes them to execute His will through the Devil. He even made the Devil the "Prince of the Air," so that it is within his power to incite storms on the sea and in the elementary heaven; for this reason, the air is sometimes called by some the "Synagogue of Satan." What then? Ought we therefore to recoil from the air and the winds and hold them in abomination, because the Devil is noted as sometimes committing his crimes by their mediation? Especially since the air is sometimes

<column-break/>

purified and cleared of corruption by the agitation of the winds, as Aristotle witnesses; for, if the air were not stirred and moved by the winds, it would easily rot, in no other way than stagnant ponds. Again, if we were to avoid the air or hold it in horror, by what vehicles, or by what spirit (I ask) would we live, since the seedbed of our life consists in the aerial spirit? We also read in the Scriptures that God made the sun rise indifferently upon the good and upon the evil, and that the Sun and Moon sometimes bring harm to the earth and to men, just as they conversely confer comfort and health to others. <margin>Psalm 121:5.</margin> And therefore King David says: *The sun shall not strike you by day, nor the moon by night; God shall preserve you from all evil.* The Moon, which is also called <term>Hecate<note>The ancient Greek goddess associated with the moon, magic, and witchcraft.</note></term> by the poets, is said to be the goddess of witches and mages: For <term>Medea<note>A famous sorceress in Greek mythology, niece of Circe.</note></term>, that famous mage, poured out her prayers to Hecate herself to favor her wicked works; and yet the air, water, and earth are irrigated by the moisture and humid virtue of the moon, and plants as well as animals [depend on] its vegetation...

### SECTION TWO, BOOK II. Part II.

...but I immediately sent word to the nobleman, so that he might destroy that work, if possible, by breaking the <note>original: "globulos"; likely referring to medicinal pellets or symbolic objects used in a sympathetic ritual</note> pellets, and render it of no consequence. He reported back that he would do this, but affirmed that it was already too late, saying that the work would be completed despite him. And indeed, the woman immediately began to recover from that point on; perhaps she herself attributed the reason for her cure to some other medicine of no importance in this work. I also cannot hide another story on this matter in this place. A certain noblewoman, the daughter of a Baron and wife of a most noble Knight, suffered severely from <term>jaundice<note>Original: "morbo icteritio." Jaundice was often treated sympathetically using yellow substances like saffron due to the "Doctrine of Signatures."</note></term>. I treated her nearly twice, but the disease returned. Seeing this, I advised her husband to send her urine to the Count. He did as I suggested. However, the Countess herself wished to undertake the care of this noblewoman as a matter of honor. Her preparation achieved some effect in treating the disease, but she could not bring it to a successful conclusion; therefore, the urine was sent a second time and prepared by the Count. Immediately, with no other medicine applied in the meantime, she recovered. Many besides myself were witnesses to this matter. Finally, I myself am not ignorant of the method and reasoning behind this cure: for that most noble Count, out of his favor, communicated it to me; indeed, his most noble daughters also cured many, both poor and rich, out of kindness. The Count even affirmed to me that he had cured some at a distance of nearly a hundred miles. 

Now, the principle of that cure is achieved in no other way than that of the <term>weapon salve<note>Original: "unguenti armarij." A controversial "magnetic" medicine of the 17th century where the weapon that caused a wound was treated with ointment rather than the wound itself.</note></term>. For the Spirit of the Blood in the infected person has a continuous relationship to its own salt. Indeed, its habitation lies within the aerial Salt of the Blood. Since this Salt is a "subtle earth" in whose center the Spirit is contracted, and since that Salt is dispersed through the urine (which is the serum of the Blood), it allures and attracts its "like" from the infected body. Existing there as if resuscitated and newly quickened, it emits new rays to meet, console, and correct those infected rays that were being ejected from the sick person's body. Furthermore, the infecting spirit of the jaundiced humor is suppressed by the power of both the saffron and the salt in the ashes; thus, just as that [preparation] dies, so the attacking jaundiced humor, with its poisonous Spirit, gradually withers and is finally extinguished. From this it is clear that, by means of one and the same Spirit in the salt of the urine and that in the blood of the sick or jaundiced person, both are restored and cleansed in a <term>Sympathetic<note>A term describing hidden connections where things of like nature influence each other across space.</note></term> manner. Meanwhile, the corrupted humor—that is, the infecting Spirit—is extinguished and annihilated in both the patient's body and the urine in an <term>Antipathetic<note>The opposite of sympathy; a natural repulsion or destructive force between opposing natures.</note></term> manner. In this respect, we compare that composition of ashes, urine, and saffron in such a jaundice cure with the weapon salve and the healing of wounds, and

<column-break/>

the urine transferred from the sick person to the mass thus composed [is compared] to the blood or spirit on the weapon or sword or similar things. Also, the quickening of the Spirit congealed in the salt of the urine, I relate to the Spirit revivifying and stirring in the dead blood, or the Spirit absorbed by the porous substance of the iron or weapon. Thus, we see here one and the same consensus: for just as the "dead" blood proceeded from a living fountain of blood, so indeed the urine, which is the whey or serous substance of the blood, is by no means destitute of blood-spirits in the transplantation of human blood-spirits. 

What shall we think of the wonderful effects on other animals or plants? Certainly, those who are versed in the mysteries of <term>Natural Magic<note>In the Renaissance, this referred to the scientific study of hidden natural forces (like magnetism or herbs) rather than demonic sorcery.</note></term>, both in the macrocosm and the microcosm, cannot fail to know that the <term>Spiritual Mummy<note>Original: "Mummiā Spiritualē." Paracelsian term for the vital life-force inherent in human tissue that could be "harvested" for medicine.</note></term>—whose seat is in the microcosmic blood—can be extracted from the human body by means of a certain Magnetic substance chosen from the same subject, and transplanted into a beast, tree, or plant. Thus, by this reasoning, the disease of a sick person can be transferred from him into the said creatures by the virtue of such an operation or "microcosmic magnet." The practice of this matter will be clearly explained in the following book.

Similarly, Johannes Rumelius Pharamundus professes that he has cured many suffering from <term>gout<note>Original: "podagra."</note></term> in such a way: namely, by cutting the hair and nails of the patient's feet and legs, thrusting them into a hole made with a drill as far as the marrow of an oak tree, and finally closing that hole firmly with a plug formed from the same tree, and lastly smearing the perforated place all over with cow dung. "Then," he says, "if the gout does not return within the space of three months, the oak will be sufficient to attract the disease to itself in a Magnetic fashion." But if it returns in that time, then this is an argument for the insufficient magnetic virtue of the oak. Therefore, he then proceeds in this manner: he drills another hole in a different oak, and—in case the first was in vain—he collects the wood fragments that came out during the drilling, crushes them, sews them into a linen bag, and applies this bag to the painful spot. He usually does this for three days before the <term>new moon<note>Original: "novilunium." Astronomical timing was considered crucial for the success of sympathetic remedies.</note></term>. Then, at the hour of the new moon, he removes the bag from the spot, takes out the wooden pieces, puts them into the hole, and closes it with a strong plug. But if finally, after three months, the patient is not perfectly cured, then he proceeds to his third operation, which is of this sort: 1. he takes the hair and nails of the patient, ties them to the back of a locust or a river crayfish, and throws the animal thus into a river, and the patient will be cured. This, he—a Doctor of Medicine—professes in a certain small book of his printed in the German language. And in that same place, he seems to announce to the world that he has cured many with this first experiment, and not a few with the first and second, and finally that he has [cured] a great many gouty patients...

## CHAPTER VI.

->*That the Devil makes use of natural things or God's creatures to perpetrate*<-
->*his stratagems against the human race, without which he can perform*<-
->*nothing: And whether those natural things are so Cacomagical*<-
->*and consequently to be avoided by men, because their*<-
->*hidden effects sometimes conform to the*<-
->*will of the Devil.*<-

We read in many places of sacred scripture that the Devil makes use of God's creatures to perpetrate his stratagems and wicked machinations against the human race. For example, *Satan*, to take away the fortunes of *Job* and to inflict poverty upon him, used the winds of God, and called (as the Text testifies) the fire of God from heaven to consume his beasts or herds. God, however, instructs us Christians better than that those creatures of God should be held by us as <term>Cacomagical<note>From the Greek "kakos" (evil). It refers to "black magic" or magic performed with evil intent or through demonic aid.</note></term> and Diabolical for that reason, just because God sometimes disposes them to execute his will through the Devil. He also made the Devil the prince of the air; so that it is placed in his power to incite storms in the sea and the elementary heaven, and for this reason the air is sometimes called by some the "Synagogue of *Satan*." What? Should we therefore abhor the air and winds and hold them in abomination because the Devil is sometimes noted to commit his crimes by their mediation, when the air is sometimes

<column-break/>

purified and clarified from corruption by the agitation of the winds, as *Aristotle* testifies: For, if the air were not stirred and moved by the winds, it would easily rot, no differently than stagnant pools. Again, if we were to avoid the air, or hold it in horror, in what vehicles or by what (I pray) Spirit would we live, since the nursery of our life consists in the aerial spirit. We also read in the scriptures that God made the sun rise indifferently over the good and the bad, and the Sun and Moon sometimes bring harm to the earth and men, just as they confer comfort and health to others elsewhere. And therefore King *David* says: <margin>Psalm 121:5</margin> The Sun shall not strike you by day, nor the Moon by night; God will preserve you from all evil. The Moon, which is also called *Hecate* by the Poets, is said to be the Goddess of witches and sorcerers: For to *Hecate* herself, *Medea* that famous Witch poured out her prayers to propitiate her nefarious works, and yet the air, water, and earth are irrigated by the moisture and humid virtue of the moon, and plants as well as animals [depend on it for] vegetation...

# SECTION TWO, BOOK II. Part II.

...acknowledge her [the Moon] as the patroness or nurturing mother. It is she who causes the seas to swell, and again, by another of her positions or aspects in the sky, the seas are lowered, and the <term>humors<note>In pre-modern science, humors were the vital fluids (like sap in plants or blood in humans) that governed health and growth.</note></term> in every vegetable creature are found to be more sparse and diminished. Indeed, we observe that all malignant aquatic spirits are subject to her influences, and even **Satan** observes the diverse times of the positions, or conjunctions and alignments of the moon with other stars—both fixed and wandering—in his malignant actions. For he has been for a long time quite skilled in **astrology**, and knows the effects of every celestial position; consequently, he is by no means ignorant of the details of their stronger influences upon the animal, vegetable, or mineral creatures that are subject to them. And therefore he understands the times in which these influences are poured down from above, and he is highly experienced in their virtues, which at that time are endowed with greater vigor and efficacy—specifically when the powerful influence of their own constellations strikes directly upon them. This excites their central spirits to emit and manifest the furthest reaches of their hidden and secret natures or conditions. At that very instant, he collects herbs or stones, or makes use of the members of animals; or at least, he teaches witches or sorceresses to perform this same thing, even without them having knowledge of the mystery of the constellations or the application of the rays at the time of collecting those creatures. Thus, when these women attempt to use those same <term>simples<note>A 'simple' is a medicinal herb or plant used on its own, rather than as part of a complex mixture.</note></term> by themselves without their master, neglecting the "time of election" out of ignorance, they find them weak and of almost no virtue; for the spirit of any herb, animal, or mineral is weaker when the star which is its nurse and, as it were, its "celestial mother," has the least power or dominion in the heavens.

The astrological physician, taught by experience, is not ignorant of any of this. For in collecting this or that herb at the exact point when the constellation—whether fixed or wandering—which has essential dominion over it is in its greatest dignity or power in the sky, he finds an admirable faculty and efficacy in it, both in its hidden and manifest properties. On the other hand, if the herb is collected at a time when its patroness or celestial mother and nurse is weak and void of virtue, it will appear in its operation as if dead and of hardly any efficacy. From these things it is quite clear that there are creatures of God which operate by their own essential natures or spirits, and produce both **Sympathetic** and **Antipathetic** effects. The Devil uses these to execute his malice, no differently than a physician, a philosopher, or a <term>natural magus<note>A 'natural magus' was a scholar-scientist who sought to use the inherent, God-given laws of nature (like magnetism or astrology) for good ends.</note></term> attempts to accomplish his good intentions with herbs, animals, and minerals. What then is to be said? That those who use

<column-break/>

God's creatures in their affairs, and who operate through their virtues—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—are to be esteemed entirely as <term>Evil Magicians<note>original: "Cacomagis," from the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'magos' (magician).</note></term>, and their works held to be Diabolical, simply because the Devil sometimes adapts their subtle and abstruse actions to establish and exalt his own name and fame among the "wise" of this world? Is it not God who is accustomed to work such effects through His creatures and produce them before the world? Did He not originally impart these virtues or faculties to His creatures by His Word in the creation, and continue them through the succession of generations even to this day? Why, therefore, is it not just as possible for man, who is formed in the image of God, to understand the true times or "hours of election" for collecting those creatures, and to understand and utilize their virtues, just as well as the Devil? What? Has man himself, after the Fall of Adam, been so blinded by ignorance that he can hardly distinguish light from darkness?

Yet we gather in part from the Holy Scriptures that Adam, after his fall, knew the virtues of the stars and the condition of every particular earthly creature subject to them. For otherwise it would have been impossible for him to assign a genuine name, suited to its nature, to each of them. But if Adam’s descendants have become so blind that they cannot distinguish colors at all, and are therefore ignorant of such secret treasures of God: how, I ask, does the Devil have such a profound insight into them? For it is certain that, because of his rebellion against his Creator, he was cast down far lower than the human race, and consequently covered by a darker veil of shadows than man—whence he is not unjustly called the "Prince of Darkness."

But the worldly-minded will reply, I know well: that the Devil is a Spirit without a body and, for that reason, is more powerful at discerning the secrets of God in creatures; wherefore he can comprehend them more quickly and better than man, who is a gross, compact, and corporeal creature. And again, man dies in every age of the world, but the Devil, by reason of his <term>aeviternity<note>A theological term for the type of 'everlasting' existence enjoyed by angels and spirits, distinct from the absolute eternity of God.</note></term> and the perpetuity of his life, is without doubt endowed with the greatest experience.

I respond that, although man dies and is not accustomed to remain long in this world, and although his intellect is somewhat darkened by reason of the Fall of his first parent; <margin>from Wisdom 9</margin> and although (as Solomon says) his soul is weighed down by a "poorly digested body" <note>This is a reference to Wisdom of Solomon 9:15: "For the corruptible body presseth down the soul."</note>; so that he can hardly distinguish by himself the things that are before his eyes; nevertheless, in the beginning after the fall of Adam, the revelation of truth was granted to him by God, as well as the detection of abstruse things in nature. These are revealed to him by succession or **Cabalistic tradition** even from his first father Adam, and also to certain people the secret of God is immediately revealed through His Holy Spirit, which to His...
