<meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s defense of "natural magic" and astrological timing. Having established that the Devil observes the stars to perform his malice, Fludd now argues that the same knowledge was possessed by King Solomon through Divine Wisdom, and that such knowledge is inherently neutral and intended for human benefit.</meta>

### ON MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY. Folio 122.

<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 7:17.</margin>
He granted it to the chosen: For, through the mediation of wisdom (as **Solomon** himself testifies), he knew the disposition of the earth, the powers of the **Elements**, the beginning, middle, and end of times, the changes of customs, the division of seasons, the course of the year, the disposition of the **Stars**, the natures of living things, the conditions of wild beasts, the powers of the winds, the differences of plants, the virtues of roots; indeed, he says, "I have uncovered all things, both hidden and secret, for wisdom, the worker of all things, taught me." <note>original: "sapientia, quæ est omnium operatrix, me docuit"</note> And again we find that he was well-versed in the mysteries of all plants, from the humble hyssop to the tall cedar of Lebanon. Was there, therefore, any diabolical action in Solomon—to look upon, inquire into, and apply practice to the secrets of plants, animals, and stones? Or to notice those stars in heaven with his **astrological** science, and to learn what their radical "mothers" and "nurturers" in heaven are, and to observe the more fitting times for their collection? For these things are created by Divine Wisdom itself, and Wisdom operates essentially in them and through them; and finally, God made Solomon a participant in His own secret operations. Is it diabolical simply because the Devil, through his own sharp observation, has also become a participant in these secrets and uses them to serve his own ways? 

What then? Because I say that a man has the knowledge of how to collect and choose this or that "simple" <note>A "simple" refers to a medicinal herb or a single natural ingredient used in a remedy.</note> creature while it is in its greatest vigor, and does so by observing the relationship between that creature and its stars, should a man not also be allowed to partake in that same natural knowledge? Should he not be made knowing and intelligent in the art of their collection or selection without the help or revelation of the Devil? Since we are taught by the open words of Scripture that God created all these creatures for human use, should the actions of those men who use them be judged diabolical? Should such knowledge be forbidden to men just because the Devil usurps these things for his own malignant inventions? It is as if one were to say that God created anything for the use of the Devil, and not to serve mankind in his necessity according to his free will—especially since it is said elsewhere that power was given to man to have dominion over every creature. 

Even if some simple animal, vegetable, or mineral might sometimes and in certain cases bring harm to a man or act as a poison, they are nonetheless proven to be healthful in another respect. No wind is found to be so wicked and malicious that it "blows good to no one." <note>original: "Non reperitur adeò pravus & malitioſus ventus, qui alicui non ſlet bonum." This is an early Latin version of the English proverb "It's an ill wind that blows nobody good."</note> **Colocynth**, **Scammony**, **Euphorbium**, **Squirting Cucumber**, **Spurge**, **Bear's Breech**, **Spearwort**, and similar things in the vegetable kingdom are sometimes proven to be poisonous in their effect, and yet they are healthfully applied to the human body by a wise physician. Likewise in the mineral kingdom: **Arsenic**, **Orpiment**, **Antimony**, **Realgar**, **Quicksilver**, and similar substances in the mineral sphere

<column-break/>

sometimes kill if they are applied without preparation or correction; and yet, when handled by the lucky hand of a **Natural Magician**, they restore lost health. Finally, in the animal kingdom, the **Toad**, the **Viper**, the **Scorpion**, the **Spider**, **Spanish Flies**, and similar creatures are known to be quite poisonous. Nevertheless, they can be applied or used in a healthful manner once the proper preparation is made; in place of their toxicity, they are known to preserve one from poison, inasmuch as they are frequently used as <term>alexipharmics<note>A historical term for medicines used to ward off or neutralize poisons and venom.</note></term>. 

Furthermore, as nothing exists in the world that operates more effectively through the way of <term>sympathy<note>In Fludd's philosophy, "sympathy" is a natural attraction or resonance between two things of a similar spiritual essence.</note></term> and according to nature than one healthy nature with another; so indeed there is nothing that acts more <term>antipathetically<note>"Antipathy" is the natural repulsion or destructive reaction between opposing natures.</note></term> (that is, contrary to nature and destructively) than the corruption of one intoxicated and poisoned spirit with a healthy spirit of the same species. And the reason for this is that, being greedy for the communication of "rays," the spirit seeks and desires help and assistance in its wasting calamity from the healthy spirits of its own nature. It applies the ray of its own infected spirits to them for the sake of assistance—just as in a time of **contagion**, a spirit ascending like a vapor or emanating from an infected person emits its contaminated rays to embrace a spirit emanating from its like. Thus, by the continuation of one to the other, that fiery poison of the one defiles and intoxicates the healthy nature of the other—and this happens only with what is specifically similar to itself. For the **plague**, which is commonly familiar to humans, does not adhere to or join itself to the spirits of beasts (namely sheep, cows, and the like), just as, conversely, a pestilence or contagion among sheep does not usually infect the human spirit; rather, a similar specific nature is always found more fit to apply its rays to its own kind. 

For this reason, it is evident that just as a healthy **Spiritual Mummy** <note>In Hermetic medicine, "Mummy" (Mummia) was not a literal Egyptian corpse, but the vital life-force or "spirit" extracted from a body, believed to have immense healing power.</note> can be extracted from a healthy man, which is exceedingly beneficial to the human race (so much so that it can be held as a **Panacea** or Universal Medicine for the preservation of health), so also a certain stupendous corruption can be extracted from the Spiritual Mummy of a man, which is exceedingly poisonous, ruinous, and malignant to a healthy spirit. 

Because of this very cause, a certain Jew of the city of **Tunis** (as a trustworthy merchant, who recently arrived from **Fez** in Barbary to the city of **Livorno** in Italy, confidently related to me) acted in a certain way. After he had walked near the port for many days and had fixed his eyes upon a sailor with red hair <note>Red hair was often associated in early modern science with "choleric" temperament and specific spiritual properties.</note> on an English ship, he pretended to be vehemently captured by love for him. He dealt with that wretched man in such a way that the sailor finally sold himself to the Jew for 300 pounds, thinking that he would later escape secretly from his master when a desired opportunity arose. ### SECTION TWO, BOOK II. Part II.

After the ship had been outfitted, the remaining sailors, wishing to say goodbye to their captive comrade before they departed, hurried to the house of a certain Jew. After they had requested to see their friend one last time for the sake of bidding him farewell, the man led them into a square courtyard that looked directly out into the burning sun. There, they looked on with great amazement at that **red-haired man** <note>In early modern folklore, red hair (ruffus) was often associated with a choleric temperament or even betrayal, linked to figures like Judas Iscariot.</note>, whose back had been broken and a piece of wood wedged between his teeth. His jaws and throat were horribly swollen because (as was later reported to them) vipers had been forced into his mouth to bite and wound him. He was suspended facing the sun, and a silver bowl had been placed beneath his mouth to catch the liquid dripping from him. From this liquid, that Jew later concocted a human poison so lethal that it could kill men by mere contact. It is said that the Jew sold this substance for an incalculable price to certain merchants.

A similar preparation of poison was reported to me by a certain pharmacist of the Papal court at **Avignon**, and I have since had it confirmed by the testimony of others living in **Rome**. A certain Cardinal (he said) had a red-haired mistress who had become pregnant by him. After she gave birth to the child, he buried her in the earth up to her breasts and applied two vipers (or as a German source reported, two hungry toads) to her nipples, whose venomous bites heavily infected her blood. This done, she was suspended facing the sun in the manner described before, and she yielded a most lethal liquid. Furthermore, the milk later found in the bellies of the toads was so contagious that nothing could surpass it. 

The reason why a more destructive poison is extracted from a red-haired person is that, from their birth, such people are subject to **Solar influences** and are consequently more liable to corruption and putrefaction. Thus it happens that when their <term>Spiritual Mummia</term> <note>Fludd uses "Mummia" to refer to the vital life-force or "balsam" that resides in a living body and remains for a time after death.</note> is contaminated by animal venom, it becomes exceedingly subtle, penetrating, and malicious after its fermentation and rotting. And although there remains in the infected Mummia a **Sympathetic** desire to be joined with its own "Like," nevertheless, because it is infected and intoxicated by the **Antipathetic** <note>Sympathy and Antipathy are the two Great Forces in Fludd's philosophy—the "pull" of love and the "push" of hate/discord.</note> spirit of the venomous beast which now dominates it, it cannot embrace its "Like" in a sympathetic way. Instead, by its antipathetic addition, it contaminates the healthy spirit similar to itself; thus, that foreign and heterogeneous poison converts both spirits into its own destructive nature.

There was a certain Hermit living near **Aix-en-Provence** (whose fame was widespread at the time I lived there recently) who, with a similar poisonous "filter," infected that whole city with a most desperate plague. So great was the destruction that a large portion of the people of that city were deprived of life. During the height of this contagion, if the Hermit was called to anyone, it was in his power alone

<column-break/>

to heal them, and for this reason, he acquired the name of the "Holy Hermit." For he had touched the door-knockers or handles of the houses in the city with a certain poison, such that whoever knocked on the doors would be killed; yet he himself carried an **Antidote** with him, by which he used to restore the contaminated to their former state of health. This diabolical man was finally discovered and paid the heaviest penalties for his crimes: for after various tortures, he was finally reduced to ashes by fire. 

By similar cunning or sorcery, the plague was introduced not long ago into the city of **Turin** in Piedmont by certain pestiferous persons, who were like devils incarnate. They also paid the price for their crime, for when the deed was discovered, their flesh was torn away and mangled with red-hot pincers. So also was the plague ignited in the city of **Milan** by the scattering of a certain poisonous powder. From these examples, it is clear that by such wicked and impious inventions, the internal spirits of men are corrupted, and the external air remains in some way polluted by the poison.

Nor should this appear strange to the true **Naturalist** or worthy **Philosopher**, since it is proven by experience that healthy air can be reduced to a corrupt and contagious state by the venomous breath of the South Wind (**Auster**). Even air that was pure and unpolluted can be defiled and rendered poisonous by the breath of a person suffering from the plague, or by the exhalation of a pestiferous carbuncle or "anthrax" <note>referring to the physical sores or boils of the plague</note>. That corrupted air will then simultaneously corrupt the healthy air neighboring it. 

Let us observe, I pray, how the infected spirit of a person defiled by the plague, or smallpox, or measles, or consumption (**Phthisis**), or eye-infections (**Ophthalmia**), can infect the spirit of a healthy man at a considerable distance. Consider also how the spirits of lepers, epileptics, and those with the **French Disease** <note>Syphilis</note> are accustomed to do the same through immediate contact. We find that what was created for health in man has now become contaminated and poisonous through evil arrangement. 

What shall I say then? Should we conclude from this that we must leave or desert our nature because it is sometimes contaminated by evil and rendered lethal to us? Or should we judge human nature to be abominable and to be shrunk from by the light itself, simply because sorcerers and enchanters (with the Devil teaching them) use flesh, hair, nails, excrements, and blood—and even the **Mummia** itself, both corporal and spiritual—to perform their incantations, potions, and sorceries? That this is indeed the case, we find confirmed not only by the testimony of history but also by the daily practice of witches. For **Apuleius** <note>A 2nd-century Roman author known for 'The Golden Ass', a story of magic and transformation.</note> narrates how his girlfriend, Fotis, was used by her mistress (who was an enchantress of potions and

Furthermore, it is a common practice for *Necromancers* <note>Those who practice magic involving the dead.</note> to visit the sepulchers of the dead, either to carry away a portion of the corpse, or to steal some part of the linen cloth in which the bodies are wrapped, or even bits of the chest or coffin in which they are buried. They do this because the **Spiritual Mummia** <term>Mummia: In Paracelsian philosophy, this refers to the vital life-force or "balsam" that remains in a body or its parts even after death or separation.</term> still clings to these objects, which they use to complete their wicked business or works. She then acknowledged that, by means of that glove, she gained dominion over the girl's body. And the reason for this was the connection that the **Spiritual Mummia** of the maiden—which had soaked into the substance of the glove via the vehicle of her sweat—maintained with her living body. This is no different from how the spirit in a wounding weapon relates to the spirit of the wounded person; just as the spirit in the weapon is affected by heat or cold, so too is the spirit of the wounded person affected. This is also apparent when a weapon or iron that has been covered is accidentally uncovered; the wound becomes more painful and disturbed by the cold. And when, for the sake of an experiment, some ointment is scraped or removed from the weapon, that portion of the wound corresponding to the scraped part will be affected by pain and disturbance. In exactly the same way, sorceresses are accustomed to apply their wicked and ruinous poison to the *Mummia* found in a glove, a shoe, a shirt, dry linen, and similar items, through which they effect their malice from a great distance. We also read in books treating *Cacomagic* how highly the limbs of infants are esteemed among such sorcerers and enchanters, and especially their skin or hide, from which, after various **Diabolical** and **Necromantic** preparations, they attempt to create their "virgin parchment." On these, they are accustomed to inscribe the names of God and the Angels whom they invoke, as well as the characters of the **Planets** or **Stars** to which those Angels belong. Should, therefore, for that reason, the magnetic

<column-break/>

effect of human nature, or its **Spiritual Mummia** and similar things in man, be considered Diabolical and damnable, simply because their mystery is revealed in an evil sense to witches by the Devil, and their secret properties are converted to an impious and least-Christian use? Should the air be refused and repudiated by us because it can be corrupted in ruinous ways and modes and converted into a lethal poison? Or is fire to be excluded from human society and regarded as damnable because, when badly applied, it is known to destroy and consume? On the contrary, if it is rightly applied, it brings nourishment and comfort to those nearby. If, by the contamination or change of one *Mummia* into a contagious or poisonous disposition, another healthy one is infected—just as we see one person infected by a plague affect another at a distance, and one house set on fire ignite another, even if they are not touching—should, I ask, the use of either air or fire be banished into exile from human society for this reason? Or is the fire of God descending from heaven to be abhorred because **Satan** made use of it in a destructive sense, namely to consume the possessions of **Job**? Or should it be said that the hidden property of the **Spiritual Mummia**, and the admirable efficacy of the human spirit in healthy and pious uses, is to be repudiated because it can be converted into a poisonous disposition by corruption? Or is a good sword, ordained for the protection of the body, to be rejected or broken because a wicked man killed a good man with it? A good thing badly applied can bring harm. The influence and light of the celestial **Sun**, in which the breath of life is situated, is observed to produce mostly wicked effects if it is poorly received by a terrestrial subject. Indeed, the Devil himself observes the statutes of the year and the solar cycles, and yet neither the Sun nor any of its virtues or acts ought to be considered Diabolical. In a plainly similar way, if we descend from the animal sphere to the vegetable and mineral spheres, we will perceive that the famous sorceress or enchantress **Medea** <note>The mythological sorceress from the story of Jason and the Argonauts, famous for her use of magical herbs.</note> made special use in her incantations (as is also recorded of other sorcerers and necromancers) of herbs, stones, and minerals. Without the help of these natural things, neither she nor her Demon—who revealed their secret virtues and effects to her—could perform anything in their art to achieve their iniquitous desires. And for that reason (as we gather from **Ovid** <note>The Roman poet Ovid, specifically in his *Metamorphoses*, describes Medea gathering herbs on mountains.</note>), she wandered the high peaks of Mount **Aeta** so that she might collect herbs serving her purpose there. There are many magi who, through the hidden property and virtue of stones revealed to them by the Devil, produce their *Cacomagical* effects, even though they themselves [use] the influences of the **Stars**, which...

For example, there was a certain sorceress or wise woman in **Scotland**, who confessed in her examination that by a certain hidden property of a stone, which had been taken from her at that time, she was able to resolve any question. For she said that if the matter asked were true, the stone would immediately emit **sweat**; but if it were false, then no sweat would appear. She also said that this stone revealed many things to her through its change from color to color. Finally, when several bystanders desired an experiment concerning this matter, she replied that she would willingly do it, provided they would grant her that stone of hers. But they, fearing lest by its help she might escape from their hands, utterly denied her this petition. This event took place at **Queens Ferry** in Scotland. 

Others are instructed by the **Devil** to choose some metal, prepare it under a certain suitable constellation, and engrave on it the characters of the **Star** to which it is subject, and describe the name of the **Angel** or **Intelligence** who is the Lady of that Star. They attempt this especially at the time when that Star is stronger and more powerful in the heavens and more free from the impediments of other planets; and then they find that such metallic plates are very effective in magical operations. What then? Since the Devil knows the virtues and properties of these natural things and is able to instruct his ministers in their evil use, does it therefore follow that **Adam**, **Solomon**, and the **Wise Men** coming from the East, as well as many other good and pious men, were ignorant of such natural virtues of simples, the times of their selection and collection, and the modes of their application in a good and lawful matter? Nay, even if a just occasion offers itself in the contrary sense, and that without transgression of the limits of nature or lawful magic—since the true subject of that operation is the **Spirit of Wisdom**, which is the basis or foundation of **Natural Philosophy**—what do we make of the manner in which **Moses** used to disperse those ashes, which produced the **Egyptian boils** not without the amazement of the inhabitants? 

But others will reply and say that this was an effect produced in a supernatural way. Yet I would wish them to look into the hidden secrets and mysteries of animal, vegetable, and mineral natures, which are so wonderful and are naturally contained within them, setting aside all suspicion of Diabolical commerce; they will find it so. Is that reverend Father **Albertus Magnus** <note>A 13th-century Dominican friar and polymath often associated with alchemy and natural magic in legend.</note> to be considered a <term>Cacomagus</term><note>original: "Cacomagus"; an evil magician or sorcerer, from the Greek "kakos" (bad) and "magus" (mage).</note> because he uncovered the abstruse, hidden, and mystical virtues of animals, vegetables, and stones? (Hermes, Plato, and other most profound Philosophers did this same thing). Or should these men be numbered among the followers of the Devil because they knew

<column-break/>

the times or hours of collection and the mode of their preparation? Not at all, by **Hercules**! For they received these secrets from the tradition of deep philosophers or wise men, such as **Adam**, **Solomon**, **Hermes**, and other such true <term>Magi</term><note>Wise practitioners of natural magic, distinct from sorcerers.</note>, who left such mysteries to the world through **Cabalistic tradition** from age to age. Was there not a marvelous property in the **Ring of Gyges** <note>A mythical ring mentioned by Plato that granted its wearer invisibility.</note>, which at times rendered him invisible? And yet the men of this world, blinded by ignorance, wish such effects in creatures to proceed from the Devil and not from the miraculous operation of the **Divine Word**. 

Whence they seem to deprive the **Omnipotent Spirit of God** of its honor, even though Solomon confesses in plain words that he received all secrets, the times of selection, and the mystical natures of the **Stars**, and the hidden virtues and properties

> For Wisdom (he says), the fashioner of all things, taught me.

By which words he seems to infer: First, that the **Spirit of Wisdom** detects and opens to man the abstruse mysteries of true **Philosophy**, which consists in the knowledge and revelation of natural virtues, both in the superior and inferior worlds. Second, that it is this same spirit which instilled such virtues into animals, vegetables, and minerals from below, and works through them in all things. 

Since this is so, what, I ask, can the **Devil** do in creating essential virtues to perpetrate his stratagems or crimes more than man himself? Since man is a rational creature just like the Devil? Or why should we attribute to him those things which, in truth, belong to the Spirit that creates all things and works in the internal creature? If it is man’s part to attribute the iniquity of any action to the Devil, who instigates man to evil and shows him the way to execute his evil and wicked wills, this indeed rightly pertains to the Devil himself, who was created to destroy (as the Prophet **Isaiah** says). To fulfill this office of his, creatures created by God come into use for him. For he employed the use of God's heavenly fire to destroy the beasts of **Job**, to overturn the house, to destroy his sons, and to corrupt the air so that he might kill the **Israelites** with that plague because of David's sin. Indeed, it was never observed that he could do anything by himself against man, except by tempting and seducing the human spirit and deluding the human imagination with deceptive portents. But he is always observed, either through the evil use of creatures, to destroy the bodies of mortals or to render them unhealthy and diseased. <meta>This page continues Robert Fludd’s discussion on the mechanics of magic and natural philosophy. Having previously discussed how sorcerers use the "Mummia" or vital spirit, he now argues that even the most "diabolical" magic relies on the physical properties of natural substances—poisons, herbs, and minerals—rather than purely supernatural power. He compares the "black" stage of alchemy to these poisons and concludes that evil resides in the misuse of God's good creation.</meta>

# CONCERNING MOSAIC PHILOSOPHY.

## BOOK II. PART II.

...working through the condition of the thing, which is contrary to being affected by evil, even though God created such "Antipathizing" creatures for the more healthy and direct use of man. I conclude, therefore, that it is necessary that evil mages <term>Cacomagi; from the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'magos' (magician)</term> and poisoners are unable to impose any evil upon anyone unless they work through a real and manifest substance of a creature, such as powders, ointments, herbs, and the like. For example: <margin>Nicolaus Remigius, *On Demonolatry*, Book 1. <note>The text reads "Pennigius," but refers to the famous witch-hunter Nicolaus Remigius.</note></margin> *Claudea Fellea, Joan Bannio,* and *Nichola the Fisherwoman*, along with their entire society, confessed in Lorraine on May 9, 1581, that powders of a triple condition—distinguished even by color—had been delivered to them by the Devil. For (they say) that **black powder** kills when sprinkled over food, or by rubbing it on the body, or by sprinkling it on clothing. But the **red-colored powder** produces diseases and infirmities. The **white powder**, however, is accustomed to cure those diseases which the red one produced. And *Odella Boncuriona*, examined on January 18, 1586, said it was the custom for poisoners of her order and condition to scatter a certain powder on the path where those they pursued with hatred would walk. And *Francisca Perine* confessed on November 4, 1588, that a certain herb was given to her by the Devil to be placed in the path where *Riberianus* would go (because he had stolen her pears), by whose virulence he immediately fell ill. *Franciscus Follers, Margarita Warny,* and *Jacobit Equine* confessed on January 15, 1584, that they possessed ointments with which they smeared rods and whips, so that if they touched only the garment of someone with them, it was necessary that the person die shortly thereafter. They also said that if they anointed their own hands with this **Magical ointment**, and touched someone's clothes, that person would die within a few days. And from these examples you can see how the Devil does not know how to work evil in reality except by poisons alone taken from creatures. For nothing of truth can proceed from him alone, but mere delusions and deceptive apparitions—namely those things which are seen and yet, in the reality of the effect, are nothing more than a painted image in respect to a true substance. And therefore, I would not wish the ministers of the Devil to boast that such wonders in nature arise from the Devil’s mere invention or his act alone. For true Alchemists testify from their own experience and practice that their matter, when it remains in **putrefaction** <note>The 'nigredo' or black stage of the alchemical process, associated with death and decay.</note> and acquires a jet-black color, is more poisonous than a **Tyrian Serpent**, and consequently kills instantly; wherefore they warn practitioners to beware of its fumes. But when, in the process of cooking, it appears between redness and whiteness, it keeps the sufferer between death and health, and thereby reduces them to a diseased state. Yet in the act of its **whiteness**, which signifies perfection in maturity, it cures infirmities and prevents that malice which the black powder induced. Thus,

<column-break/>

it may be seen that the Devil cannot elicit more from the mysteries of nature than what has been given to the human race to know. Again, regarding the scattering of such deadly powder through the streets of **Milan**, it is recorded that this occurred in the year 1629. As for the lethal ointment, which is accustomed to kill by touch alone, the Jew and the Cardinals previously mentioned composed this so that they might violate the creatures of God just as Devils do. And again, this was carried out in an impious manner by a Hermit, who infected the door handles with them (as was said), and he even carried his own **Antidote** <term>Alexipharmacum; a Greek-derived term for a remedy against poison</term> with him, just as the Devil and his evil-magician disciples do. From these things, therefore, you can see that a man endowed with an impious mind or soul, and inclined toward harming the good creatures of God, is just as prone as the Devil to turn herbs, animals, and minerals away from that true purpose for which they were created by God—namely, to be turned toward human benefit. Wherefore he may deservedly be numbered among the Devils, and distinguished by the name of an **"Incarnate Devil,"** because he, clothed in flesh and bone, finds many ways of destroying and killing by poison without the help of the Devil—no differently than the spiritual Devil, who is destitute of flesh and bone.

I conclude, therefore, that there is great absurdity and madness in worldly unbelievers, who with such rashness and audacity take the hidden and secret wonders of God in his creatures to be the inventions and actions of the Devil, and publish this to the world—even if their effects are pernicious to us, and much more so when they are good and health-giving, as is that **Weapon Salve** <term>Unguentum armarium; a controversial "sympathetic" ointment believed to heal a wound by being applied to the weapon that caused it</term>. For it is known not only to God himself, but also to men enjoying true intellect, that it is a creature (animal, vegetable, or mineral) that produces unhealthy and mournful effects through abuse, yet produces good ones in their due and appropriate faculty, which was originally ordained by God for the benefit and health of the human race. For God created all creatures good, and consequently for good uses; but it is the malice of the Devil that diverts them from the purpose ordained by the Creator, according to that saying of **Solomon**: *God created all things that they might exist, and he made the nations of the world healthy, and there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor is there a kingdom of the underworld upon the earth; and he created man imperishable and made him in the image of his own likeness, but by the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world, etc.* <margin>Wisdom 1; Wisdom 2:24.</margin> For it should be known that before the fall of **Adam**, all things were taken directly and justly, and therefore were not twisted at all from the true path. But after he had tasted of the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**, his bodily eyes were opened, and creatures were distinguished as much for evil as for good, and were converted to both uses. For from that hour, the mystery of both iniquity and justice...

### SECTION II, BOOK II. Member II.

...began to reign in the world, and evil first began to oppose itself to goodness and virtue at the very entrance, or threshold, of the world after the Fall. In that primordial practice or conflict, injustice and vice prevailed against justice and virtue. Here, therefore, we can see that in the beginning of all things, the Devil—or the serpent—was able to establish the foundation of all evil through a natural thing, namely the apple. And thereafter, by a wooden club, the unjust Cain slew his just brother Abel; whereas, on the other hand and in a contrary sense, this wood, in the form of a cross (signifying that opposition which was made in this world between good and evil), was the instrument of death itself, without which there was no certainty of salvation or redemption.

From these things, we perceive that all hidden operations proceed from a virtue hidden in natural things or creatures. This virtue was revealed by the Divine Spirit of God to humankind, just as it was grasped by the sharp observation of Satan. To good men, I say, it was revealed by the good Spirit of God for the purpose of doing good and resisting evil. For unless the perverse disposition of a creature is known, an <term>alexipharmacon; a remedy or antidote against poison</term> for its cure can hardly be obtained. Yet, these things are also sometimes revealed to the wicked by the Devil for the purpose of doing harm and executing iniquity. I shall now enumerate some of the abstruse virtues in the three kingdoms of composite creatures: namely the animal, vegetable, and mineral. First, then, in the animal kingdom, the owl is said by Albertus Magnus <note>Albert the Great (c. 1200–1280), a prolific medieval philosopher and theologian noted for his writings on natural history.</note> to contain many virtues within itself. For, he says, if its heart and right foot are placed upon a sleeping man, he will immediately reveal in his sleep whatever he has done, or whatever you might ask of him. He says this was found to be true by certain of his brothers. And again, if these same parts are placed under the armpit, no dog will dare to bark at him. Also, the blood of a goat is said to render glass not only <term>malleable; capable of being hammered or pressed into shape without breaking</term> but even soft like paste, provided the glass is boiled in it with vinegar; so much so, that if it is thrown against a wall, it will not break. And if anyone makes an ointment of the same composition and smears his face with it, terrible things will appear to him. And if a portion of that composition is placed on a fire, and someone is present who suffers from <term>Epilepsy; the "falling sickness," often treated with occult remedies in this period</term>, and a magnet touches him, he will suddenly fall into an epileptic seizure, as if dead; but if cold water is given to him to drink, he will immediately rise again. So says Albertus. Furthermore, he says that if a candle is smeared with the blood of a camel, all the men in that place will seem to be imbued with the heads of camels. And so he proceeds in that history of his with descriptions of those wonders which are effected by the hidden properties of beasts, vegetables,

<column-break/>

and stones. If Master Foster <note>William Foster (1591–1643), an English parson and critic of Fludd who argued that the weapon-salve was magical and demonic.</note> with his companions shall reply and say that all these things are nothing but lies, I answer that a most learned philosopher and a theologian celebrated in fame was their author, who passed these things down on his own faith. No doubt (if he were still surviving among the living), he would affirm that they ought first to learn and understand the true <term>election hours; the specific times chosen through astrology for gathering ingredients</term> in which those simple substances must be collected, and also to know the stars which have dominion over them, along with the times of their greater strength and exaltation in the heavens. As for what pertains to me, I confess that I am not ignorant of the wonderful secrets in man and beasts, for all of which the <term>Peripatetics; followers of Aristotle's philosophy, who Fludd argues cannot explain these hidden forces</term> can clearly give no sufficient reason. For example: that the dried intestines of a pike fish powerfully provoke urine; that epilepsy can be cured by the flow or attraction of blood from the severed nose of a mole, and that after swallowing that blood the patient will be exceedingly sick (just as we are taught by the experience of several people, and among the rest, by a certain most noble lady of the county of Kent). Also, that a burnt mole reduced to powder has a certain hidden virtue for expelling the pain of colic; that the heart and liver of a frog is a medicine appropriated for the cure of epilepsy; that the sloughed skins of snakes expel the birth in women; that the menstrual blood in a woman, if drunk, induces leprosy; that a burnt toad stops blood flowing excessively; as does also a live spider, if it is applied to the nostrils. All these things I, along with many others, have experienced for myself.

As for other hidden virtues of stones, metals, herbs, and animals, the disciples and imitators of the true Solomon—Hermes, Plato, Thebit, Albertus Magnus, Dioscorides, and others—teach them to us abundantly. All of these men, without a doubt, would not seem so foolish and empty of truth and frivolous as to publish such huge lies or such great impossibilities to the world, nor would they falsely assert that those things had been brought to a conclusion within their knowledge. They would not, in such a stupid manner, lose that reputation among worldly men which they earned for themselves by their distinguished wisdom. But now I shall betake myself to the practice of this fuller business of ours: namely, to that **Sympathetic** and **Antipathetic** respect which exists between the various types of **Mummies** <note>In Fludd's context, "Mummia" or "Mummy" refers to the vital spirit or "balsam" remaining in a body (living or dead) that carries its life force.</note> of the human body, and the ocular demonstration produced by the property of the **Magnet**. It is my intent to prove to you, by demonstrating in this last book, more than anyone else has ever achieved until this day.

### *The Author’s Preface to this present book, in which those things which were said before are briefly reviewed.*

I have recounted to you in my preceding discourse, and proven with sufficient demonstration, that the Spiritual Christ—or the Divine Word, or Eternal Wisdom—is the true foundation and essential basis of Philosophy. For He is the secure and never-failing Cornerstone, in whom and upon whom the entire creation consists and is built, insofar as life exists in Him; and that life is that essential Light which gives life to all things, and consequently works all in all, as the Scripture testifies in express words. For, if the Spirit of the Lord imparts life and inspiration and all things of life to the creature; and again, if that Spirit fills the orb of the earth and is present in every single thing of this world, as Solomon writes; then it is necessary that we acknowledge that the central Spirit of any specific thing is that Divinity, in which consists the essential root of all Magnetic attraction and Antipathetic expulsion.

For, since He is that Universal Love <note>Latin: *Catholicus ille amor*</note> who imparts Himself to every particular existence and assigns to it action and motion, by which it may allure a nature similar to itself toward itself—for the sake of nutrition, assistance, and consolation—He likewise makes the organ in which He works strong and valid enough to expel and drive away such emanations that disagree with it, whether in order, quality, or essence, or which oppose its specific existence and conservation, or attempt to bring it some harm.

For that reason, therefore, this Spirit endowed the creature with a double affection: namely, a concupiscible desire <note>The "concupiscible" faculty is the soul's power to seek out what is perceived as good or pleasurable.</note> and an irascible hatred <note>The "irascible" faculty is the soul's power to resist or flee from what is perceived as harmful or evil.</note>. The former of these rejoices with and tends to sympathize with its like, and therefore allures and attracts it to itself for its own assistance and consolation; the latter, through a hateful or Antipathetic aspect, avoids and expels that which is opposite or harmful to its nature. 

And this is the act of that Wisdom which creates and sustains all things, which created every creature with a certain successive preservation, which it attracts from its like so that it may exist in this world; and consequently, He also granted it the irascible faculty, so that it might fortify and defend itself against things contrary to it in nature. By these things we can see how this Spirit, which gives life to all, governs with a hand that is by no means sparing; so much so that, although He created all things through opposition—namely light and darkness, and therefore in human respect good and evil—He nevertheless ordained and disposed it so that every individual should be endowed with the irascible faculty and with Antipathetic hatred to avoid and flee from evil (that is, things adverse to it either in order, or nature, or both), until that time is fulfilled in which, after His exaltation, He shall have cleared away all contrariety and discord from both worlds through the establishment of a firm union. 

This is also what St. Paul seems to confirm: *When he shall have abolished all rule and all authority and power, he must reign, until he has put all enemies under his feet.* But the last enemy 
<margin>1 Corinthians 15.</margin>
to be destroyed is death, for He has put all things under His feet. But when all things shall be subjected to Him, then the Son Himself shall also be subjected to Him who put all things under

...to Him all things, so that God may be all in all <note>original: *ut sit Deus, omnia in omnibus*; a reference to 1 Corinthians 15:28</note>, etc. This universal **Magnetic virtue** <note>Fludd uses "magnetic" to describe a spiritual force of attraction and repulsion that governs the universe, not just physical magnets.</note> is recognized by the Spirit, in Christ, <margin>John 12.</margin> from those words: *If I be lifted up from the earth, I will draw all things to myself* <note>John 12:32</note>, etc. As if He had said: I, by my attractive and Magnetic virtue and union, shall bring back all things into my union and identity; that is, I shall bring them into my own proper nature. <margin>Revelation.</margin> *Behold* (says the Text elsewhere), *I make all things new* <note>Revelation 21:5</note>, etc. By these words it is clear that, just as in the beginning all things arose from one—being implicitly contained within Him—and then afterwards, in their explicit existence, were held under two contrary Principles; so indeed in the end all things held under these discordant Principles shall be brought back into one and the same radical Principle. 

But for now, we are still subject to contrary Principles: For the whole world, along with its members, is composed of strife and concord, of enmity and friendship, of darkness and light, of good and evil; and for that reason they exist under the protection of this one Divine Wisdom, which governs all things and strives to have victory over confusion and discord. This is so that at last, peace and union—or a universal consensus—might be achieved in this world, and consequently, that all things might return into her, live in her, and be united with her, who is the one and only **Charity** <note>original: *Charitas* (Divine Love)</note>. The creature itself has the power to effect a symphonic agreement <note>original: *consensum Symphoniacum*</note> with its like, and conversely, through an irascible or <term>Antipathetic</term> <note>Antipathy refers to a natural repulsion or "dislike" between certain spirits or substances.</note> property, to either avoid or repel its contrary with its greatest effort.

Now, since this Spirit is in all things, and therefore in every specific thing, it follows consequently that it attracts <term>Sympathetically</term> <note>Sympathy refers to a natural attraction or "affinity" between substances of the same nature.</note> that which preserves its nature and condition in any specific thing from the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms; and it expels **Antipathetically** from itself that which is harmful, hateful, and detestable, or is contrary to its disposition. Thus ends the summary of my preceding Theory of Sympathy and Antipathy. 

Now, I shall immerse myself for a short while in the practice of both, so that by this reasoning you may be more easily led to believe that such things which were previously put forward by us theoretically are effective, and that a real practice can be produced gently (contrary to the vain opinion of certain ignorant men of this world) and naturally—that is, without any <term>Cacomagic</term> <note>original: *Cacomagica*; from the Greek *kakos* (evil) and *magia* (magic). Fludd is distinguishing his natural philosophy from "black magic."</note> or Diabolical operation. I shall proceed, therefore, to my purpose, and so that I may move forward more methodically, I shall distinguish this book into two different members: the first of which will treat Sympathetic effects; the second will briefly explain those Antipathetic outcomes which are produced **Magnetically** in the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms.

Since it is a matter worthy of observation among the wise that there is nothing in the celestial kingdom that does not have its likeness in the terrestrial one, so indeed there is nothing in the mineral kingdom that does not enjoy its likeness in the vegetable kingdom. And again, the image of the vegetable sphere—whether in love and hate, or in attraction and avoidance, or in union and divorce—is to be found in the animal. 

But, because in the mineral kingdom nothing is found closer in the virtue of action and life to animals than the <term>Magnet stone</term> <note>The lodestone or natural magnet.</note> itself, insofar as it sensibly affects its iron likeness, and pursues it with a desirable love, and greedily attracts it, and finally joins and unites with it in a marvelous way—just like male and female in the animal kingdom—for this reason, every likeness in the animal or vegetable kingdom that operates in this manner (namely, by attracting its own likeness) is not wrongly called "Magnetic." 

From this, Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a famous Swiss physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of minerals in medicine.</note>, who was most skilled in mysteries of this kind, when he mentions mystical <term>Mummies</term> <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Mummia" refers to the vital life-force or spiritual balsam residing in a body, not a preserved corpse.</note>, both bodily and spiritual, and also the active ways and means to extract them from both the living and the dead body, he himself—for the better instruction of his disciples and those whom he calls "sons of art"—brings forth examples taken from the Magnet stone and iron. For through these, he denotes the method of extracting such Mummies clearly enough; and consequently, in his own way, he explains what the animal and <term>microcosmic Magnet</term> <note>The "microcosm" is the human being, viewed as a miniature version of the universe (the macrocosm).</note> is, by means of which the microcosmic Mummy is drawn out of its body. 

He explains, namely, that it is a certain bodily thing or substance, as it is right to gather from these words of his: *The Spiritual Mummy* (he says) *does not work, except through bodily means.* By which he argues for bodily modes, or those Magnetic bodies, which are accustomed to extract this Mummy from the body of a living animal, and cause it to work both at home through immediate contact, and elsewhere and at a distance; indeed, even at an unknown

<column-break/>

interval, and that by means of a proper <term>transplantation</term> <note>The theory that a disease or a vital spirit could be "transplanted" from a human into a plant or another medium to effect a cure.</note>. He, therefore, who is wise and deep in the mysteries of nature, and to whom the sympathetic agreement, the hidden property, nature, virtue, and origin of the Magnet and iron are well known, will acknowledge without doubt that their examples can be most aptly compared to man. 

For through these, one can most easily discern the microcosmic Magnet, and understand the reason for the extraction of the Spiritual Mummy from man, and at the same time conceive of its use and purpose destined for human health. Therefore, so that these things may be better expanded and explained to the reader, I think it worthwhile first to strike that same string of symphonic concord which concerns the nature and origin of the Magnet stone and iron (which I touched upon a little more fully in my preceding book), so that from there we may gather with greater ease who the microcosmic Magnets are.

## BOOK II.

...is seated, the **sulphureous spirit of life** <note>original: "Spiritus vitæ sulphureus"; in Fludd’s alchemy, sulphur represents the active, fiery, and formal principle of life.</note> is observed to contract itself from the circumference <note>the outer edges of the body or skin</note> toward the center; for this reason, a bloodless paleness or a yellow-livid hue is noted to take over the outward appearance of the face and the entire body. Indeed, a backward motion of these Spirits of this kind is **Antipathetic** <term>Antipathetic: A force of repulsion or hostility, the opposite of Sympathy.</term> and is caused by a passion contrary to nature. Conversely, once those Sulphureous Spirits have gained their liberty, they dilate and expand themselves into the open air; this is because they have no obvious Magnet to attract them toward a center or to contract them into a narrower place.

We conclude, therefore, that the **microcosmic Magnet** must go forth from, or have its origin in, the microcosmic sulphureous Spirit within its own **salt** (in which its form consists) and from a more foreign and alien **Mercury**. Because of its nearness and proximity, this Mercury is more familiar in its service to the spirit, and is bound to it as if by acquisition. This Mercury is the passive matter of this Magnet. Therefore, from these two portions of the living Microcosm—namely the formal <note>the active, shaping principle</note> and the material—our Magnet is drawn out. By its mediation, the **Spiritual Mummy** <term>Mummy (Mummia): Not an Egyptian corpse, but the "vital balsam" or life-essence found in living or recently deceased tissue, believed to have healing powers.</term> is extracted from a living man. By the help and action of this essence, wonderful cures as well as ruinous damage can be performed, both at a distance and through immediate contact. Furthermore, that internal Magnet, or attractive salt within man—in whose interior the vivifying Sulphureous Spirit has its seat, and from whose condition and root our aforementioned Magnet

<column-break/>

arises—can provide the same health-giving effects, as well as many other rare experimental conclusions. This occurs if it is transferred from a living person—either in the **Blood**, the **nails**, or the **hair** of a living man—and is transplanted in the proper manner, and this through a certain insensible outflowing.

There is also another microcosmic Magnet which is taken from the corpse of a dead man. By its help, the Spiritual Mummy can be drawn from a living man and can contribute to human health, both by immediate application and by transplanting it into a vegetable—namely into a herb or a tree—as will be stated more clearly below. But, since the method and order of these things in our **demonstration *a posteriori*** <note>original: "demonstratione à posteriori"; a logical argument that works backward from observed effects to their original causes.</note> will be very suitable to human understanding, I shall strive in this explanation of mine to ascend from the gross Elements to the more subtle and hidden things; as if I were raising myself little by little by steps of proportion from the earth to the stars. It is my intention, therefore, first to explain and magnetically demonstrate to you those things which are perfected solely by the contact of two bodies of one and the same nature and condition. But, before I begin with that Mummy which is extracted from a dead body, I think it will be necessary, especially in the first place, to hand down something here concerning the **mystery of the human Corpse**, so that we may proceed better and more methodically in what follows.

### SECTION TWO, BOOK III. Member I.

We must hold it as an axiom in general philosophy that the corrupted assumes the nature of its corrupter. For example: if a human cadaver is corrupted in the earth, it then changes and passes into the nature of the earth, and becomes useless for human health. Indeed, it is rendered more destructive than constructive or salutary. Again, if corruption occurs in water, then the corrupted flesh or the dead body, soaked in water, acquires and assumes a mucilaginous <note>slimy or mucus-like</note> nature; and therefore, it will be inconvenient and useless for the conservation of the vital spirits. Finally, by the immoderate violence of fire, the Spirits in the Mummial body <note>original: "corpore Mummiali"; the body as a vessel of vital essence</note> are consumed and will breathe their last. 

Now truly, the reason why these aforementioned bodily Mummies are unsuitable for the protection of health in such a state is because those three elements <note>Earth, Water, and Fire</note> so destroy and corrupt their body that they force its earth, water, and fire to return to their own proper matter. So much so, that since earth and water are ordained to be the receptacles of the two Elements—namely fire and air—both of which can only be preserved in an uncorrupted body, it must necessarily follow that in the three aforementioned Mummies, those vivifying Spirits must fly away and vanish due to the lack of a natural body, which has now become corrupted, putrid, and consequently unnatural. Since, therefore, nothing is required in a true Mummia except that which is fit for the conservation of life—indeed, for the sake of life alone or the Spirit, which is air—and since this air is banished into exile and expelled by the three aforementioned Mummies, therefore nothing can be extracted from them except sickness, death, and destruction, and consequently **Antipathetic** <term>Antipathetic: A force of repulsion or hostility, the opposite of Sympathy or attraction.</term> effects. Thus, if a healthy body that has been killed or suffocated is corrupted under the earth or in the water, it will not be fit or proper for the healthy use of the human body. That same respect must be held for such bodies that die from some infirmity; and although these are not visibly corrupted by the three said external Elements, nevertheless it sometimes happens that a certain invisible, corruptible influence or impression is made or caused by the external Element upon the internal. From this, therefore,

<column-break/>

proceeds that internal war in the human body, by which the Elements kill and corrupt one another, but in a way and reason plainly diverse—namely, differently in one body than in another—according to which one Element or Elemental alteration is said to have Dominion over another. And this is the reason that such a variety of diseases frequents the human body. For example, **Dropsy** <term>Dropsy: Edema, or the buildup of fluid in the body's tissues.</term> proceeds from a strong impression of the waters; **Hectic and burning Fever** arises from fiery things in the pulses; and **leprosy** from the Dominion of the earth and its fixed saltiness, etc. And therefore, wherever such elemental corruption happens to any body, there the Spirit of the Healthful bodily Mummia, along with its habitation or dwelling, is utterly subverted; whence the spirit is also forced to depart, and by consequence, contrary Mummial spirits predominate. These are prepared and fit to work Antipathetically and destructively, just as will be expressed more widely in the second member of this book. 

But truly, if a healthy body, free of infirmity, is killed through or in the Element of air—that is, either by suffocation, hanging, and the like—then no impression of the said corrupting Elements will be found in that cadaver; and for this cause, it will remain uncorrupted, nor will it permit any resolution of the Elements as long as it is reserved in the air. If, therefore, the body or Tabernacle of the spirits and the **vital Balsam** <note>original: "Balsami vitalis"; a hypothetical healing fluid or life-force believed to exist in all living things.</note> remains whole, then the airy Balsam of life will not be compelled to withdraw from its dwelling, so long as the body or cadaver is dissolved neither by nature nor by art. But if it is dissolved, then that dead body leaves as the soul and also the astral Spirit (which reconciled the one with the other) depart; but the vital vegetable and Balsamic Spirit remains in the uncorrupted body. It follows, therefore, that this airy species of **microcosmic Mummia** <note>The vital essence extracted from a human (the microcosm).</note> is most proper for the conservation of the vital spirits in a living man, if it is extracted and prepared in the due manner, and finally applied to the sick by a skilled physician. Now truly, I shall briefly approach our Magnetic experiments pertaining to the mummial subject.

### *An experiment regarding this.*

I myself took or selected a small portion of **Northern Mummia** <note>original: "Mummiæ Borealis"; refers to the flesh of a person who died a "cold" or violent death, often by hanging</note>, namely the flesh of a hanged man, in which the central **Mummia** inhabited centrally. I applied it to a part of my body which was naturally closest in position to the applied **Mummia**. I bound it to the spot firmly enough throughout the night, and found it at first contact to be very cold and frozen like Northern ice. After it had remained there for some time, however, I perceived—by the excitation of its frozen spirits, which were centrally contracted in a Northern manner, by the equinoctial heat of my body—that something of my own Mummial and vivifying spirits was greedily attracted [by it]. The adjacent parts [of my body] were sometimes, as if by turns and fits, sensibly and painfully plucked and contracted in a magnetic operation. Finally, after some time, namely in the morning, I removed that physical **Mummia** of the dead man and found it greatly altered in both smell and color, by reason of the quantity of my spirits which it had attracted. I intended both these spirits, thus gathered into one in a magnetic manner, to be prepared and reserved for the healthy use of my body. However, because perhaps this assertion of mine will appear false to some doubters, I will prove the possibility of every particular part or member of this matter with examples or demonstrations.

## *The first demonstration, made by relation to the microcosmic nature.*

To prove and demonstrate that the **Microcosmic** spirit <note>the human spirit</note> is no less fit than the **Macrocosmic** air <note>the world's atmosphere</note> to take on any polar impression—and is consequently more attractive and **Magnetic** in its Northern or cold property than in its equinoctial or Southern state—we must look at our machine or experimental mirror <note>Fludd is referring to his thermoscope, a precursor to the thermometer, which he used to demonstrate the expansion and contraction of air</note>. And this is clearly proven in it by the fact that when the said winds blow, the internal air (and consequently the external) is more fit for expanding itself, by reason of the emanation of those sulfurous or celestial spirits from the center to the circumference, which are inserted into any of the said airy spirits. For by such emanation, a certain expulsion occurs, or rather an expansion of the airy parts through the rarefaction of their bodies. Therefore, let it be observed in the instrument that while hot winds blow, the water will not rise in the neck of the glass beyond the mark or figure 1, but is rather driven further downward. Conversely, however, when Northern winds blow, the air—which was expanded in the universal element and made more mobile—is condensed by contraction and reduced into immobile snow, ice, and <column-break/> frost. That is, it takes on an earthy condition, so that we see the air in this state is wonderfully contractive. Just as it is depicted to the life in the description of that instrument made in Book 1, Section 1 of this work. I have indicated the reason for this matter in the preceding parts: namely, because the hidden sulfurous nature of the spirit—which is the Sun, the actor of light and life—carried in its airy spirit, avoids the assaults of the cold pursuing it. It remains against the actions of its enemy, with the air around its central seat drawn over and condensed.

In exactly the same way, the cold and frozen spirits of the dead **Mummia**, centrally contracted for the same reason and as if mortified and frozen, [are affected] by the application of that **Mummia** to the spirits of a living body—like cold, Northern air to an Equinoctial or Southern sun. Thus, being excited and called forth by the contact of a living human, they greedily attract the spirits in the living body, as if imploring their help and assistance against their cold enemy. They seem to rejoice in their possession, being fortified and somehow satisfied. That this is so [is shown] by this example...

OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK III. Part I.

...I will most easily prove, by a demonstration taken from the Magnet, in the following manner.

## 2. DEMONSTRATION.

That neither the Spirit in the body of the dead attracts dead Spirits, nor the Spirit in the body of the living attracts living ones to itself Magnetically except very slowly and moderately, is argued in this way from the observation of Magnetic disposition.

### PROBLEM 1.

The South Pole of one Magnet, by a certain natural hatred, avoids the South Pole of another, and they will by no means allow themselves to be joined by the bonds of mutual love: But one, by a natural **Antipathy** <note>In early modern science, "antipathy" described a natural repulsion between objects, the opposite of "sympathy" or attraction</note>, will escape the contact of the other: But indeed, if the North Pole of one is applied to the South Pole of the other, they will embrace each other by a natural inclination, and cling to each other with a strong attraction.

->*For example.*<-

Take a Magnetic Stone <note>a lodestone</note>, with its poles clearly identified and marked both South and North; place it in a small boat made of cork, or let it float in a basin or tub filled with water so that the poles are positioned correctly toward the plane of the Horizon, or at least not much elevated or slanted. Hold another stone in your hand, whose poles are also known: Position it so that its South Pole is toward the North pole of the floating stone near its side: For immediately the floating stone follows the stone in your hand (as long as it remains within its strength and domain), and does not stop or leave until it adheres: Unless, by withdrawing your hand, you cautiously avoid the union. Likewise also, if you oppose its North pole;

<column-break/>

<margin>William Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, Book 1, Chapter 5.</margin>
<margin>Mark Ridley, *Treatise on the Magnet*, Chapters 22 & 24.</margin>
Which you hold in your hand, to the South pole of the floating stone, they run together and mutually follow one another: For contrary poles entice contraries. Now indeed, if you oppose North to North and South to South in the same way, stone puts stone to flight; it turns it away just as a sailor driving a boat with an oar diverts it, and it sails away in the opposite direction, plowing the waters, nor does it stand still or rest anywhere if the other pursues: For stone disposes stone, one turns the other, brings it into order, and leads it into its own harmonies. This is according to Gilbert <note>William Gilbert (1544–1603) was Queen Elizabeth I’s physician and the author of the first great scientific work on magnetism</note> in Book 1, Chapter 5 of *On the Magnet*, with whom Ridley <note>Mark Ridley (1560–1624), another English physician who wrote extensively on magnetic experiments</note> agrees in Chapters 22 and 24 of his magnetic treatise, by arranging two stones skillfully in their vessels or small boats in this manner.
<margin>Ridley, Page 75.</margin>

### 5. A Relative Demonstration of Animal Magnetism.

A certain nobleman, called the Burgrave of Bohemia, used this kind of medicine for the cure of his gout <note>Latin: *podagra*</note>: He took a portion of raw beef and moistened it with a little wine, and applied it to the affected area, renewing this medicine every six hours. It extracted a great quantity of foul and filthy matter; and if a dog should afterwards eat that meat, it would also be infected with the same disease and become lame, as was proven upon two dogs belonging to that nobleman. As Hans Tanker, a minister or priest, asserted to Baron Lord Hoffman; and he himself acknowledges that he saw with his own eyes the effect upon another dog. If, therefore, that coarse mass of matter <column-break/> could have attracted to itself so strongly in its simple nature, our faith ought much more to be founded or placed upon the more spiritual and airy "Mummy," or Mummial Magnet, such as that extracted from a living man in the manner cited before. I have described this not so openly, but only by reference to the "monstrous" generation of the Magnet, so that it might be understood by the wise and pious, and not at all by the foolish, malevolent, impious, and devils incarnate; for by its mediation, as much evil can be committed as good can be performed. I also know as a proven fact <note>Latin: *pro re experta*</note> that epilepsy <note>Latin: *Epilepsiam*</note> was transferred in a similar way from a servant of the sister of Sir Robert Cotton <note>A famous English antiquarian and bibliophile (1570–1631)</note> to a dog, the man remaining free from it thereafter.

### 6. A Demonstration also involving an Animal.

It is held as a supreme remedy in the plague <note>Latin: *peste*</note> when a carbuncle <note>A painful, pus-filled boil associated with the plague</note> appears: if we apply a dried toad macerated in vinegar to the tumor or affected area. For that topical medicine is said to vividly attract the poison of the disease to itself. This has been proven quite often, and can undoubtedly be proven with successful results by anyone infected. The reason, however, is because the toad is magnetically attractive and styptic <term>styptic: a substance that contracts tissues to stop bleeding</term>, partly in respect to its cold and even Northern <note>Latin: *Borealis*; Fludd associates the North with cold, death, and contraction</note>, dull, heavy, and melancholic disposition, and partly because it is observed to stop blood. Thus, that coarse and earthly poisonous Magnet performs its duty in attracting poison from a carbuncle similar to itself, <column-break/> although not as subtly and spiritually as that Elementary or Northern airy Mummy does from a living person or one of a Southern <note>Latin: *australis*; associated with warmth and life</note> nature.

I could recite to you the natures of many vegetables which have the property of alluring and attracting to themselves, provided they are applied to the soles of the feet or the pulses of the arms in febrile imbalances <note>fevers</note>. But since such a work will perhaps seem tedious to you, leaving that aside, I shall proceed to the second degree in the magnetic power of Mummies, which also regards things at a distance—indeed, even at an unknown length—and that by means of a spiritual attraction in the air, as explained more broadly in the following chapter.

OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK III. Member I.

### 1. An experiment confirming the stated proposition.

A certain Italian nobleman had the misfortune of having his nose cut off and amputated. On the advice of his physician, he ordered a wound to be made in the arm of a certain servant (or prisoner) of his. He applied his own mutilated nose directly to this wound and bound it firmly, continuing in this state until a complete union was formed between the flesh of the servant and that of his master. After this, the portion or piece of the servant's flesh adhering to the nose was cut away and reshaped into the form of a nose. The servant's wound was healed by surgeons, and for his pain, patience, and merit, he was not only granted his freedom but also received a reward—namely, a good portion of money. He then made his way toward Naples, which was a city at least one hundred miles from his master's residence.

Now, the flesh adapted to the nose thrived successfully, and it received its nourishment from the veins as long as the servant lived. However, it happened that the freedman died in Naples; whereupon it occurred that the flesh adapted to the nose immediately began to wither and gradually become affected by gangrene. This happened to such a degree that if the nobleman had not cut it off suddenly and without delay, he would undoubtedly have been in danger of death. This account of mine is confirmed as true by many learned men and other trustworthy people; it is commonly publicized among the Italians and was publicly defended in the writings of a certain learned German.

By this history, therefore, we can see that as long as the two bodies that had made contact were of one and the same 

<column-break/>

condition—namely, Southern or Equinoctial <note>In Fludd’s system, "Southern" (*Australis*) refers to the warm, vital, and life-giving quality of the spirit</note>—they operated together by a profound Spiritual Sympathy, even when separated from one another. That is to say, notwithstanding that great distance between them, they were nonetheless present in Spirit, or they met one another through the gaze of sympathetic rays. By this reasoning, the flesh of the one was spiritually animated by the living fountain of the other, not otherwise than a grain of wheat has its nourishment and is brought to life by the application of solar rays to it. 

But when the Southern or Equinoctial property of the one (namely, the servant) was changed into a Northern <note>Latin: *Borealem*; Fludd associates the North with cold, contraction, and death</note>, dead, and cold nature, then the life-giving Spirit within him ceased from its action. That is, it rested from its former application to the adapted flesh. In place of that life-giving gaze, his Spirit—now reduced to a Northern condition—attracted and fled back toward itself that entire nature which its disposition had previously occupied. This occurred in plainly the same way that Northern frost in the world almost kills and, by its Northern and contractive faculty, extracts the life from a grain, seed, plant, or herb. And for that reason, Gangrene (which is a Northern disease) occupied the portion of flesh adapted to the nose. Here, then, we see how the same Spirit, altered from a Southern or Equinoctial to a Northern disposition, operates in a contrary, unnatural, and privative <note>A "privative" action is one that removes or negates a quality, such as cold removing heat</note> manner, doing so secretly and from a great distance.

We see in our "Calendar instrument" <note>An early type of thermoscope or weather-glass used by Fludd to measure atmospheric changes</note> or experimental device described before, that between the head of the glass and the location of the water—namely, through the entire tube of the matrix—there is an invisible airy Spirit. Although this spirit cannot be seen in itself, it nonetheless operates visibly in its effect. For if the external air is quite hot, then the air enclosed in the glass expands; this is clearly demonstrated because the water raised at that time is pushed downward, even though no other visible agent is found. 

Truly, through an intellectual insight, we can discern that this happens by the power of living light in the air—an emanation of Sulfur <note>Fludd refers to the chemical principle of "Sulfur" as the source of heat and light</note>. By the secret emission of its rays, the enclosed air becomes rarefied, and by this rarefaction, it precipitates the water that was drawn up in the tube.

<column-break/>

Conversely, however, in the Northern cold, the water is raised high by reason of the contraction of the emitted Spirits. Thus, we are able to perceive how living emanations—and consequently the acting and life-giving Spirits—are emitted from a living and warm microcosmic fountain to creatures suited for animation and vivification. But if that fountain should become cold and icy, instead of adding Southern life-action, it will produce a deadly and privative distraction. This is also very easily observed in my experimental instrument from the spiritual concurrence—or rather, the invisible and insensible continuity—which is established between both extremes in the instrument.

Even if someone suffering from a fever takes the herb called **Iberis** <note>original: "Iberis"; likely Bitter Candytuft or Pepperwort, which was historically used in folk medicine for sciatica and inflammatory conditions</note>—specifically a handful of it—and places it in their shoes, and walks in this way until they become warm, they will indeed perceive that this herb draws to

### 2. Experiment.

**Johannes Karfmannus** has handed down as a truth that warts on the hands and other parts can be removed by taking straws and cutting the knots in them; he prepares two for each wart, and the straws should be the length of a thumb; then those two sections are to be arranged in this manner

over the wart; so that the knots directly touch the warts: And it is

### 3. Experimental demonstration.

Wondrous things are told concerning the **Chamaeleon** herb <note>original: "herba Chamæleonte"; likely *Carlina acaulis*, the Stemless Carline Thistle, which was thought to have magical strengthening properties</note>: And it was reported to me by a certain German nobleman as a certain fact, and commonly known by very many people, that coachmen on the borders of Bohemia are sometimes accustomed, by means of the Chamaeleon herb, to draw away the strength of other horses and place it into their own: Whence it happens that their horses, in carrying loads, are made far more robust and powerful than they were before: On the other hand, the others become much weaker at sustaining labor: This (he says) happens either by itself, if the herb or rather the root is collected at its proper and convenient hour, or after it

<column-break/>

This author of mine asserted on his faith that he had drawn the strength of another horse by means of this herb, even placing it between the teeth of his own horse in the bridle: But he said he kept a portion of it for himself. This he told on his word, if it be right to believe it.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*How the magnetic method of healing may be proved and demonstrated to be natural, and consequently in no way "Cacomagical" <note>original: "Cacomagica"; referring to "evil magic" or black magic associated with demons</note>, as some who are inconsistent with themselves falsely believe.*<-

To perform this with a better method, we shall express—in our previous manner and as if on the frontispiece of the chapter—the most essential proposition pertaining to this kind of healing; <column-break/> then, afterward, I shall elucidate and clearly demonstrate it with evident proofs derived chiefly from the power of the Magnet <term>magnet: at this time, "magnetic" referred to any force that acted at a distance, including gravity, static electricity, and biological sympathy</term>.
