### PROPOSITION.

If, a break in continuity or a wound having been made, a portion of the shed blood with its Spirits <note>original: "Spiritibus"; in 17th-century medicine, these were the vital, subtle substances that carried life through the body</note> remains on the weapon—or if a portion of the Spirits of that same blood, even without any visible blood, has penetrated the weapon or any other object that probed the depth of the wound—and is transferred to some suitable ointment at some unknown and undetermined distance; and if that ointment's composition is Balsamic <note>restorative or healing</note> and agreeable to the nature of the wounded creature; then, provided it is applied in a proper order and "transplanted" into the ointment, the ointment thus animated by these Spirits will immediately become Magnetic toward the radiant Spirits which shine out from the wound insensibly and invisibly. [This occurs] by the direction of the Blood Spirits in the weapon or other object, which will apply those Spirits by receiving and soaking them up. And the lively and Southern <note>original: "australes"; Fludd associates the South with heat, vitality, and the "outward" flow of life</note> rays, gushing or shining forth from the wound, will—by means of the Northern <note>original: "Boreali"; associated with the cold, "inward" attraction of the magnetic pole</note> ointment, or rather by the attraction of the Spirits enclosed there—desire to animate and unite themselves in a Magnetic manner with the Northern and congealed (or fixed) Blood Spirits held in the ointment, and incite them to act "Southerly" or Equinoctially—that is, from the center to the circumference. Thus, through a reciprocal action, <column-break/> union, or continuity of this kind, the lively Southern rays will act upon the sleepy, cold, and fixed Northern rays and revive them. These will animate the ointment with Magnetic power, and return the animated Spirits of the ointment to both sets of Spirits as agile agents. These [Spirits], by that same union or continuity, impart their Balsamic healing power to the Spirits in the wound (which were previously magnetically attracted) and to those Spirits which were first transplanted into the ointment. And these then afterward, by a certain inseparable harmony, transmit that power all the way to the wound.

This, therefore, is the reason for that sympathetic and antipathetic relation observed by experience to exist between the ointment and the wound. So much so, that if the whole extent of the weapon that made the wound is anointed, covered, and defended from the cold, the person will find comfort, and his pain will be mitigated. But, if a part of the ointment is scraped off with a knife or anything else, or wiped away from the sword, axe, or other wounding weapon, pain and disorder will be felt immediately in the wound. Likewise, if the anointed part of the weapon is kept moderately warm, the wound will behave the same way; but if it is uncovered and held in cold air, then indeed the wound will be troubled and even affected by the cold.

### The first member or portion of the preceding proposition, with

<margin>First Member.</margin>
In the first place, therefore, we gather from the preceding proposition that two magnetic bodies of a similar nature can concur <column-break/> and be united to each other spiritually <note>In 17th-century science, "spiritually" refers to the movement of "spirits"—invisible, subtle substances or vapors—rather than religious spirits.</note>, by means of replacement and the natural inciting of a similar nature, and that for this reason a wounding weapon, or another penetrating material, is accustomed to imbibe the bloody spirits and become magnetic.

### A demonstration taken from the Magnet.

Have a stone with distinct poles, that is, marked both South and North; place it in its wooden vessel so that it floats, and let the poles be correctly positioned toward the plane of the horizon, or at least not much elevated or oblique. Hold another <margin>Gilbert, book 1, chapter 5, on the Magnet <note>Refers to William Gilbert's "De Magnete" (1600), the first scientific study of magnetism.</note>.</margin> Magnet in your hand, whose poles are also known; so that its Southern pole is toward the Northern pole of the one floating near it from the side. ### The fifth part of the aforementioned proposition with its proofs.

Fifthly, that we shall perceive the Magnetic act—or the operation of the celestial Spirits or "astralitions" <note>original: "astralitionum." Fludd uses this term to describe the subtle, light-like influences or radiations coming from the stars.</note> flowing downward—is not to be determined by the human mind, nor to be hindered in any of its motions, if only we wish to look into the depth of this business with the intellectual eye.

For a better anatomy and expression of this part, we have found it necessary, for the surer instruction of the reader, to distinguish it into two branches or separate particles. ### THE CONCLUSION.

It is therefore manifest that the spiritual or formal <note>In Renaissance philosophy, "formal" refers to the "form" or soul of an object that gives it its essential properties.</note> extension of the Magnet’s emanation, and even that of all other magnetic bodies, is not to be enclosed within certain limits. Insofar as it acts and applies its rays even to the seat and station of the polar star, the polar star similarly works in a reciprocal manner by sending out its influences. It applies itself to, or gazes upon, the Magnet; and thus between those ascending rays and those descending rays, a continuous spiritual union is made. We discern this with our eyes, because both the Magnet and the iron, with great diligence and manifest sympathy, gaze upon and are moved toward that star. Therefore, these things being duly weighed, I would have one consider how great that interval or space is which lies between the earth and the eighth sphere <note>In the Ptolemaic system, the eighth sphere is the firmament of the fixed stars.</note>. Without a doubt, he will perceive it to be almost infinite, or rather immeasurable. Consequently, the irradiations made by a magnetic body do not know how to terminate at some fantastical and sensible limit of activity (according to the imaginary opinion of certain fantastical philosophers). 

But if such an act at such a great distance—either of the Polar star or the Magnet—is denied by some, and if the opinion of Fracastoro <note>Girolamo Fracastoro (1478–1553) was a physician and poet who suggested magnets were attracted to specific magnetic mountains in the north.</note>, along with that of many other doctors, is received and held as authentic—which says that the Magnet, the iron, and the needle touched by a Magnet tend toward the North by reason of the attraction of various rocks consisting of Magnet-stone situated in the far northern mountains—if (I say) that opinion is held as true, we can still elicit from it that the very act of the Magnet and the actual regard which magnetic bodies have for it cannot be terminated by any certain limits. Even in that consideration, the irradiations of such bodies will be observed to cooperate from the location of the Equator all the way to the far northern rocks. But we have proved their opinion to be false and vain elsewhere. Now, however, we shall apply all that has been said to our present purpose—namely, the first article of this member.

## Several problematic demonstrations to confirm this part of the argument.
---

### 1. *The Problem previously recited.*

If a Magnet of no power or strength—which can be easily discerned—is placed upon the pole of a stronger Magnet, it will display vigor, as if it were just as strong as the one to which it is united. But after it has been removed, it will be just as weak as it was before, unless this process is repeated more frequently.

### APPLICATION.

The Southern Blood <note>original: "Sanguis Australis" — In Fludd's system, the "Southern" or "Austral" spirit is often associated with the life-giving, warming breath of nature that animates matter.</note> penetrating through the oily Magnet <note>Fludd refers to the "weapon salve" or ointment as an "oily magnet" because it is designed to attract and hold the vital spirit of the blood.</note>, animates it, and by animating it, gives it life. It preserves the transplanted Spirit from the harshness of the external air and warms that Spirit which has been attracted through its own Southern nature. It thus transports and vivifies the dead Spirits of the languishing blood, just as we see the Spirit in a dead grain of wheat, when buried in the earth, animated anew as if from death to life by the earth being vivified with Solar rays. But if a portion of the ointment is removed from the site of the weapon or arms to which the blood adheres, or where the Blood-Spirits were penetrating, the revived Spirits will languish once more, and the wound will become painful, just as it was before it was "buried" in the ointment. Similarly, if the earth is removed from the vigorous Spirits in a dead grain, they will languish, and the plant will neither grow nor multiply. However, if the ointment is reapplied and animated as before, the wound will prosper and heal without pain, just as if the earth that was removed from the revived Spirit in the grain were immediately reapplied to it; that Spirit will grow again.

---

<margin>Ridley, chapter 16.</margin> <note>Referring to Mark Ridley's *A Short Treatise of Magneticall Bodies and Motions* (1613).</note>

### 2. *PROBLEM.*

If a weak Magnet is rubbed at one of its poles with a stronger Magnet, it will thereafter be improved in virtue and vigor, provided it is not increased in size thereby.

### Demonstration: To confirm this.

It is experienced daily by those who brew beer: if beer that is completely dead and of no vigor is added to new and recently fermenting beer, it will be turned into excellent beer of the highest strength.

### APPLICATION.

This typical proof also exactly confirms the same part of the argument: namely, that living Spirits will invigorate those that are languid.

---

<margin>Gilbert, *On the Magnet*, book 2.</margin> <note>William Gilbert (1544–1603), whose 1600 work *De Magnete* founded the modern study of magnetism.</note>

### 3. *PROBLEM.*

A Magnet will lose some of its attractive virtue and will languish, as if by old age, if it is exposed to the open air for a long time and is not replaced or hidden within iron filings <note>original: "liniatura ferri" — refers to iron scales or filings used to "feed" or maintain a magnet's strength.</note>.

### APPLICATION.

So also human blood, poured out from its "mine" <note>The body is seen as the "mine" or source of the blood's mineral-like vitality.</note> and exposed to the open air, languishes and is rendered weak, unless it is preserved in the weapon ointment, which is of its own nature.

## Several problematic demonstrations to confirm this part of the argument.

### 1. PROBLEM.

In the calendar or experimental glass <note>original: "vitro calendario" — Fludd is referring to a thermoscope, an early thermometer that shows the expansion and contraction of air due to temperature changes</note>, of which mention has been made so often, you will find between its head (or upper flask) and the water below a certain continuous air in the neck of the glass. You must imagine that this enclosed air is not without its sulfurous spirits <note>Fludd uses "sulfurous" in the alchemical sense, referring to the active, flammable, or "soul" principle of a substance</note>, which by their expansion also expand the aerial vehicle in which they reside; and with the vehicle expanded, the water is pushed down. Yet we see that the air, which is between both extremes, is one air continued from one extreme to the other. Therefore, much more so is the occult and celestial Sulfurous spirit, which dwells and acts in it, and is like a soul in a body—present in the whole and in every part. <column-break/>

in number, is derived from the soul of the world, it works as a universal spirit in the greater world [Macrocosm], namely from the North or from the South. In like manner also, this part of that universal spirit works in its enclosed air. For, if the Universal <note>original: "Catholicus" — here meaning "universal" or "all-encompassing," not referring to the religious denomination</note> spirit of the world acts or breathes from the North and produces in the air freezing and contracting effects, then indeed the central spirit in the glass works similarly, according to the same mode: for it contracts its vehicle and draws up the waters. But, if the Universal spirit of the world breathes from the South, then the air previously contracted is now expanded again, and then also the formal enclosed spirits in the glass will work according to the same manner, and will dissipate and extend their aerial vehicle in a larger proportion or mode, as can be discerned by visual demonstration in the said instrument.

### 2. PROBLEM.

The North wind <note>original: "Boreas"</note> blowing in the Macrocosm continues the essence of its blast from the North to the South: but, the more it approaches the equinoctial line <note>The Equator</note>, the weaker is its effect in contraction and freezing. In this it agrees with the Magnet, whose parts, the closer they are to the pole, exist as more powerful in their operative or attractive faculty; and the farther away they are, the feebler and weaker they are. But this spirit emanating from the North to the equinoctial is one and the same spirit in essence, although it varies in its property in its different parts. <column-break/>

And again, the Northern property of that same spirit, being most powerful during the winter time, flees by attraction and magnetically directs these spirits which were driven from the South; and the more favorably it attracts them to the poles, the more quickly it condenses them into clouds, which—on account of the Sulphurous nature <note>In Fludd’s chemistry, "sulfur" represents the principle of heat and combustibility</note> they bring from the summer or the equinox—are immediately resolved into rains. This is the reason why Southern winds are so frequent among us in winter time, and consequently why rains are abundant at that time. Thus, it can be seen how the doubled property of one and the same spirit works at one and the same time toward the effect of one and the same thing in the single, universal air of the world, as I said before in my *Mosaic Philosophy*. **T**here is a certain noble Earl, of no small renown among us English, and he is a prudent man, religious, and of the best reputation, who commonly used to cure jaundice <note>original: "icterum"</note> at a distance, sometimes (as he told me) of 100 miles, and that only by means of the patient's urine brought to him. And the method is this: he mixes the ashes of the ash tree with the patient's urine, and from there reduces it into a paste, and then into little balls, 3, 7, or 9 in number. In the top of each of the said rounds, having made a hole, he places a filament of Saffron <note>original: "Croci"</note>, and then fills it up with the remainder of the urine. Then afterwards, he places or disposes these balls in some secret place where no one sees them: and immediately the jaundice in the patient—whether he be far away or near to the physician—will decrease. This experiment has been proven in several hundred people, both poor and rich, and many of them were such that the physicians had despaired of them. Not only he himself, but also the most noble ladies, his daughters, who freely for God’s sake have done good to many poor people, affirm this to be true. And I myself can affirm this much: that I was called to the wife of a Surgeon in the year 1632, after other

<column-break/>

doctors had abandoned her, who was most foully infected with the said "arched disease" <note>original: "morbo arquato," another term for jaundice, referring to the rainbow-like yellowing of the skin</note>, even after using medicines, but in vain. At her request, I sent her servant into the country with letters to the said noble lady to implore her help. But in the time while the urine was being sent, the said woman was persuaded by certain foolish old women that this was done by cunning and Magic. This so greatly disturbed her that she even treated her servant harshly upon his return. Hence, I dispatched a messenger immediately, asking that her Ladyship destroy what she had caused to be done because of the ingratitude of the said woman. She sent word back to me that she was willing to do so, but replied at the same time that it would be in vain; for she would restore her to health now, let me do what I would: and indeed she recovered immediately. Similarly, there was a certain daughter of a noble Baroness, and the wife of a most noble Knight, William Brooke <note>Sir William Brooke (1601–1643), a prominent English politician and soldier</note>, who was foully defiled by the said disease. And therefore, this applies much more to the serous matter <note>original: "materiâ ferosa," likely referring to the watery part of the blood or bodily fluids</note> which has been separated from the blood. Thus, just as the power of a plant with saffron <note>original: "croco"</note> removes and neutralizes the infection in the urine, so also by the mutual consensus that exists between the two extremes of the infection—namely, the blood and the urine—the infection in the blood is observed to gradually fail, languish, and perish. But I will present to you a Magnetic Problem to confirm the possibility of this proposition.

### 2. THE PROBLEM.

Two Magnets properly joined at opposite poles will, upon the arrival of a stronger Magnet or magnetized iron, cause a "miscarriage" <note>original: "abortum," here meaning a sudden separation or failure of the connection</note>; the newly arrived magnet will easily drive away the other, which is facing it, and will command it; and thus the coherence or union of the other two will cease and end.

Being unnatural, it is forced to flee and depart from the natural spirit by the help of another, which is more powerful than the unnatural one. ## DEMONSTRATION.

There is no reason to waste time in further demonstration of the possibility of these operations regarding the Spiritually transplanted Mummy, since by the same proofs with which I confirmed the method of curing through the weapon salve <term>weapon salve: Also known as the *unguentum armarium*, a powder or salve believed to heal a wound by being applied to the weapon that caused it.</term> and transplantation—which is fully and clearly described in the aforementioned chapter of this book—the reason for these occult and secret actions in this kind of healing is explained to those who, like Thomas <note>A reference to "Doubting Thomas" from the Gospel of John, who refused to believe in the Resurrection until he saw and touched the wounds.</note>, refuse to believe anything unless it is confirmed by the senses. In a word, I say: namely, that by means of it, pleurisy, Dropsy <term>Dropsy: An old term for edema, or the swelling of soft tissues due to the accumulation of excess water.</term>, Consumption <note>original: "Phthisis," typically referring to pulmonary tuberculosis.</note>, vertigo, Epilepsy, the French disease <note>original: "morbus Gallicus," a common historical term for syphilis.</note>, Paralysis, Cancer, fistula, putrid ulcers, tumors, wounds, hernias, fractures, superfluities, suppressions of the menses in women, as well as sterility in them, hectic fever, Atrophy or the wasting of members, and similar things can be cured by these natural Magical means, and that from a distance and without any immediate contact. And Paracelsus affirms that this Magnetic mode of curing, which is performed by natural magic, excels in power and operation all other medicinal secrets that can be extracted from herbs, roots, or minerals. Finally, since I have made further mention of these mysteries regarding Magnetic Medicines in that book—my Treatise on Medicine described by the oracle of Apollo—I refer you who are judicious, learned, and prudent to that work.

Now indeed I shall proceed to the second part or member of this book, which treats of the Antipathetic effects of this Mummial experiment.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*A brief Apology for the use of mystical or Spiritual Mummy, and to prove that both the Antipathetic abuse of the same, as well as its Sympathetic use, and the use of all other natural things, ought to be known and understood by the natural Mage, or wise physician, for the sake of prevention: Although not put into action, except where necessity requires.*<-

Truly, I am not unaware that there will be many barking Cynics, railing Critics, and satirical Momuses <note>Momus was the Greek god of mockery and unfair criticism.</note> whose sole pleasure is usually fostered by the fire of indignation or malice; who, suffocated as if by the smoke of blind and sluggish ignorance, will say: That if the Sympathetic effects of the **Spiritual Mummy** <note>original: "Mummiae Spiritualis"; in this context, it refers to the vital life-force or "balsam" within a living body, rather than an Egyptian corpse.</note> are permitted and granted to the physician, nevertheless its Antipathetic <note>original: "Antipatheticae"; properties that cause repulsion, disease, or harm.</note> properties are hateful and by no means to be tolerated; indeed, they are **Cacomagical** <note>original: "Cacomagicae"; relating to "black magic" or evil sorcery.</note>, because the Devil instructs his ministers concerning the abuses or evil use of this Microcosmic species of corruption; and therefore, for this reason, even the knowledge of such a thing ought not to be tolerated, etc. These objections (I know) will be raised by a kind of chatterer devoid of sense and reason regarding the knowledge of so mystical a business. 

But if their words find a place among the wise, what, I pray, will become of the art of Solomon in **natural Magic** <note>The study of the hidden powers of plants, stones, and animals, considered a legitimate science in the Renaissance.</note>, or why would he (who was thought the wisest of men) be so far deceived as to aspire to the knowledge of all things, and understand the enemies of human nature as well as its friends? <margin>Wisdom 7.</margin> For it is said of him, that he knew the natures of living creatures, the ferocity of beasts, the thoughts of men, the different virtues of the plants' roots, and of all other things which were hidden and secret. Indeed, why would he say that Wisdom, the artisan of all things, had taught him? Are there not plants, animals, and minerals which are as potent poisons to human nature as they are benign and salutary? He knew (says the Text) the nature of all living creatures or animals: and why, if that were true which these railers blather? Why would he know and contemplate the properties of those things which are poisons and harmful to the human race? Is it not the Asp, the viper, the adder, and that putrefying and corrupting worm which is called the **Seps** <note>A legendary serpent or insect whose bite was said to cause the body to dissolve or rot instantly.</note>, or in French the *Pourrisseur* <note>meaning "The Rotter."</note>, by reason of its putrefying venom; the serpent called the **Dypsas**, which affects the spirit with unmeasurable thirst; the **Amphisbaena** <note>A mythical serpent with a head at each end.</note>, the Basilisk, the Dragon and the **Hoilio** <note>likely referring to a "stellio" or spotted lizard, often associated with venom.</note>, the Salamander, the Cantharides <note>The "Spanish Fly," known for its toxic and irritant properties.</note>, and an infinite number of other animals, both of the earth and the water: are these not (I say) venomous and in a wonderful

To which I reply: All these, although they are poisonous in themselves, yet when treated and prepared in the proper way by the wise, they become medicinal; and I would have them know that God created all things good: But it is the Devil and his instruments who, through their evil use or application, render those things hateful and detestable to human nature. For, just as by their genuine and legitimate use and application they can produce Sympathetic effects: so indeed by their abuse they bring forth nothing but Antipathetic actions and rebellious conflict in human nature. God (I say) ordained them for good uses, namely for human health, but the Devil applies them in a destructive and malicious manner. From which it is clear that it was the Devil and wicked men who are the instruments of death and extermination; and truly they are incarnate Devils who adapt to an evil use that which is in truth good and legitimate.

### 3. PROPOSITION.

If two small pieces of flesh, recently wounded, are applied to one another, they will sympathize and unite, becoming assimilated, and will be restored as one continuous piece of flesh: so that, as one of them prospers, so also will the other; provided that he, from whom that added flesh was borrowed, remains healthy, alive, and in his vital <term>disposition<note>A state of health or bodily temperament; the specific balance of "humors" or spirits in a living thing.</note></term>. But if indeed the animal tree from which the graft was taken (I mean the body from which the flesh was borrowed or cut out) should wither or perish—that is, <column-break/> should cease to act and grow—then indeed this borrowed flesh will break faith with the flesh of the lender, who [no longer] lives and grows; and consequently, Antipathy will proceed from that union which was previously Sympathetic; so that the dying flesh must now be amputated, or cut away from the living flesh upon which it was transplanted and fixed, lest it cause the living flesh also to become gangrenous and corrupted along with it.

#### *An experiment to confirm this.*

This has been duly proven and established by that experiment previously cited in Italy. For when a certain nobleman had lost his nose in a wound, and a wound having been made in the arm of one of his slaves, by the advice of physicians he fitted that [arm] to his own similarly wounded nose, and thus the flesh of the one was firmly attached to the flesh of the other, continuing in that manner until, by sympathetic agglutination and union, both pieces of flesh grew together into one; and then a portion of the slave's flesh was cut away from the arm and formed into the shape of a nose on that Nobleman, and the slave was thus [dismissed] from his hand <column-break/> [and] sent away with enough money for the pains he had suffered. However, it happened some time later that the slave died, and although he departed this life far distant from his master, nevertheless the borrowed flesh in the master's nose began to wither and turn gangrenous, to such an extent that the Antipathy between both pieces of flesh—even though they were united into one substance—increased so much that, unless that dead flesh had been immediately cut away, it would have corrupted and destroyed the remaining healthy parts.

### 5. PROPOSITION.

The Spiritual **Mummy** <note>In this context, "Mummy" (Mummia) refers to the invisible, balsamic life-force or "vapor of life" that resides in all living things.</note> of a <term>Sympathetic<note>Sympathy: The natural resonance or attraction between two things of a similar nature.</note></term> nature, when turned toward an <term>Antipathetic<note>Antipathy: The natural force of repulsion or corruption between things of a differing or hostile nature.</note></term> one, is able to infect not only the surrounding air but even a denser medium—namely, liquids.

### *A demonstration confirming this.*

There is a story of this kind that can confirm this, regarding **The de Bruer**: In the city of Canterbury in the County of Kent, there was a certain man of great renown in the crafting of ale, who held no small reputation for his skill. It happened many times, for a reason quite unknown, that the ale he made suddenly be-

<column-break/>

came very bad, "dead," and of almost no value. He complained to many of his friends about this matter, nor could he investigate the reason why he, who had at other times crafted ale praised by everyone, had now erred so evidently and on various occasions? One day he was informed by an old woman <note>original: "vetula." While this can mean a wise woman or midwife, Fludd likely refers to a practitioner of folk-remedies.</note> that this could happen through the foul breath of one of the servants engaged in the crafting and boiling of the ale, and that this occurred from her own experience. Therefore, having examined the servants working in the crafting of the Ale, he found one above the rest affected by a very foul breath and a contagious spirit; having paid his wages, he ordered him to leave. He began to make new ale again, and without any obstacle, he created good ale, and he consistently had such good success while that corrupt breath was absent. After the space of a year, for the sake of experimenting, he took back that servant affected by the corrupt breath and employed him in the business of his craft as before. Once this was done, he perceived his ale returned to its former [spoiled] state. Being thus made more certain and sure of this matter, he again dismissed that servant whose spirit was so deadly to his ale. This is known by many trustworthy people.

### APPLICATION.

If, therefore, that Spirit is so deadly to a foreign spirit <note>i.e., the "spirit" or life-force of the fermenting ale.</note> that it can corrupt it at a distance, it was without a doubt much more Antipathetic to the Spirit of its own nature and species, as may be seen in the human spirit infected by the plague; for it has been observed that the final breath of a man dying of the plague is exceedingly contagious to those present, being ruinous and so lethal that nothing could be more so.

### CONCLUSION.

I could indeed (judicious reader) gather an entire volume of experimental propositions, together with their proofs, concerning the abyss and infinite forest of Sympathetic and Antipathetic effects in the three kingdoms—namely, the animal, vegetable, and mineral—both mutually between any species, and between individuals from one genus to another. But I did not set out to express my bolder and more constant opinions regarding true Philosophy and its appendages in a more flowery phrase, considering the harshness and hastiness of my pen by reason of my defect and insufficiency in its polished nature. In turn, I am not ignorant that refined and decorated words and phrases are nothing but the fleeting bubbles and mere shadows of a powerful and wealthy subject, which, as they are <term>Protean<note>Ever-changing in form, like the Greek sea-god Proteus.</note></term> and changeable into infinite colors, so also the fancies and judgments of men are greatly variable; according to the proverb: *As many men, so many opinions.* <note>original: "Quot homines, tot sententiæ."</note> I truly believe, and my mind foretells, that however curious or exact I am in my writing, or in my phrasing—

# SECTION TWO. BOOK III. Part II.

Though the labor of my expression is difficult, yet my better efforts will appear without fault or crime in the eyes of the curious, although perhaps they may be sufficiently pleasing to others. Wherefore I think it enough that I dare to be confident in the fundamental subject of this essential Philosophy, since it has truth itself for its defense and vindication, without any adornment of superficial words. Furthermore, just as truth does not seek corners <note>original: "veritas non quærit angulos." A common Latin proverb suggesting that truth is open and does not need to hide in shadows or use deception.</note>, so it also has no need for the expression of eloquent words, polished sentences, or phrases to illustrate it or make it clearer in the eyes of the wise and learned; since it can be hidden from no one that truth conquers all things:

<margin>Wisdom 7.</margin>
For it is a lucid splendor or emanation, arisen from the omnipotent and eternal fountain, which illuminates all things and reveals itself in effect to everyone. Therefore, it is so manifest in all its works that it does not need any golden-tongued orator, or smooth methodical rhetorician, or eloquent philosopher to reveal its excellence or to relate the perfection of its joys to the whole world—even though unworthy worldlings may be unwilling to acknowledge or receive it with proper reverence, as is fitting.

<column-break/>

Instead, they perpetually hide it with all their efforts under the veil of dark ignorance, and thus they do not cease daily to persecute and crucify the **spiritual Christ**, who is the only truth, true wisdom, the true Corner-stone, and the essential subject of true and legitimate Philosophy. Blessed be his name forever! He alone sustains and preserves heaven and earth and all things; he works all things in all people and reigns in glory and power with the Father eternally. He shall deign to defend his servants from the evil-hearted and, like a shield and place of refuge, protect the herald of his truth from the viperous tongues of wicked tricksters, the evasions of railers, and the poisonous jests of cynical and satirical **Momus** <note>Momus was the Greek god of mockery and unfair criticism; Fludd frequently invokes this figure to describe his intellectual critics.</note>. It is he who gave these words to the cultivator of his truth:

<margin>Luke 21:15</margin>
> I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict.

Therefore, I will conclude with the Prophet David:

<margin>Psalm 63:8</margin>
> In the shadow of your wings I will sing: Lord, in you I trust. Vindicate and preserve me from my enemies according to your mercy. Amen.

---

->THE END.<-

<meta>This page serves as the title page for Robert Fludd's polemical response to William Foster. It marks a transition from Fludd's theoretical works on philosophy and magnetism to a direct, spirited defense of the "Weapon-salve"—a controversial medical treatment of the time. This document follows Fludd’s earlier discussions on the "spiritual mummy" and natural sympathies, now applying those theories to a specific theological and medical debate.</meta>

# A RESPONSE
## TO THE
# HOPLOCRISMA-SPONGE
### OF MR. FOSTER, PRIEST, PREPARED BY
### HIM FOR THE DESTRUCTION OF THE 
### VALIDITY OF THE 
### WEAPON-SALVE.
<note>The "Weapon-salve" (Unguentum Armarium) was a controversial "sympathetic" medicine. Instead of being applied to a wound, the ointment was applied to the weapon that caused the injury. Supporters like Fludd believed natural magnetism cured the patient at a distance.</note>

->that is,<-

# THE SQUEEZING OUT
## OR THE CRUSHING
## OF THE SPONGE OF MR. FOSTER, PRIEST.
<note>William Foster had published a book titled *Hoplocrisma-Spongus* (A Sponge to Wipe Away the Weapon-Salve) in 1631, arguing that the cure was magical or diabolical. Fludd’s title plays on this by "squeezing" Foster’s metaphorical sponge until it is destroyed.</note>

->In which<-

The supposed power of his sponge in wiping away the Weapon-salve is squeezed out, crushed, and utterly abolished; and finally, his immodesty and incivility toward his Brothers is corrected and completely extinguished by the sharpest vinegar of truth.

> *The sharpest bile, corrected by the sharpest vinegar, is rendered sweeter.* <note>A proverbial expression suggesting that harsh criticism (bile) can only be improved or neutralized by an even sharper application of truth (vinegar).</note>

> A brutish and foolish man does not understand the works of God.
Psalm 92:6. <note>original: "Psalm 92:7." Fludd uses the Vulgate numbering; in modern English Bibles, this is verse 6.</note>

### BY THE AUTHOR,
### ROBERT FLUDD, also known as "of the Floods,"
<note>original: "de Fluctibus." It was common for scholars to Latinize their surnames; "Fluctibus" is the Latin word for floods/waves.</note>
### Esquire and Doctor of Medicine of Oxford.

<image-desc>An oval engraved emblem featuring a nude female figure seated on a stone block, representing Truth. She holds an open book in her left hand and a radiant sun in her right hand. The central figure is enclosed within a thick, ornate wreath consisting of various flowers, fruits, and leaves. Two small floral decorative vignettes flank the emblem on the left and right sides.</image-desc>

->GOUDA,<-

--- Page 356 ---
<meta>This page serves as the concluding section of Robert Fludd's defense against the priest William Foster. Having spent the preceding pages arguing for the natural and "magnetic" reality of the Weapon-salve, Fludd here transitions into a humble yet defiant spiritual conclusion, placing his work under the protection of divine truth rather than human eloquence.</meta>

### OF THE SECOND SECTION. BOOK III. Member II.

Although my efforts in expressing myself are laborious, my better attempts will appear without fault or crime in the eyes of the curious <note>In the 17th century, "curious" referred to those who were carefully observant or seekers of hidden knowledge.</note>, and perhaps will be quite pleasing to others. For this reason, I think it enough that I dare to be confident in the fundamental subject of this essential Philosophy; for it has the truth itself to defend and vindicate it, without any adornment of superficial words. Therefore, just as truth does not seek out corners <note>original: "veritas non quærit angulos". A common Latin proverb meaning that the truth is open and does not need to hide in shadows or use deception.</note>, it also has no need for the expression of eloquent words, polished sentences, or sophisticated phrases to illustrate itself or make it clearer in the eyes of the wise and learned. Since it can be hidden from no one, it overcomes all things:
<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 7.</margin>
For it is a lucid splendor or emanation, arisen from the Almighty and the eternal fountain, which illuminates all things and reveals itself through its effects to everyone. Therefore, it is so manifest in all its works that it does not need any golden-tongued orator, or smooth methodical rhetorician, or eloquent philosopher to reveal its excellence or report the perfection of its delights to the whole world—even if the unworthy people of the world refuse to recognize

<column-break/>

or receive it with the reverence it deserves. Rather, they perpetually hide it with all their efforts behind a dark veil of ignorance, and thus they do not cease daily to persecute and crucify the spiritual Christ, who is the only truth, true wisdom, the true cornerstone, and the essential subject of true and legitimate philosophy. Blessed be his name forever; he alone sustains and preserves heaven and earth and all things; he works all in all and reigns in glory and power with the Father for eternity. He will defend his servants from the evil-hearted and, like a shield and a defensive asylum, he will fortify the herald of his truth to preserve him from the viperous tongues of malicious veterans, the backsliding of railers, and the poisonous taunts of the wicked. It is he who handed down to the worshiper of his truth:
<margin>Luke 21:15</margin>
"I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict." Therefore, I shall conclude with the
<margin>Psalm 63:8</margin>
Prophet David: "In the shadow of your wings I will sing: Lord, in you I trust; vindicate and preserve me from my enemies according to your mercy. Amen."

---

->**THE END.**<-
